- list 2 of 4What are the challenges facing the Mecca agreement?
- list 3 of 4Will Pakistan-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact change US strategy?
- list 4 of 4Iran changed the rules in Hormuz. The Gulf is changing the rules for Iran
The attacks came a day after Houthi missiles killed at least seven people and wounded 30 others in al-Makha, which is also known as Mocha. The strikes caused extensive damage at the city’s port area.
Elsewhere in Yemen on Monday, a Houthi drone strike killed two Yemeni government soldiers and wounded seven others in the south-central province of Shabwa, according to local media reports.
Yemeni forces, in a series of posts on X, said they targeted Houthi rebels and their sites in eastern al-Jawf province, northwestern Saada province and the al-Tibas area of central Marib province.
The tit-for-tat attacks are the deadliest in years in Yemen’s civil war and mark a major escalation in the conflict, which has been reignited by the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran on February 28.
The Iran-backed Houthis captured Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, in September 2014, with a Saudi-led coalition intervening in March 2015 on the side of the government.
The conflict, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people, deteriorated into a deadlock, and the warring parties reached a truce in April 2022 that ended major fighting across the country.
But the violence reignited on July 13 with a Saudi air strike on the runway of Sanaa airport, preventing the landing of an Iranian flight carrying a high-ranking Houthi delegation.
Following the strike, the Houthis attacked the Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia and announced a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea. They have also attacked Saudi vessels as well as oil facilities in the kingdom, adding further disruption to the global economy.
The Saudi-led coalition in turn has struck Houthi-controlled Hodeidah and Kamaran, Yemen’s largest island in the Red Sea. It has also reinforced Yemeni troops along the front lines in Yemen to launch a ground offensive on Houthis.
Meanwhile, the United Nations has called for restraint.
“Yemen today faces a greater risk of renewed large-scale conflict than at any point since the UN-brokered truce of April 2022,” UN envoy Hans Grundberg warned on Friday.
The escalation, he said, risks “jeopardising the gains of the 2022 truce … while also drawing the country into a broader regional confrontation, with devastating consequences for its people”.

title: Turkey's parliament approves a pardon-like bill for thousands of PKK militants
summary: Turkey's parliament approved legislation that would introduce a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants in a bid to advance the government's peace initiative with their insurgent group.
full_text:
Turkey's parliament approves a pardon-like bill for thousands of PKK militants
ANKARA, Turkey — Turkey's parliament on Monday approved legislation that would introduce a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants in a bid to advance the government's peace initiative with their insurgent group.
Legislators voted 468-88 in favor of the measure that would only come into effect after Turkish authorities have verified that the Kurdistan Workers' Party, or PKK, has fully disarmed.
The PKK announced last year that it is ending its decades-long armed campaign against the Turkish state, declaring a decision to dissolve itself as part of the peace effort. The move came in response to a call from its imprisoned leader, Abdullah Ocalan.
The group then staged a symbolic disarmament ceremony in northern Iraq, where it is based, and announced that it was withdrawing fighters from key locations in Turkey to Iraq.
Law could have regional implications
The measure, which is a step toward ending a conflict that has killed tens of thousands of people, could have implications beyond Turkey's borders, leading to closer Turkish-Iraqi ties. It could also support the Syrian government's efforts to integrate areas that were under the control of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, affiliated with the PKK.
It also offers Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan the opportunity to court the support of the pro-Kurdish DEM party to help him remain in office beyond the presidential two-term limit. Erdogan could run again if parliament calls an early election during his current term.
The 12-article legislation outlines the procedures for the group's disarmament and the rehabilitation of thousands of PKK members.
It will suspend some prison sentences for convicted PKK members and postpone ongoing investigations and trials against others for five or 10 years, depending on the severity of the alleged offenses. If no terror-related crime is committed within the time frame, the cases will be dropped.
Militants convicted of intentional killings and those sentenced to life terms before 2005 are excluded from the bill's provisions. This applies to Ocalan and other senior PKK figures.
The proposal also sets up ministerial and parliamentary committees to monitor the disarmament process. The measures will come into effect only after Turkey's National Security Council confirms that the group has disbanded and surrendered all weapons.
Those wanting to benefit from the law will have six months to apply after the National Security Council's decision is published in the official gazette.
Media reports have said exiled PKK members and those in Iraq and Syria are expected to benefit.
"With the armed organization laying down its arms and dissolving itself, we will build a new era in which peace, brotherhood, and solidarity will prevail," Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmus told reporters following the vote.
PKK says the legislation is a start but many things are missing
The PKK-linked ANF news outlet carried a statement from the group in which it said that the Turkish legislation is a "beginning" to resolving the outstanding issues but has "serious shortcomings and deficiencies." It called for Ocalan's release from prison, saying that the peace process can move forward only if he "lives and works freely."
It also said that the legislation failed to address demands for democratic reforms and Kurdish rights, adding that PKK fighters would not give up their weapons and return to Turkey "if, upon returning to Turkey, they are unable to engage in democratic politics on the basis of freedom of thought and freedom of association, and if they are prosecuted and imprisoned because of their views or the organizations they establish."
"The people of Turkey, who have paid a heavy price for many years, now have an opportunity to consolidate peace and build democracy," Gulistan Kilic Kocyigit, of the pro-Kurdish Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party, or DEM, told parliament.
"Of course, the proposal has shortcomings, and we now have a responsibility to address these shortcomings," she added, in an apparent reference to demands for greater rights for Kurds and for democratic reforms.
Musavat Dervisoglu, the leader of the center-right nationalist Good Party, which opposes the bill, said it "would pave the way" for Erdogan to stay in power.
Ocalan's release is not in the cards, but conditions might improve
DEM has lobbied for Ocalan, who has been imprisoned since 1999, to be granted official status to coordinate the transition process, leading to his release.
The current proposal, however, makes no mention of Ocalan's status or possible release.
Media reports have suggested, however, that Ocalan's conditions in his island prison off Istanbul will likely be improved, giving him broader visiting conditions and communication with the outside world.
The PKK has waged an armed insurgency since 1984 that has claimed tens of thousands of lives and spilled into Iraq and Syria. It has been designated a terrorist organization by Turkey, the United States and the European Union.
The group initially sought an independent Kurdish state but later shifted to demands for autonomy and expanded rights in Turkey.
Previous peace efforts between Turkey and the PKK have failed, most recently in 2015.

title: Trump pivots back to sanctions for Iran as other strategies to end his war fizzle
summary: The shift comes as U.S. stockpiles of key weapons have dwindled and as stop-start talks seem again to have stalled. But Trump insists the pressure can lead to a breakthrough.
full_text:
Trump pivots back to sanctions for Iran as other strategies to end his war fizzle
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump likes to say that he started his war with Iran after 50 years of economic pressure had failed to stop its nuclear weapons ambitions — but he's now betting that another financial squeeze can bring an end to that war.
The Trump administration is hoping that months of bombing have pushed Iran's economy to a breaking point that will force its leadership to cave to demands to end its nuclear program and fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz to oil and natural gas tankers.
The president on Monday said that since Iran is seeking compensation as part of any peace talks, he now intends to demand the same for the U.S. side. It's part of a larger pivot this weekend by Trump to argue that Iran is now on the cusp of financially collapsing, even though it has already endured decades of financial sanctions, which are often a longer-term strategy rather than an immediate tool of warfare that can halt a conflict.
The shift comes as U.S. stockpiles of key weapons have dwindled and as stop-start talks seem again to have stalled. But Trump insists the pressure can lead to a breakthrough.
"Yeah, they can make trouble, but they're broke," Trump told reporters. "They have no money. You know, Iran is broke, totally broke. And, they're not paying their soldiers. They have inflation of 300%."
Inflation is running high in Iran, although Trump's estimates were higher than what administration officials have been citing to reporters. But the prospect of a longer war also carries inflation risks for other nations, including the U.S. — where the war and higher gasoline prices are unpopular.
Crude oil prices climbed on Monday as investors interpreted Trump's comments as a sign that fewer ships would be traversing the Strait of Hormuz, continuing to limit global supplies of gasoline, jet fuel, natural gas and other forms of energy. The Iran war largely closed the waterway involved in shipping roughly 20% of global oil supplies before the conflict — and attempts to reopen the strait have been short-lived as it has become a source of leverage for the Iranians in negotiations.
Iran does not appear to be publicly intimidated by the prospect of more financial sanctions.
"Whenever Washington proves itself incapable of pursuing diplomacy, it retreats into sanctions; and whenever those sanctions fail to produce results, it simply increases the dose," said Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesman for Iran's Foreign Ministry, on social media. "The real risk is that American politicians, clinging to this bad habit, will instead strangle their own remaining chances of a less humiliating exit from a crisis of their own making."
The White House has called this 'Operation Economic Fury'
The president didn't say what additional financial pressure would be applied, but the administration has since April 16 been engaged in what it calls " Operation Economic Fury " against Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called this component the "financial equivalent" of a bombing campaign as the countries that buy oil from Iran or bank with it could be sanctioned.
But one problem with this pivot is that the sanctions are unable to bite as quickly as the impact of the largely shuttered strait, said Richard Nephew, a senior research scholar at Columbia University who helped direct Iran sanctions strategy in the Obama administration.
Nephew stressed that the value of sanctions as a tool is limited because Trump has not articulated clear strategic goals for the war, at times stressing that it can't have a nuclear weapon, then emphasizing the strait and then talking about ballistic missiles. Instead, Trump has engaged in a massive series of aerial assaults and a level of destruction that has not produced the quick end that he initially promised.
"Economic pressure is a possible element in his strategy, but he's yet to explain the purpose," Nephew said. "Trump has systematically weakened his own hand through his inadequate use of force, inarticulate elucidation of an objective, and vacillation on negotiations."
Still, the sanctions and the ongoing U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports give the U.S. economic and financial leverage, said Juan Zarate, a deputy national security adviser in the George W. Bush administration. Zarate said the U.S. sanctions threatening third-party countries doing business with Iran also have an impact. But these things take time, he noted.
"The ultimate question will be how far the United States is willing to go to constrict Iran's oil trade and threaten third countries with severe sanctions -- and whether it has the patience to test whether the economic pain will change the regime's behavior," Zarate said.
Past presidents used sanctions. Trump has said they didn't go far enough
Trump's latest pivot to economic issues with Iran is something of a flip-flop. Trump has long derided past presidents who used sanctions to limit Iran's economic ability to pay for its military and nuclear development. In a speech last week in Las Vegas, he defended the bombing, missiles and drone attacks that began on Feb. 28 by indicating that the sanctions from previous administrations that date back to November 1979 had failed to succeed.
"It's been 47 years, but really, it's been 50 years because they've been saying 47 for three years, it's been 50 years," Trump said. "And no other president has done what you should have done a long time ago, because Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, can't have it."
The Iranian economy has suffered gravely because of the war, with the International Monetary Fund estimating the overall economy shrinks by 5.4% and the Iranian government recently reporting an annual inflation rate of 88.6%. The U.S. Treasury Department said average loadings of Iranian oil have decreased from 1.8 million barrels per day before the war to less than 500,000 barrels per day over the past month.
The U.S. economy — the world's largest — has continued to grow, but inflation is elevated and borrowing costs have risen in ways that have hurt Trump's popularity and led to disapproval of the Iran war.
A senior U.S. official, insisting on anonymity to discuss strategy, said the U.S. military has set back Iran's ability to produce, sell and ship oil and other energy resources. The administration sees the naval blockade of the strait and sanctions as effective and views Trump as having additional options that can be cranked harder in the weeks and months ahead.
Trump is essentially arguing that U.S. voters are better able to tolerate any economic inconveniences than Iranians, who have been in a state of economic hardship for years.
"It's not just what the military can do — we've got the most powerful economy in the world as well," Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Monday in a joint appearance with Bessent. "And when you've got a motivated treasury secretary who can pull a lot of levers because he knows how to do it, you can put a lot of pressure on adversaries."

full_text:
Zhu Senlin, a former Guangdong governor widely regarded as a key enforcer of the province’s economic transformation in China’s critical period of opening up in the 1990s, died on Monday aged 95, according to official media.
Nanfang Daily, the mouthpiece of the Guangdong party committee, confirmed on Tuesday that Zhu had died due to illness.
Shanghai-born Zhu spent more than five decades in the southern province that neighbours Hong Kong.
He is widely remembered as a pragmatic, steady administrator who steered Guangdong through the most critical two decades of China’s reform and opening-up era – first as mayor and party chief of Guangzhou in the 1980s, and later as governor of Guangdong from May 1991 to February 1996. He took over as governor from Ye Xuanping, the eldest son of marshal Ye Jianying.
Zhu was also known for accompanying late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping on the Guangdong leg of his landmark Southern Tour in the spring of 1992, which covered Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Guangzhou and Shanghai.
Along with then Guangdong party chief Xie Fei, he flanked Deng during the party patriarch’s visit to the province. Zhu and Xie were widely regarded as part of the core team implementing Deng’s instructions to revive China’s commitment to reform amid isolation from the West and heavy resistance from political conservatives after the Tiananmen Square crackdown in 1989.
Designated as China’s first special economic zone in 1980, Shenzhen grew rapidly following Deng’s visit to serve as the bridgehead of Guangdong’s vibrant export sector, with Hong Kong channelling investments to mainland China and connecting it to the world.
In 1948, Zhu enrolled at Tsinghua University to study sociology in 1948. He joined the Communist Party in 1952 and was sent to Guangzhou – a city that would become his home and political theatre for decades – that same year.

US House panel slammed for asking if scholars lost jobs to Chinese hires
Congressional panel seeks complaints from US academics, but critics call its focus on Chinese applicants a “disgrace”
A Republican-led congressional committee focused on US competition with China has issued a public call for American academics to come forward if they think they missed out on jobs in favour of “applicants from China”.
“Are you an American student, postdoctoral researcher, or academic who believes you were denied a research position, laboratory opportunity, or postdoctoral appointment because preference was given to applicants from China?” the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party posted on X, formerly Twitter, on Monday.
The committee urged those with “first-hand” information or supporting documentation to contact it through its whistle-blower email.
The appeal drew fierce backlash, with critics warning that singling out Chinese applicants risked further fuelling anti-Chinese sentiment.
Kaiser Kuo, host of The Sinica Podcast, called the move a “disgrace”.
He wrote on social media: “Really? THIS is what they’re worried about? … At a time when racial profiling is driving talent away from American shores and harming US competitiveness, they want to stir up anti-Chinese grievance?”

title: Australia’s prime minister refuses to apologise to Japanese counterpart over melon gaffe
summary:
Anthony Albanese faces criticism after appearing to joke on a podcast about a gift of melons from Sanae Takaichi

full_text:
The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has rejected calls to apologise to Japan’s prime minister over a joke he made about melons on a satirical podcast, amid a media frenzy and accusations of sexual innuendo.
Government MPs have defended the prime minister as criticism mounted over last month’s remarks, branded by the Coalition opposition as “grubby”. The assistant minister Pat Gorman told media: “I don’t know why we’re still talking about this.”
During an interview on the comedy podcast Bush Deep in early July, Albanese spoke about Japan’s leader, Sanae Takaichi, giving him a gift of Japanese melons.
Discussing the present, he appeared to make hand gestures in front of his chest, saying “she brought two, as you do”. Host Nikki Osborne joked: “She came in looking like Pamela Anderson.”
Albanese had not previously addressed the comments, but in parliament’s question time on Tuesday, was asked by the opposition whether he would apologise. In her question, the Liberal MP Mary Aldred described Albanese’s comments as “foul-mouthed, classless” and “disrespectful behaviour”.
Albanese responded: “I reject the assertion in the question.”
He continued, “Australia and Japan have never been closer or more strategically aligned. And my government has taken our special strategic partnership to new heights,” noting recent economic, strategic and security collaborations between the countries.
During his answer, one Liberal MP interjected: “Why didn’t you say that in the podcast?”
Aldred later asked again whether Albanese would apologise, to which he again noted various meetings with Takaichi and the close relationship between Japan and Australia.
The melon comments have since been canvassed regularly by media outlets including The Australian, the West Australian and the Australian Financial Review. But it resurfaced as a political issue after The Australian ran a comment piece on Monday from the former Japanese ambassador Shingo Yamagami, who claimed Albanese had insulted Takaichi.
In an op-ed titled “sexist melon joke was not only ungracious, it betrayed the close bond of our two nations”, Yamagami – who left his post in 2023 and previously had a less-than-warm relationship with some in Labor – called out “crude jokes”.
The Australian reported on Tuesday that Japan’s government had sent a diplomatic cable to Australia in July, days after the podcast originally aired, claiming there had been “sensationalised reporting in the Australian media” and saying they detected no “ill intention” in Albanese’s statement.
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, on Monday demanded Albanese apologise, while his deputy, Jane Hume, claimed the melon comments were “grubby” and “beneath the office of the prime minister”.
Shiro Armstrong, the director of the Australia-Japan Research Centre at the Australian National University, told Radio National last week there had been “no mention of [Albanese’s comments] in Japan until weeks later”, calling it a “non-issue” in the country.
Yamagami told News24 on Tuesday that Albanese should consider visiting Japan this year to meet Takaichi, claiming the issue was a topic of debate in his country.
“We need to move on, but I think we need to show mutual respect to each other,” Yamagami said.
Labor MPs have closed ranks around Albanese, defending the prime minister and deflecting questions about his remarks.
Asked whether an apology was needed, Gorman said: “There is no need for that.”
The resources minister, Madeleine King, referred to the Japanese cable saying there had been “sensationalised reporting”, and claimed Albanese’s comments had been “mischaracterised”.
The agriculture minister, Julie Collins, said Albanese had rejected “the type of inference that you’re applying” while the environment minister, Murray Watt, said “some media interpretations of that episode of that podcast have been misinterpreted”.
The same podcast interview earlier attracted controversy after Albanese nominated singer Kylie Minogue while playing a game of “shag, marry, date” with Osborne. After the podcast, Albanese said he apologised “unequivocally” for those comments.
The host later said attention on the game had been a “moment taken out of context”.

title: Coalition divided over tougher gambling laws – with MPs warning Angus Taylor against overreach
summary:
Some Liberal and National MPs warned against over-regulation in party room discussion, while others argued for more stringent rules

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Coalition MPs have warned the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, not to overreach in talks with Anthony Albanese on Labor’s gambling advertising crackdown, insisting rules that are too stringent would not strike the right balance on personal responsibility.

The prime minister and the opposition leader continued talks on Tuesday over a deal to advance Labor’s legislation to limit online gambling advertising, with betting inducements and more restrictions on advertising hours among possible avenues for movement.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Coalition MPs have warned the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, not to overreach in talks with Anthony Albanese on Labor’s gambling advertising crackdown, insisting rules that are too stringent would not strike the right balance on personal responsibility.
The prime minister and the opposition leader continued talks on Tuesday over a deal to advance Labor’s legislation to limit online gambling advertising, with betting inducements and more restrictions on advertising hours among possible avenues for movement.
Debate over the issue dominated a meeting of the joint Coalition party room in Canberra on Tuesday, with nine Liberal and Nationals MPs making their views known to colleagues.
Among the contributions were five MPs pushing for tougher restrictions and four arguing the Coalition needed “to get the balance right” and not go too far in limiting advertising. Some warned overly restrictive rules for Australian gambling companies could push some punters to illegal overseas operators, citing comparisons with the rise of illegal tobacco amid rising government excises pushing up retail prices.
Taylor himself raised the question of personal responsibility in a media conference on Monday, an issue that was also raised in Tuesday’s meeting alongside concerns about “over-regulation”.
Coalition MPs used the meeting to raise concerns about “perceived behaviour of gambling preying on the vulnerable”, but the possibility of a deal remained “a moving feast” as parliament resumed after the winter break.
The gambling industry is increasingly resigned to the paring back of inducements, but it says that such restrictions could send gamblers to unregulated offshore operators and particularly impinge the earnings of smaller wagering operators.
Industry sources said they were seeking to warn Coalition MPs about the impact of further changes to inducements or ad rules, but rejected claims from the Greens that they were intimately involved in negotiations.
While Labor sources say they are still confident Taylor will get on board, the Greens are also still talking with the government, signalling a deal with the Coalition is not yet done. Albanese on Monday said publicly he would “later this week” have progress on inducements and advertising rules.
Labor has been criticised for falling short of the ambition of a parliamentary inquiry led by the late Labor MP Peta Murphy three years ago, and is talking with the Coalition and the Greens to find a pathway through the Senate. Murphy’s 2023 committee recommended the government “prohibit all online gambling inducements and inducement advertising, and that it do so without delay”.
Guardian Australia understands some small tweaks to the timing of TV advertising, specifically to lessen the impact on children, could be among the things being considered.
Labor’s proposed changes would see gambling ads restricted to three an hour on broadcast TV between 6am and 8.30pm. But further tweaks to that may be part of the discussions. Other reforms potentially in the frame could be around the discrepancy in ad rules on broadcast TV versus streaming services.
Opt-in provisions for advertising on streaming platforms are also being discussed.
Simon Kennedy, one of the Liberal MPs helping drive tougher action, used a speech in parliament to call for an independent review of the rules after the next election. That plan would help make any newly introduced protections even stronger within three years.
Kennedy said there were “two glaring gaps” in the existing laws: inducements to keep punters gambling longer and unlimited advertising online.
“There should be an independent review of wherever we land after the next election, so we can do more,” Kennedy said.
The government is expected to make amendments to the bill in the lower house, where the bill is listed for debate on Wednesday.

summary:
Elaborate ruse was used to transport president to military flight from Air Force One to return from Nato meet

Donald Trump departed on a secret military flight from Turkey to Britain last month when the White House said he was flying aboard ⁠Air Force One, in an extraordinary ruse – prompted by an Iranian assassination threat – that involved hiding the president in an airport catering container, according to reporting from the Washington Post and the New York Times.

The operation took place when Trump was in Ankara for a Nato summit with world leaders, according to the Post. Continue reading...
full_text:
Donald Trump departed on a secret military flight from Turkey to Britain last month when the White House said he was flying aboard Air Force One, in an extraordinary ruse – prompted by an Iranian assassination threat – that involved hiding the president in an airport catering container, according to reporting from the Washington Post and the New York Times.
The operation took place when Trump was in Ankara for a Nato summit with world leaders, according to the Post. The president reportedly boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras, and then was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies preflight, a US official told the Post.
An official also confirmed the operation to the New York Times.
The Guardian has reached out to the White House and the US Department of Defense for comment.
Trump’s actual location was concealed from journalists and some White House staff members. A US official told the Post that a credible threat to Trump involving Iran set the “deception operation” in motion.
The administration had previously claimed that Trump left Turkey on 8 July on the former Air Force One. The president had also announced on Truth Social that he would use the “former Air Force One” rather than the plane that flew him there, a new Boeing 747-8 gifted by Qatar.
The trip to the Nato summit was the first international travel for the new plane, whose speedy upgrades triggered questions over its cost and security, and took place as hostilities escalated with Iran, which borders Turkey.
Before departing Ankara, Trump said on Truth Social that he would use an older, baby blue Air Force One plane “for old time’s sake” to RAF Mildenhall in Britain while the new plane stopped at the same base so US service members stationed there could tour the aircraft.
After Trump boarded the old Air Force One in front of cameras in Ankara, he was secretly shuttled to a smaller plane, an Air Force C-32A, the Post reported, citing a US official familiar with the operation and corroborating material it reviewed.
The deception operation was triggered by a credible threat to Trump, the Post reported. A similar operation had taken place in 2000, when Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as decoy.
On this occasion, the journalists who thought they were traveling with Trump on the older Air Force One reported being advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post said aside from reporters, some White House staff also believed the president was on board.
When asked later by reporters why they had to keep their shades shut during the flight, Trump said it was because they were “probably on a dangerous flight”. He went onto say: “But if I go, you go. Right?”
The C-32A carrying Trump flew to Britain, arriving at around 10.20pm local time with the older Air Force One and media arriving minutes later, the Post reported.
The New York Times reported: “Mr Trump was brought by vehicle from the third plane that he had arrived on to the older Air Force One, boarded it through a different entrance and strode down the step from the upper left-side door as he would typically do, according to [a] US official.”
Trump’s traveling press pool reported he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10.56pm local time. He gave press a peace sign but didn’t walk over to talk to them. He then spent some time greeting service members before walking to the new, Qatar-donated plane.
When asked for comment on the revelation of a secret flight on a third plane, the White House provided a statement from Steve Cheung, the communications director, saying the Qatari-donated jet has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” Cheung said. It was the same statement provided to the Post.
Maanvi Singh and Reuters contributed to this report

title: A $2 trillion asset class is getting a new blockchain rail
full_text:
A $2 trillion asset class is getting a new blockchain rail
ADI Chain and Shipfinex are partnering to tokenize commercial ships, aiming to open the $680B ship-finance market to wider capital pool.
- ADI Chain and Shipfinex are partnering to tokenize commercial ships. No tokens have been issued yet.
- Shipfinex only holds a preliminary regulatory approval from Dubai's VARA, not a full operating license.
- This isn't the category's first – rivals Galactica and Ethra Ship already have live maritime tokenization deals
The world's commercial ships (the vessels themselves, not the cargo they carry) are worth an estimated $2 trillion in total. Yet the market financing their purchase and construction remains closed and relationship-driven, dominated by a small circle of shipowners, banks and specialist lenders.
That structure shuts smaller operators and alternative investors out of a significant pool of capital.
Blockchain platform ADI Chain and Dubai-based maritime tokenization firm Shipfinex want to route that market, worth an estimated $680 billion in bank lending, leasing and export credit today, through blockchain technology to open it up to a wider pool of institutional capital.
"Maritime finance has the scale, real assets and commercial activity to become a major new real-world asset category," Ramana Kumar, President of Stablecoin Ecosystem at ADI Foundation, said in the announcement shared with CoinDesk.
The deal signals that tokenization is expanding beyond financial instruments such as government bonds and money market funds into physical, capital-intensive infrastructure, like ships and warehouses, that underpin the global economy.
Shipfinex's job is to find ships and package them into deals while figuring out which vessels qualify, what they're worth, and how the investment should be structured.
ADI Chain's job is to turn those deals into blockchain tokens and handle payments using stablecoins (digital tokens pegged 1-to-1 to real currencies like the UAE dirham or the U.S. dollar), so money moves instantly without a traditional bank wire. For now, this is aimed at "qualified institutional participants," or large, vetted investors, not everyday retail buyers.
Shipfinex CEO Capt. Vikas Pandey said the partnership would let the company "create a regulated digital route into this market, with every instrument tied to a real vessel, its economics and its legal structure."
No maritime asset tokens have been issued yet and Shipfinex doesn't yet have a green light to do so. Its regulatory clearance from Dubai's Virtual Asseets Regulatory Authority is an "In-Principle Approval" — a preliminary thumbs-up confirming it has passed an initial background check, not a finished license to operate.
Nevertheless, Shipfinex has earmarked around 35 vessels worth about $500 million combined as candidates for tokenization, once the regulatory approval and deal structure are finalized. Each ship will eventually sit in its own separate legal entity, so if one ship runs into financial trouble, it doesn't drag down investors in the others.
Buying a token, once one becomes available, could mean one of a few different things for the institutional investors, depending on how each deal ends up being structured. It could mean a loan backed by the ship (similar to earning interest on a loan), a share of the money the ship earns from shipping contracts, or a broader economic stake in the vessel's value.
None of that, however, gives the token holder a share in legal ownership of the ship. The token only represents a financial claim tied to the vessel, while the ship itself stays owned and operated the way commercial ships always have been.
Maritime shipping accounts for more than 80% of international trade in goods by volume, according to Tuesday’s announcement, and remains a largely untapped corner of the tokenized real-world asset market, which currently stands at roughly $38 billion.
That said, the ADI and Shipfinex partnership isn't the category's opening move. Galactica has already closed tokenized vessel financings, including a bridge-financing deal for a 145,000 CBM LNG carrier, on InvestaX's regulated platform, and Ethra Ship launched a competing maritime RWA protocol in June built on an existing shipping business.
ADI Chain is the Abu Dhabi-based institutional blockchain platform founded by Sirius International Holding, the technology-focused subsidiary of International Holding Company (IHC). The blockchain already hosts DDSC, a dirham-backed stablecoin licensed by the UAE Central Bank. Earlier this year, IHC used DDSC to process a $30 million transaction on the chain.

Anthropic reportedly struck a $9 billion deal with Riot for 191 megawatts of capacity from the Bitcoin miner’s Rockdale campus in Texas.
Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms said it secured a 20-year agreement to supply 191 megawatts of capacity from its Rockdale, Texas, campus to a “leading frontier AI” company, according to a Monday press release.
The customer is Anthropic and the deal is valued at about $9 billion, Bloomberg reported Monday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Cointelegraph has approached Anthropic and Riot for comment.
Anthropic also struck a $19 billion deal for a 20-year data center lease with Bitcoin miner TeraWulf on July 6.
The reported agreement would add Riot to a growing list of Bitcoin miners expanding into AI and high-performance computing, including Bitdeer, CleanSpark, MARA Holdings, Core Scientific, Hut 8 and IREN.
Riot’s shares fell 5.4% on Monday but rose more than 21% in overnight trading. The stock is up more than 53% year–to–date, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Riot ranks as the world’s fourth-largest Bitcoin mining company with a $7.33 billion market capitalization, according to CompaniesMarketCap data.

title: Coinbase rolls out derivatives for UK professional investors
summary: Coinbase launches perpetuals, futures and options to UK professional clients after obtaining its MiFID license.
full_text:
Coinbase rolls out derivatives for UK professional investors
Quick Take
- Coinbase is rolling out perpetuals, dated futures, and crypto options to UK professional investors.
- The rollout follows Coinbase’s recently announced MiFID license.
We'd love your feedback.
Coinbase announced the launch of a suite of derivatives products for professional investors in the UK, expanding its derivatives offering as it advances its broader "Everything Exchange" strategy.
The exchange is rolling out perpetuals, dated futures, and crypto options to eligible UK professional clients, with access beginning progressively over the coming weeks, it said in a statement shared with The Block Tuesday.
According to the statement, the offering covers more than 170 contracts across crypto, commodities, equities, and foreign exchange, with perpetuals available around the clock and leverage of up to 50x.
Dated futures will offer fixed settlement dates and leverage of up to 20x, while the options offering will be limited to crypto and include calls, puts, and multi-leg strategies, the exchange said.
The launch follows Coinbase's recently announced MiFID license, which the company said enables it to offer derivatives contracts in the UK. Access is limited to investors who meet the eligibility requirements and are classified as professional clients.
The rollout also adds another product category to Coinbase's broader "Everything Exchange" strategy in the UK. The company has been expanding its product lineup beyond crypto trading to include equities, stablecoins, savings, and borrowing products.
Last week, the exchange began rolling out access to nearly 4,000 U.S. stocks for eligible UK users, adding equities trading alongside crypto and fiat holdings.
The derivatives rollout also comes as Coinbase has been expanding revenue sources beyond bitcoin spot trading. In its second-quarter report, Coinbase said 88% of its net revenue came from sources other than bitcoin spot trading, while its global crypto trading volume share reached a record 10.3%, up from 9.1% in the first quarter.
The company's UK expansion has followed its recently secured MiFID license, which Coinbase said expanded its permissions to offer more products, including derivatives for professional traders and equities for retail investors.
Coinbase describes itself as "the most comprehensively regulated crypto player" in the UK market. Its UK regulatory disclosures state that its subsidiary, CB Payments Ltd, is authorized and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority for investment services and is also authorized under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 for issuing electronic money.

title: UK Lawmakers Write to Bank CEOs Over Crypto Account Refusals
summary: The APPG has asked banks to explain their crypto policies, warning that access could be one of the single biggest barriers to growth.
full_text:
In brief
- The Crypto and Digital Assets APPG has written to the chief executives of all major UK banks asking them to set out their approach to crypto firms.
- The letter poses six questions, including whether banks expect to change tack once the FCA regime takes effect.
- It follows a parliamentary inquiry launched on July 21, with written submissions open until August 31.
The co-chairs of Parliament's Crypto and Digital Assets All-Party Parliamentary Group have written to the chief executives of every major UK bank, asking them to explain how they treat crypto and digital asset firms.
The letter, sent Tuesday by Labour MP Gurinder Singh Josan and Lord Vaizey of Didcot, a former digital economy minister, says the group has heard "repeated instances where crypto and digital asset firms have struggled to open accounts with UK banks," alongside reports that several banks have restricted crypto-related payments.
"Access to banking services could be one of the single biggest barriers to growth for UK crypto and digital asset businesses, and could potentially undermine the success of the UK's forthcoming crypto regime," the co-chairs wrote, adding that limited access could sway the decisions of firms weighing whether to invest in the country.
The letter puts six questions to each bank: what its policy is, whether it currently serves crypto firms and why not if it does not, what limits it applies to crypto-related transactions, what factors drive that approach, whether the incoming regime will change it, and what the Government or regulators could do to help.
Josan and Vaizey said they accept that banks have legal obligations to prevent financial crime and protect consumers, but noted that many firms argue decisions should reflect a company's individual risk profile more than the sector it sits in. Vaizey told the Financial Times that the difficulties amounted to "an unnecessary piece of friction" in running a business, and counted among the obstacles facing anyone setting up a firm in the UK.
UK banks including HSBC, Nationwide, NatWest, Santander and Starling have curbed crypto-related payments in recent years, with research from the UK Cryptoasset Business Council in January finding that banks were blocking or delaying an estimated 40% of attempted transfers to crypto exchanges.
Banks point to a rise in crypto-related scams and the risk of retail customers losing large sums to volatile prices, according to the FT, which reported that HSBC, NatWest, Monzo and Nationwide cap monthly transfers to crypto exchanges at between £5,000 and £10,000, while Starling and Chase UK bar them outright. Crypto losses are not covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.
What the Government has said
HM Treasury has already conceded the problem, with Economic Secretary Lucy Rigby telling Parliament in March that under the new regime the Government "would not expect" FCA-licensed firms to face restrictions from banks "simply because of the sector they belong to."
The letter follows the APPG's inquiry into banking access, launched July 21, which is taking written evidence until August 31 before reporting to Government. The co-chairs said the letter is not intended to pre-empt those findings. The FCA finalized its rules for the sector in June, with the regime becoming mandatory in October 2027.
Crypto debanking has been contested in other markets, with U.S. firms blaming a pressure campaign they call Operation Chokepoint 2.0 for cutting their banking ties, and Kraken winning $22 million from an auditor it said abandoned it during the episode.

title: 韓國廢除 700 美元免申報門檻：所有加密轉帳全面適用 Travel Rule
summary:
韓國內閣 8/11 批准修訂加密貨幣 Travel Rule，廢除原有的 700 美元門檻，所有註冊 VASP […]

〈韓國廢除 700 美元免申報門檻：所有加密轉帳全面適用 Travel Rule〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
韓國內閣 8/11 批准修訂加密貨幣 Travel Rule，廢除原有的 700 美元門檻，所有註冊 VASP 之間的轉帳都將納入資訊交換規範，6 個月後生效。
（前情提要：韓國擬實施「超嚴格反洗錢」打擊拆小額漏洞：金額680美元以下，交易所需KYC蒐集個資）
（背景補充：韓國執政黨推七大加密新政：廢除交易所銀行限制、開放比特幣ETF、STO 合法化…）
據 MSN 財經報導，韓國內閣於 8 月 11 日批准修訂《特定金融交易資訊報告及使用法施行令》，將加密貨幣 Travel Rule 的適用範圍從「100 萬韓元（約 700 美元）以上」擴大到所有金額，且規範物件涵蓋所有註冊虛擬資產服務提供者（VASP）之間的轉帳。
門檻歸零：堵住拆單規避漏洞
現行規則下，只有超過 100 萬韓元的轉帳才需要交換傳送者與接收者的身分資訊。韓國金融情報單位（Financial Intelligence Unit）指出，這留下了明顯的規避空間。
據 Business Insider 報導，官方揭露一起典型案例：
- 一名使用者將約 2 億韓元（約 14 萬美元）存入加密貨幣交易所
- 購買 Tether（USDT）後，分 216 筆提領
- 每筆金額都控制在 100 萬韓元以下，成功避開 Travel Rule 的資訊交換要求
修訂後，無論金額大小，接收平台都必須取得傳送者與接收者的完整資訊。如果資料不完整，平台可以要求補件或直接拒絕該筆交易。
海外交易所與個人錢包：依風險分級管理
這次修訂同時強化針對海外加密貨幣交易所和個人錢包的轉帳管理：
- 當地註冊 VASP 必須依交易對手的風險等級決定是否允許轉帳
- 轉往「低風險」海外交易所：允許
- 涉及其他境外交易所或個人錢包：通常僅限於傳送者與接收者為同一人的場景
- 被評估為高風險的交易對手：一律禁止
另外，針對涉及境外交易所或個人錢包、金額達1000 萬韓元（約 7000 美元）以上的轉帳，加密貨幣平台必須建立獨立的可疑交易監控系統。
韓國監管機構表示，隨著既有 AML 規則漏洞被利用，涉嫌透過海外交易所和個人錢包進行洗錢的案件已經增加。
VASP 註冊標準同步升級
《施行令》也同步提高 VASP 的註冊門檻，涵蓋以下面向：
- 財務健康度要求
- 內部控制機制
- 人力配置標準
- 基礎設施規範
- 大股東審查範圍擴大
VASP 註冊條款將於8 月 20 日生效，但現有業者獲一年緩衝期，可逐步符合財務、人力、基礎設施和內部控制的新要求。
時程：6 個月後全面適用
擴大後的 Travel Rule 及其他轉帳相關 AML 規範，將在《施行令》公布後6 個月生效。換言之，預計在 2026 年 2 月底前，韓國加密貨幣轉帳將完全進入「零門檻、全覆蓋」的資訊交換時代。
市場影響：合規成本上升、海外轉帳收緊
這次修法對韓國加密貨幣產業的短期與中期影響值得觀察。首先，零門檻 Travel Rule 意味著每筆轉帳都需要身分資料交換，VASP 的合規成本與技術負擔必然上升。對小額使用者來說，體驗可能變差，原本不受規範的 700 美元以下轉帳，現在也可能遭遇補件或延遲。
其次，海外交易所與個人錢包的分級管理，代表韓國使用者將鏈上 P2P 轉帳的便利性會受到限制。目前韓國使用者常透過海外去中心化錢包或境外交易所繞開國內限制，新規則讓這種做法的合規風險大幅提高。若 VASP 對境外轉帳採取保守態度（把更多對手列為高風險），實際效果可能接近「軟性鎖國」。
不過，從監管趨勢看，韓國這次修法與 FATF Travel Rule 的精神一致，也是亞洲加密法規逐漸向全球標準收斂的一環。對希望進軍韓國市場的國際 VASP 來說，CODE（Crypto Overseas Exchange Directory）合規與當地夥伴的 AML 協作，將是必要條件。

title: AFA Awards 30 強出爐！台灣 7 家提名 6 家入圍，XREX、奧丁丁、Whoscall 都上榜
summary:
亞洲金融科技聯盟（AFA）8 月 11 日公布第一屆 AFA Awards 30 強名單，台灣金融科技協會推薦 […]

〈AFA Awards 30 強出爐！台灣 7 家提名 6 家入圍，XREX、奧丁丁、Whoscall 都上榜〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
亞洲金融科技聯盟（AFA）8 月 11 日公布第一屆 AFA Awards 30 強名單，台灣金融科技協會推薦的七家企業有六家入圍，入圍率超過八成五，涵蓋跨境支付、資安、金融基礎建設與區塊鏈金融。30 強接下來將由國際創投、私募股權與主權財富基金組成的評審團選出 10 強，9 月 1 日在台北進行總決賽與頒獎。本文源自台灣金融科技協會發布之新聞稿，原始公告請見亞洲金融科技聯盟官方網站。
（前情提要：AFA Awards 9/1 台北決選 88 家，蔡玉玲：加密公司在 VASP 專法上路後就是金融機構）
（背景補充：奧丁丁 OwlPay Harbor 7 月金流處理量月增 107.6%，連六個月成長、企業客戶達 79 家）
重點摘要
- 台灣提名七家企業有六家挺進 AFA Awards 30 強，入圍率超過八成五
- 六家分屬金融基礎設施、監理合規、市場拓展三大獎項，XREX、奧丁丁、Whoscall 在列
- 第二階段評審團含凱雷、SBI、戈壁創投等機構，9 月 1 日台北選出 10 強
亞洲金融科技聯盟（Asia FinTech Alliance, AFA）8 月 11 日在台北正式公布第一屆亞洲金融科技大獎（AFA Awards）30 強名單。由台灣金融科技協會推薦的七家金融科技企業，共有六家成功搶進 30 強名單，彰顯台灣金融科技產業的堅強實力與國際競爭力。
台灣金融科技協會名譽理事長暨 AFA 主席蔡玉玲表示：「我們非常驕傲，台灣此次提名七家企業，有六家成功挺進 AFA Awards 30 強，入圍率超過八成五，展現台灣金融科技產業的強勁實力。AFA Awards 是亞太區域的國際級獎項，所有參賽企業均須由 AFA 會員正式提名，每個會員最多推薦七家企業參賽。換言之，企業在踏上國際競逐的舞台之前，首先必須在所屬市場中經過一輪嚴格的提名與篩選，能夠從亞洲 16 個經濟體的眾多參賽企業中脫穎而出、挺進 30 強，實屬不易。」
「下一階段的 10 強評選，將由來自國際創投、私募股權基金及主權財富基金的專家組成評審團，從企業的創新能力、市場潛力與跨境規模化能力等多個面向評分。我期待這六家台灣企業能贏得國際評審的肯定挺進 AFA Awards 決賽，串連 AFA 16 個亞洲經濟體的資源、人脈與資金，站上世界舞台為台灣金融科技產業爭光。」
六家台灣金融科技企業 獲選 AFA Awards 30 強
本次成功入圍 AFA Awards 30 強名單的台灣金融科技企業，涵蓋跨境支付、資安、金融科技基礎建設、區塊鏈金融等多個領域，展現台灣金融科技產業多元發展的成果。這 6 家企業分別入圍 AFA Awards 三大獎項，包括：
金融基礎設施卓越獎（Financial Infrastructure Award）
- 博士旺創新股份有限公司（BaaS Innovation CO., LTD.）
監理合規卓越獎（Regulatory Excellence Award）
- 走著瞧股份有限公司 Whoscall（Gogolook Co., Ltd.）
- 歐簿客科技（奧丁丁）（OwlTing Group, OBOOK Holdings Inc.）
- XREX 集團（XREX Inc., XREX Group）
市場拓展卓越獎（Market Expansion Award）
- 奧義賽博（CyCraft Technology）
- 東聯互動（EASTERN UNION INTERACTIVE CORP.）
（以上依企業英文名字字母排序。完整 AFA Awards 30 強名單請見文末附件一）
AFA Awards 總決賽與頒獎典禮 9/1 在台北登場
AFA Awards 為亞洲第一個由 16 個亞洲經濟體的代表性金融科技協會共同發起的區域性金融科技獎項。有別於多數獎項專注於鼓勵早期新創，AFA Awards 致力於尋找下一個亞洲金融科技的跨境獨角獸，表彰已有成功跨境經驗、具有規模化可能，且具備國際發展潛力的成熟企業。
第一屆 AFA Awards 五大獎項共獲得 88 個提名，競爭相當激烈。在公布 30 強名單後，入圍企業將進入第二階段評選出 10 強名單。第二階段評審團陣容堅強，匯聚亞洲金融與資本市場代表，包括：中華開發資本、馬來西亞大華銀行（UOB）、全球知名私募股權投資機構凱雷集團（Carlyle Group）、日本 SBI Investment、戈壁創投（Gobi Partners）、韓國 KB 金融集團旗下創投 KB Investment、四大會計師事務所安永在菲律賓的成員所 SGV & Co.、烏茲別克創投 TMT Global，以及斯里蘭卡 Fintech Digital Pvt Ltd 等機構。透過串聯銀行、創投、私募股權與專業諮詢服務等多元資本與產業資源，AFA Awards 也進一步成為連結優質國際資本的重要平台。
AFA Awards 將於 2026 年 9 月 1 日在台北舉行 AFA Awards 頒獎典禮。入選 10 強的企業與第二階段評審團都將親自來到台北，於當日進行總決賽的現場簡報，評選出第一屆 AFA Awards 五大獎項的最終贏家。
關於台灣金融科技協會（TFTA）
台灣金融科技協會（TFTA）是一個非營利組織，旨在促進台灣金融科技（Fintech）的發展和創新。它成立於 2017 年，自此成為台灣金融科技業的領導者之一。
TFTA 倡導支持國內和國際金融科技創新的監管政策和措施。TFTA 與政府單位、產業利害關係人和國際組織有著密切的聯繫，是台灣金融科技界聯繫、合作和促進發展的重要平台。
TFTA 是亞洲金融科技聯盟（Asia FinTech Alliance, AFA）的正式成員，該聯盟是由亞洲各國和地區的金融科技協會組成的聯盟。TFTA 與 AFA 之間的策略合作夥伴關係使台灣能夠積極參與更廣泛的亞洲金融科技界，符合區域趨勢並擴大台灣在全球金融科技領域的影響力。

（以下名單依企業英文名字的字母排序）
年度跨境金融科技獨角獸潛力獎（Grand Award – Cross-Border Fintech Unicorn Potential）
金融基礎設施卓越獎（Financial Infrastructure Award）
監理合規卓越獎（Regulatory Excellence Award）
市場拓展卓越獎（Market Expansion Award）
高速成長卓越獎（Fastest Growth Award）

常見問題
台灣有哪六家企業入圍 AFA Awards 30 強？
金融基礎設施卓越獎的博士旺創新，監理合規卓越獎的走著瞧（Whoscall）、歐簿客科技（奧丁丁）與 XREX 集團，以及市場拓展卓越獎的奧義賽博與東聯互動，是台灣提名七家中入圍的六家。
AFA Awards 30 強之後的流程是什麼？
30 強將進入第二階段評選出 10 強，評審團由中華開發資本、大華銀行、凱雷集團、SBI Investment、戈壁創投等機構組成。10 強企業須於 9 月 1 日到台北現場簡報，當天選出五大獎項最終得主。

title: CME 機構淨多頭只有 2,100 枚 BTC，槓桿基金仍淨空 36,200 枚
summary:
CryptoQuant 創辦人 Ki Young Ju 提醒，CFTC 截至 8 月 4 日數據顯示，CME […]

〈CME 機構淨多頭只有 2,100 枚 BTC，槓桿基金仍淨空 36,200 枚〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
CryptoQuant 創辦人 Ki Young Ju 提醒，CFTC 截至 8 月 4 日數據顯示，CME 全體申報交易者確實小幅淨多，但規模只有 420 口、約 2,100 枚 BTC，僅佔未平倉 2.09%。翻多的是交易商與資產管理，槓桿基金在標準比特幣期貨仍淨空 36,200 枚 BTC。
（前情提要：CryptoQuant：CME 避險基金轉多：比特幣期貨罕見出現淨多頭）
（背景補充：30 年美債殖利率飆破 5.2% 創 2007 年後最高，金融海嘯前夕的既視感）
重點摘要
- 撐起 CME 淨多頭的是交易商與資產管理，兩者合計淨多 27,555 枚 BTC，槓桿基金反而淨空 36,200 枚
- 槓桿基金跨標準與微型合約的淨空頭一年內從 72,424 枚縮到 35,806 枚 BTC，減幅 50.6%
- 三個月期貨基差年化約 3%，低於 8 月 7 日 2 年期美債的 4.19%，自 2 月起連續六個月倒掛
美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）最新一期持倉報告的資料日落在 8 月 4 日，CME 標準比特幣期貨的全體大額申報交易者（Total Reportables）淨多 420 口合約，換算約 2,100 枚 BTC，只佔當週未平倉合約的 2.09%。
CryptoQuant 創辦人 Ki Young Ju 以這份資料補充他先前的部位判斷，機構偏多的方向沒變，但幅度小到必須說清楚，因為這欄不是避險基金一家的部位。
淨多頭只有 420 口
Ki Young Ju 特別點出，Total Reportables 涵蓋的不只避險基金，資產管理機構、交易商與其他達到申報門檻的交易者都算在內。CFTC 這份金融期貨交易者報告把 CME 標準比特幣期貨（一口 5 枚 BTC）的參與者分成四個申報類別，8 月 4 日當週未平倉合約 20,143 口，各類別淨部位換算成 BTC 之後如下。
- 交易商與中介機構: 淨多 2,969 口，約 14,845 枚 BTC
- 資產管理與機構投資人: 淨多 2,542 口，約 12,710 枚 BTC
- 槓桿基金: 淨空 7,240 口，約 36,200 枚 BTC
- 其他申報交易者: 淨多 2,149 口，約 10,745 枚 BTC
把四類相加就得到前面那 420 口，前三類的多頭合計 38,300 枚 BTC，幾乎剛好被槓桿基金的 36,200 枚空頭抵銷，剩下的那點差額就是所謂的「小幅淨多頭」。
Ki Young Ju 口中的 hedge funds，在 CFTC 分類裡對應 Leveraged Funds（槓桿基金）這一欄，而它到 8 月 4 日仍是淨空，空單佔全部未平倉的 57.0%。撐起那筆淨多頭的是交易商與資產管理機構的帳，不是套利基金掉頭。
基差收益跌到公債之下
槓桿基金的空單長年以來不是看空，是基差交易另一條腿。買進現貨、同時在期貨端放空，鎖定期貨相對現貨的溢價，收的是展期收益。這套策略只要基差高於無風險利率就有利可圖，2021 年牛市主要交易所的年化基差曾衝破 20%。
基差交易讓他們在結構上長期偏空，這就是為什麼這張圖多年來一直是紅的。你沒辦法用套利交易做出一個淨多頭。
現在這個前提消失了，CoinDesk 引述的三個月期貨年化基差約 3%，而美國 2 年期公債殖利率 8 月 7 日收在 4.19%，10 年期 4.65%、30 年期 5.19%。扣掉交易對手風險與展期摩擦，收益比直接買公債還低約 1.2 個百分點，這條腿越來越短了。
8 月 3 日的統計指出，三個月基差自 2026 年 2 月起每個月都低於 2 年期公債殖利率，這是有紀錄以來第二次。上一次倒掛出現在 2022 年 8 月到 2023 年 1 月，持續約五個月，結束在那一輪週期低點之後。這次已經走到第六個月，比上次更長。
*本文僅供參考，不構成投資建議。加密貨幣市場波動劇烈，投資前請審慎評估風險。*
常見問題
CME 的 Total Reportables 是什麼？
指 CFTC 持倉報告中所有達到申報門檻的大額交易者總和，包含交易商、資產管理機構、槓桿基金與其他申報者四類。8 月 4 日 CME 標準比特幣期貨這項數字為淨多 420 口，約 2,100 枚 BTC。
槓桿基金為什麼長期在比特幣期貨做空？
主要是基差交易。買進現貨同時放空期貨，鎖定期貨溢價收取展期收益，期貨端因此結構性偏空。當三個月基差年化約 3%、低於 2 年期美債 4.19% 時，這套策略就失去吸引力。
本文由 Mickey帽鼠（幣價分析作者）整理撰寫。

full_text:
CryptoQuant 分析師 Axel Adler Jr 在 8 月 11 日指出，持有 0 到 3 個月的比特幣買家 NUPL 已回升至 -0.02，距離盈虧平衡只差 2%，但持有 3 到 6 個月的群體仍停在 -0.14。比特幣同日報 64,048 美元，24 小時下跌 1.77%，年輕籌碼的壓力來源正在往上一個年齡層集中。

重點摘要

CryptoQuant 分析師 Axel Adler Jr 在同日發布的鏈上晨報分析，把年輕籌碼拆成兩格來看，結論是市場的壓力來源換人了。
新買家 NUPL 回到 -0.02
NUPL 衡量特定年齡層的幣相對其取得成本的未實現損益。0 到 3 個月群體的 NUPL 已從 6 月的 -0.13 回升到 -0.02，接近盈虧平衡；3 到 6 個月群體仍停在 -0.14，同樣自 6 月低點反彈，但幅度小得多。
用現價回推，兩批人的成本差距相當清楚。0 到 3 個月群體的平均取得成本約在 65,300 美元，只比現價高 2%。3 到 6 個月群體約在 72,989 美元，比現價高出 12.3%。
Axel Adler Jr 在 8 月 8 日給出的短期持有者已實現價格是 67,523 美元，當時現貨 64,952 美元，低於成本 3.81%。短期持有者涵蓋 0 到 155 天，正好是上面兩格的加總，3.8% 落在兩者之間，互相驗證。
四月買入者套最深
今年 4 月 22 日，灰度研究主管 Zach Pandl 用過同一套邏輯給出樂觀判斷。當時比特幣約 76,000 美元，1 到 3 個月交易者的已實現價格約 74,000 美元，短期買家剛好由虧轉盈。
如果比特幣價格在未來幾天進一步上漲，會有更多近期買家進入獲利區間，這通常標誌著牛市的第一階段。
（灰度研究主管 Zach Pandl，2026 年 4 月 22 日）
他當時認為 65,000 至 70,000 美元已經構成「堅實底部」。從 4 月 22 日到 8 月 11 日是三個半月，那批剛回本的買家現在正好落在 3 到 6 個月這一格，平均成本 72,989 美元，跟灰度給的 74,000 美元幾乎重疊。四個月過去，他們從回本變成虧 12.3%，堅實底部區間也已經失守。
差別在於這一次的接近回本是怎麼來的。4 月是價格站回成本之上，這次是成本追著價格往下修，新買家的成本基礎只有 65,300 美元，因為他們全部在低位進場。NUPL 修復不等於價格修復。
已實現市值回撤不是虧損，是籌碼在老化
3 到 6 個月群體的已實現市值回撤從 6 月中的 -53% 擴大到 -69.6%，兩個月惡化 16.6 個百分點，是近 90 天最差讀數；0 到 3 個月群體則長期維持在 -64% 附近，兩者差距 5.6 個百分點。
Axel Adler Jr 在報告裡特別澄清，這個指標不能直接解讀成已實現虧損或資金外流。年齡層是流動的，幣會從 0 到 3 個月移進 3 到 6 個月再移出去，指標衡量的是某個年齡層當前的已實現價值離自身高點有多遠。
換句話說，-69.6% 不是這群人虧掉近七成本金，而是這一格沉澱的資金規模只剩自身峰值的三成。新錢沒補進來，舊籌碼持續老化出去。
宏觀沒有給喘息空間
10 年期美債殖利率 8 月 11 日報 4.73%，較前一交易日上行 2 個基點。市場對 9 月升息 25 個基點的押注升到 51%，前一天還是 44%，推力來自油價走高帶起的通膨疑慮。克里夫蘭聯準會主席 Beth Hammack 表示，要把通膨拉回 2% 目標，可能需要多次升息。
另一邊的就業數據卻在轉弱。7 月非農就業意外減少 23,000 人，5 月與 6 月合計向下修正 103,000 人。就業走弱疊加通膨升溫，聯準會兩頭被綁住，這種組合同時抽走了降息的想像空間與經濟成長的支撐。恐慌貪婪指數 8 月 11 日讀數 29，落在恐懼區，前兩日分別是 31 與 30。
兩條警戒線比支撐位更值得盯
技術面上，比特幣近一個月在 63,800 至 65,400 美元之間反覆整理。上方第一道阻力就是 0 到 3 個月群體的平均成本 65,300 美元，站穩才代表最新一批買家真正翻正，再上去是短期持有者整體的已實現價格 67,523 美元。往下看，8 月 11 日凌晨的 63,806.27 美元是這波低點，若失守，六萬美元整數關是下一道防線。
衍生品端沒有明顯的槓桿堆積，全網比特幣未平倉合約約 467.5 億美元，幣安 BTCUSDT 永續未平倉量 106,322 枚，資金費率 0.002007%（八小時結算），接近中性略偏多方付費，沒有出現軋空行情前常見的深度負值。8 月 11 日凌晨那波下殺，4 小時爆倉 1 億美元，24 小時全網清算 1.86 億美元、74,959 人，量級屬於清洗浮動槓桿，不是系統性去槓桿。
比起支撐位，Axel Adler Jr 給的兩條線更明確。3 到 6 個月群體的 NUPL 重新站上零，代表壓力真正解除；反過來，若 0 到 3 個月群體的 NUPL 掉回 -0.10 以下，代表未實現壓力正在往最新一批買家蔓延。已實現市值回撤那邊也有一條，3 到 6 個月群體若持續往 -70% 以下走，說明這一格相對自身峰值還在弱化。
常見問題
NUPL 是什麼指標，-0.02 代表什麼？
NUPL 衡量特定年齡層的幣相對取得成本的未實現損益。-0.02 代表該群體平均仍虧 2%，用 8 月 11 日的 64,048 美元回推，0 到 3 個月買家的平均成本約 65,300 美元，已經很接近盈虧平衡。
已實現市值回撤 -69.6% 是不是代表這群人虧掉近七成？
不是。它衡量的是該年齡層當前已實現市值距離自身歷史高點多遠。幣會在年齡層之間流動，Axel Adler Jr 特別註明這個指標不能直接等同已實現虧損或資金外流。

title: 兩根鐵磨出台灣首富！85 歲川湖林聰吉憑「伺服器滑軌」，身家 5,387 億超車郭台銘
summary:
《富比士》台灣首富換人！85 歲川湖董座林聰吉憑伺服器滑軌，身家 5,387 億超車國巨陳泰銘、鴻海郭台銘。他 […]

〈兩根鐵磨出台灣首富！85 歲川湖林聰吉憑「伺服器滑軌」，身家 5,387 億超車郭台銘〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
《富比士》台灣首富換人！85 歲川湖董座林聰吉憑伺服器滑軌，身家 5,387 億超車國巨陳泰銘、鴻海郭台銘。他如何用七十年磨出 AI 時代的隱形冠軍？
（前情提要：國巨陳泰銘4900億登上新台灣首富！被動元件之王押 AI 年飆125% ）
8月 11 日，《富比士》即時富豪榜悄悄改寫了台灣財富史：登上首富寶座的，不是科技新貴，也不是金融世家，而是一位85歲、只有國小學歷的「黑手」：川湖科技董事長林聰吉。
他以 167 億美元（約新台幣 5,387 億元）的身家，一舉超車國巨陳泰銘與鴻海郭台銘。
讓他攀上頂峰的，不是晶片、不是面板，而是伺服器機櫃裡兩根不起眼的金屬滑軌。
從抽屜學徒到鐵工廠老闆
1941 年出生於高雄的林聰吉，自幼家境清苦，國小四年級就被送進家具廠當學徒，蹲在木屑堆裡學做抽屜；國小畢業後，他再也沒有踏進校門。
但數十年與五金、機械為伍的日子，把他的雙手磨成了最精密的儀器。1977 年他投入五金業，從門把做起、再轉做鉸鏈；1986 年，45 歲的他在高雄路竹創立川湖科技，當時，這只是一間生產門把、鉸鏈和家具滑軌的傳統鐵工廠，沒有人多看一眼。
一紙急單改寫命運
命運的轉折來得又急又狠。2000 年前後，一家占營收近四成的大客戶強硬要求降價三成，林聰吉硬是不從，結果訂單被砍、營收腰斬，四成員工出走，公司瀕臨破產。
誰也沒想到，絕境竟是天堂的入口。2001 年，電腦大廠康柏（Compaq）因原供應商設計出包，緊急尋找替代廠商，林聰吉抓住這根救命繩索，一週內交出設計圖並通過認證，拿下約 10 萬美元的伺服器滑軌試產訂單。
就是這張急單，把一間家具五金廠推進了全球伺服器供應鏈，自有品牌「King Slide」從此誕生。
被砍單砍怕了的林聰吉，立下鐵律：只做高門檻、高毛利的產品，絕不跟人拚價格。他的名言是：「一台伺服器那麼貴，沒人會拿頭髮試火。」意思是，客戶買的是萬無一失，不是最低價。
1％ 的成本、100％的命門
這個哲學在 AI 時代迎來大爆發。一組滑軌占整座 AI 機櫃成本不到1％，卻是工程師上架、抽拉維修伺服器時唯一的依靠；輝達 GB200 整櫃重量突破一噸，價值連城的 AI 伺服器全掛在那兩根鐵上，承重、精度、穩定度差一絲一毫都不行。
川湖靠著逾 3,700 項專利築起護城河，加上少量多樣、快速交期的客製化能力，讓客戶想換供應商都難。
成績單說明一切：2026 年第 2 季毛利率高達 87.42％，比許多晶片設計公司還驚人；上半年稅後純益 105.74 億元、年增 237％，每股純益 110.96 元。
前七月營收 226.87 億元、年增 136.58％。股價更在 8 月 6 日衝破萬元大關，成為台股史上第三檔「萬金股」，8月 11 日盤中站上 1.2 萬元，林聰吉單日身家一度暴增約 354 億元。
85 歲仍天天巡廠
登上首富，林聰吉沒有停下腳步。當年單一客戶的教訓，如今變成另一種風險：導軌產品占營收比重高達97.87％。
為此，川湖斥資約 100 億元在台擴產，美國休士頓廠預計今年 9 月量產，分散地緣風險；同時為輝達下一代 Rubin 平台開發更高承重的新品，並悄悄布局機器人零組件。女
兒林淑珍以總經理身分掌舵營運，85 歲的林聰吉則依然每天動腦、巡廠。
從木屑堆裡的小學徒，到身家 5,387 億元的台灣首富，林聰吉花了七十多年證明一件事：再不起眼的零件，只要做到沒人比你好，就能卡住整個時代的重量。

title: Claude 宣布 AI 生成內容全面埋入「隱形浮水印」與數位簽章
summary:
Anthropic 宣布 Claude 生成內容將全面嵌入隱形浮水印與 C2PA 數位簽章，回應歐盟 AI 法 […]

〈Claude 宣布 AI 生成內容全面埋入「隱形浮水印」與數位簽章〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Anthropic 宣布 Claude 生成內容將全面嵌入隱形浮水印與 C2PA 數位簽章，回應歐盟 AI 法案透明度義務，全球適用。
（前情提要：Claude Opus 4.6 來了：自己寫編譯器、做 PPT、隨手挖出 500 個零日漏洞，你的工作它都想試試）
（背景補充：Anthropic 新推「回顧儀錶板」：檢視你跟 Claude 互動、教你更聰明與 AI 協作）
AI 生成的文章、圖片滿天飛，到底哪些出自人類之手？Anthropic 今日更新重大措施：自 2026 年 8 月 2 日起，旗下聊天機器人 Claude 生成的內容將全面嵌入「機器可讀標記」，文字藏著肉眼看不見的浮水印、檔案則附上數位簽章的來源紀錄，而且適用範圍遍及全球。
這是歐盟《AI法案》（AI Act）第 50 條透明度義務正式上路後，大型 AI 公司交出的首批成績單之一，也象徵「AI內容無從辨識」的時代開始走向終結。
隱形浮水印＋數位簽章
根據 Anthropic 官方說明文件，Claude 的標記機制分為兩套。
第一套是「嵌入式文字浮水印」：在生成的文字中直接編織難以察覺的訊號，官方強調「不會改變回應的含義、品質或可讀性」，使用者閱讀時完全無感；當文字被複製貼上到其他地方，浮水印也會跟著傳播。
由於浮水印在模型層級套用，所有 Claude 產品與介面一體適用。
第二套是「簽署的來源元資料」，適用於 SVG、PNG、JPG 等檔案類型，採用「內容來源和真實性聯盟」（C2PA）的開放標準，在檔案中附加數位簽章，證明該檔案曾經 Claude 處理，還能偵測檔案事後是否遭到篡改。
這套機制涵蓋 Claude 應用程式、API 平台、Claude Code 等全系列產品，就連透過 AWS、Google Cloud 或 Microsoft Foundry 等雲端夥伴取用的服務也不例外。
2026 年 8 月 2 日後推出的新模型自上線起即支援標記，較早的模型也正在加緊改造。Anthropic 並承諾將公開偵測方法的技術文件，讓使用者與第三方都能驗證內容是否經 Claude 之手。
歐盟《AI法案》上路
Anthropic 此舉並是回應歐盟《AI法案》第 50 條的透明度義務。該條款自 2026 年 8 月 2 日起適用，要求 AI 供應商為生成或篡改的「合成內容」加上機器可讀標記，讓下游用戶、平台與監管機關能辨識AI產物。
今年 5 月歐盟通過的「AI綜合法案」（AI Omnibus）暫時協議，則給予既有系統寬限至 12 月 2 日。歐盟執委會同時推出自願性的《AI生成內容透明度行為準則》，鼓勵業者採用開放標準與統一的標示圖示，Anthropic 即是簽署承諾的業者之一。
值得注意的是，Anthropic 選擇「全球一體適用」而非只在歐洲實施，等於讓布魯塞爾的法規再度發揮「布魯塞爾效應」，形塑全球 AI 產業的遊戲規則。
偵測到標記≠AI原創
不過 Anthropic 也坦承，這套標記並非萬無一失的「測謊器」。
首先，偵測到標記只代表內容「曾由 Claude 處理」，不代表 Claude 是原作者，許多人用 Claude 校對、翻譯或摘要人類撰寫的文字。
其次，沒有標記也不能證明內容出自人類：舊模型生成的內容、經大幅改寫的文字、過短的段落都可能不帶標記；圖片只要經過截圖或格式轉換，元資料就會消失。
科技媒體《The Register》更不客氣地指出，研究早已證明影像浮水印可被移除，光學字元辨識（OCR）技術也能輕易繞過文字浮水印，網路上甚至已有現成的 C2PA 元資料移除工具；報導並分析，此舉可能反而推升不帶浮水印的開源模型吸引力，因為部分使用者「未必希望讀者知道內容是 AI 寫的」。
透明度軍備競賽才剛開始
儘管技術上仍有漏洞，AI 內容標記已是大勢所趨。
對內容農場、學術抄襲、深偽詐騙等亂象而言，浮水印至少墊高了造假成本；對一般使用者來說，未來看到一篇文章、一張圖片時，多了一個追溯來源的線索。
這場 AI 透明度軍備競賽，考驗的將是科技公司的誠意，以及道高一尺、魔高一丈的攻防能耐。

title: 比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈落後 326 區塊、自我修復還要 6.3 年：礦工不買單
summary:
比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈在 8 月 9 日分裂後只挖出 2 個區塊就停擺，目前落後主網 326 個區塊。 […]

〈比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈落後 326 區塊、自我修復還要 6.3 年：礦工不買單〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈在 8 月 9 日分裂後只挖出 2 個區塊就停擺，目前落後主網 326 個區塊。由於分叉鏈繼承了與主網相同的挖礦難度，卻沒有任何市場價值，礦工缺乏挖礦動機；而它要等到挖滿 2,016 個區塊才能降低難度，依當前進度估計還需 6.3 年以上。
（前情提要：比特幣今晨軟分叉！BIP-110 支持者跑少數鏈，主網已甩開 26 區塊）
（背景補充：比特幣 BIP-110 分叉只挖 2 個區塊就卡死，先鋒礦工 Roughnecks 宣布放棄）
比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈在分裂不到 48 小時後已進入實質停滯期。根據資料，這條少數派鏈仍停在第 961,633 個區塊，也就是分裂後挖出的第二個區塊。主網則已前進至第 961,959 個區塊，差距擴大到 326 個區塊。
BIP-110 怎麼分裂比特幣的？
BIP-110 是一項比特幣改進提案，主張在一年內禁止使用者在比特幣交易上儲存圖片、文字等非付款資料。改變比特幣共識規則需要礦工同意，協議要求兩週內有 55% 的區塊標記支援才算透過。BIP-110 在整個計票週期內的最高支援率僅約 2.6%。
提案設計了一條「第二路線」，當區塊到達 961,632 時，執行 BIP-110 軟體的節點將開始拒絕所有未標記支援的區塊，不管礦工意願。幾乎沒有區塊帶標記，於是這些節點拒絕了主網絕大部分算力建構的鏈，轉而追隨僅由標記區塊組成的少數派鏈。
為什麼分叉鏈挖不動？
核心問題在於算力與獎勵的失衡。分叉鏈分裂時繼承了與主網相同的挖礦難度，但兩個關鍵條件讓礦工毫無動力：
- 挖礦成本與主網完全相同，同樣的算力要求
- 產出的幣沒有市場、沒有交易所上線、沒有買家
比特幣的挖礦難度調整機制是每 2,016 個區塊重新計算一次，若區塊產出太慢就降難度、太快就升難度。在正常節奏下，2,016 個區塊約需兩週。
分叉鏈要降低難度，必須先挖滿 2,016 個區塊。依照目前每小時近乎零的產出速度，一個即時監控器估計下一次難度調整要 6.3 年，比上週日的 350 天大幅後退。
這個數字是從近期的區塊產出間距推算的，所以每一小時停滯都會讓它更遠。主網比特幣的下次難度調整則定在 12 天後。
有人認為為時尚早
並非所有人都認為這已是定局。Arch 共同創辦人 Himanshu Sahay 透過訊息對 CoinDesk 表示：
我認為從初期的區塊產出下任何明確結論都為時過早。比特幣規則的改變依賴礦工、開發者與整體生態系統之間的協調，雖然這個差距值得關注，但我謹慎看待將它描述為失敗的說法。
冷麵分析：這場分叉的三個觀察點
BIP-110 分叉鏈的停滯並非意外，而是協議設計與經濟誘因錯配的必然結果。從三個角度來看後續發展：
第一，分叉鏈的唯一齣路是「有人願意白挖」。 難度調整機制是數學規則，沒有外部幹預的選項。除非有礦工願意在無市場價值的條件下持續投入算力，否則這條鏈將成為一個靜止的區塊鏈化石。這不是一場技術戰，而是一場耐心與成本的消耗戰。
第二，BIP-110 的「強制路線」暴露了比特幣共識模型的脆弱點。 提案設計者認為可以在礦工不買單的情況下，透過節點軟體單方面強行分裂。但結果顯示：沒有算力支援的鏈，節點再多也沒有意義。這不是第一次有人試圖繞過共識（參見 Roughnecks 礦池的早期嘗試），但每次的結果都在證明同一件事，比特幣的共識是算力共識，不是投票共識。
第三，BIP-110 事件對比特幣協議治理的長期影響尚未發酵。 短期內這條分叉鏈將被市場遺忘，但它揭示了一個問題：任何協議層面的「強制變更」如果與經濟誘因相悖，最終都會被算力市場用腳投票。在比特幣社群對協議升級日益分歧的背景下，這可能成為未來提案設計者需要正視的一課。

title: BlackRock：比特幣與美股脫鉤趨勢浮現，ETF 資金流創 4 月以來最佳
summary:
BlackRock 數位資產主管 Robert Mitchnick 指出，過去約一個月比特幣市場情緒出現溫和改 […]

〈BlackRock：比特幣與美股脫鉤趨勢浮現，ETF 資金流創 4 月以來最佳〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
BlackRock 數位資產主管 Robert Mitchnick 指出，過去約一個月比特幣市場情緒出現溫和改善，BTC 與美股的相關性今年以來持續下降。上週美國現貨比特幣 ETF 連續五個交易日淨流入，合計約 8.535 億美元，創 4 月中旬以來最佳單周表現。
（前情提要：比特幣 ETF 單週吸金十億美元創 4 月新高，Coldcard 錢包漏洞效應浮現？）
（背景補充：Wintermute 最新報告：加密市場展現抗跌韌性，美股靠 AI 基金百億爆倉洩壓）
黑石集團（BlackRock）數位資產主管 Robert Mitchnick 在 8 月 10 日的訪問中表示，過去約一個月比特幣市場情緒出現「明顯但溫和」的改善，今年以來 BTC 與美股的相關性已有所下降。
BTC 與美股的「脫鉤」趨勢
Mitchnick 指出，7 月 AI 概念股大幅回撥期間，比特幣表現明顯優於美股。這種相對跑贏的現象，強化了比特幣作為資產組合分散工具的邏輯，並使其成為潛在的尾部風險避險資產。
他說，今年早些時候比特幣與美股逐步脫鉤，一度被視為負面訊號，但隨著 7 月 AI 股大跌而 BTC 相對穩住，這種「脫鉤」被重新解讀為健康發展——比特幣不再完全跟隨美股科技股的波動。
ETF 資金流：長線持有者主導
Mitchnick 強調，比特幣 ETF 的投資者仍以基本面驅動、長期持有型資金為主，而非短線投機。資金流資料支援這一觀察：
- 上週美國現貨比特幣 ETF 連續五個交易日淨流入
- 合計流入約 8.535 億美元，創 4 月中旬以來最佳單周表現
- 其中 BlackRock IBIT 單隻流入約 6.937 億美元，佔總流入逾 80%
同步進展：IBIT 實物換購門檻大降
同一時間，BlackRock 將 BTC 實物換購 IBIT 的最低門檻，由原先的 2,500 萬美元大幅降至 100 萬美元。Mitchnick 表示，未來希望進一步降低門檻，最終讓任意規模的投資者都能使用該機制。
這項調整降低了機構和大型投資人將既有 BTC 轉入 ETF 的門檻，可能進一步強化 IBIT 在市場中的主導地位。

title: Trump hidden in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
summary: The US president was moved from the old Air Force One to a military plane as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month, US media say.
full_text:
Trump hidden in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
- Published
Donald Trump secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month in response to a possible Iranian threat, US media report.
The US president boarded Air Force One in view of television cameras before being smuggled onto an elevated airport catering truck and transported to a military aircraft, without journalists and some White House staff on board knowing, the Washington Post said.
Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The White House has not confirmed the secret switch.
Trump had earlier said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara.
The clandestine manoeuvre came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war.
Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake".
On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport. But according to the Washington Post, he was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice president - via a catering truck which had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs in an effort to make the flight appear normal, according to the newspaper.
Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board.
Trump then flew to the UK en route to the US, where he reboarded the old Air Force One and was seen descending from the aircraft after it landed at RAF Mildenhall. It is unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the legacy jet.
The president then transferred to the new Qatari-donated Air Force One to travel back to Washington.
During that flight, Trump spoke to reporters on board where he noted the threats posed by Iran but did not mention the earlier plane swap.
Asked why reporters had been told to lower the window shades on the plane from Turkey, Trump said: "Because you're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags we have to deal with."
He said he had a "threat all the time" on his life, and that he is "number one" on Iran's "list".
"But if I go, you go, right?", he said, adding: "Perhaps someday you want to change professions."
White House communications director Steven Cheung did not directly confirm or deny the reports, but said the new Air Force One was a "state-of-the-art aircraft" fitted with security measures to protect the president and his staff.
US intelligence had previously warned of a specific threat of an attack on Trump or his aircraft, according to earlier reporting by CBS News.
The New York Times previously reported on security concerns regarding the Qatari-gifted jet, including that the Secret Service had urged Trump to switch planes on his return from the Nato summit.
Several of the publication's journalists were summoned to testify under oath in response. The Justice Department subsequently told the BBC that it was investigating illegal leaks.
The US has spent months retrofitting the $400m Boeing 747-8 to prepare it for the president. Older Air Force One planes have laser technology to blind incoming missiles, sources have told CBS News. It is unclear what systems the Qatari jet has.
"The new Air Force One is perfectly safe for the President's travels, but will receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement to CBS News.

title: Man, 29, arrested in police raid over racist traffic-cone attack
summary: Police are investigating after a traffic cone was thrown at a delivery driver following an anti-immigration protest in Glasgow last month.
full_text:
Man, 29, arrested in police raid over racist traffic-cone attack
- Published
Police have arrested a man over an attack on a delivery driver during disorder in Glasgow city centre last month.
A traffic cone was thrown at Muhammad Jawad Yaqoob, 31, following an anti-immigration protest at Glasgow Green on 25 July.
Officers have charged a 29-year-old man with racially-aggravated assault over the incident, which was filmed and widely shared on social media.
He was arrested in the Govan area of the city. Fifteen people were arrested on the day of the protests.
Police Scotland said a major investigation team was trying to identify more suspects and further arrests are planned.
An anti-racism protest had taken place at Glasgow Green before counter-protesters turned up at the scene last month.
Police said "disparate groups" engaged in acts of violence, disorder, intimidation and hate-motivated offences at various locations - all coinciding with the opening weekend of the Commonwealth Games.
The force said 1,700 people were in attendance and an operation was put in place to support public safety and minimise disruption.
Delivery driver Yaqoob previously told BBC Scotland News he felt too afraid to leave his home or return to work after the incident.
He had just picked up an order from the Palm Tree Kitchen on Bridge Street in Glasgow on the Saturday afternoon when he encountered dozens of protestors.
Yaqoob, who moved to Glasgow from Pakistan, told the BBC he has mostly found Scotland to be a welcoming place - but that his recent experience had "not been welcoming at all".
'Not welcoming at all'
The video of the attack shows a number of young men shouting abuse before one throws the orange cone. They cheer as Yaquoob runs away from them into a nearby restaurant.
He previously told the BBC: "When I crossed the road away from the crowd a man shouted, 'you brownie, you Asian, you Pakistani' and other racial abuse at me.
"One guy then tried to hit me with a traffic cone. So I ran around the back of the shop then Uber sent me a message asking me to complete my delivery.
"Uber didn't know what had happened to me so I completed my delivery then returned to the shop and said I was going to report it to the police and asked for the CCTV footage."
Yaqoob said the restaurant did not have CCTV but he reported the incident anyway.
He said when he arrived home and went online he discovered the video of the incident had spread on social media, as far as his home country.
"Now I am so scared, I am upset," he said.
"I haven't been able to go back to my work since the incident. I am fearful it will happen again but I have bills to pay so I can't just sit at home."

title: Australia PM under fire for remarks on Japanese counterpart's melon gifts
summary: An ex-Japanese envoy said the "sexist" comments "betrayed the close bond" between the countries.
full_text:
Australia PM under fire for remarks on Japanese counterpart's melon gifts
- Published
Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is under fire for comments he made about two melons gifted to him by his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi, after a former Japanese envoy called it an insult.
During an appearance on the Bush Deep podcast, Albanese gestured near his chest while referring to the crown melons, calling them "pretty strange" gifts that "ended up being quite good".
That episode, which aired in July, had already landed the PM in hot water because of "inappropriate" comments he made about popstar Kylie Minogue.
Opposition leaders are now demanding he apologise to Takaichi, but Albanese's position is that it was the host who made the joke, not him, the BBC understands.
While discussing the melons Takaichi's team had presented to Albanese during her visit to Australia in May, the host of Bush Deep, comedian Nikki Osborne, quipped: "She brought two... She just came in looking like Pamela Anderson."
"She brought two, and they are beautiful," Albanese responded.
The exchange, which drew relatively little interest when the episode aired, has resurfaced after Tokyo's former ambassador to Canberra Shingo Yamagami labelled Albanese's comments a "sexist joke" and said they "betrayed the close bond" between Japan and Australia.
"The last thing [Takaichi] expected was to be so casually mocked by the trusted leader of Japan's special strategic partner," he wrote in an opinion piece published by The Australian on Monday.
Crown melons are the "most prized fruit" in Japan and "treasured as something special", Yamagami added, noting that a single melon costs more than 30,000 yen ($188).
"So, prime minister, please enjoy Japan's sweet and juicy melons without thinking about a woman's anatomy, and instead focus on what our two countries must do together," he said.
During his two-year stint in Australia, Yamagami had a notably frosty relationship with some members of Albanese's Labor Party over disagreements regarding China.
An opposition MP asked Albanese on Tuesday if he would apologise for the "foul-mouthed, classless comments about women", to which the prime minister said he "rejected the assertion of the question".
He went on: "Australia and Japan have never been closer. My government has taken our special strategic partnership to new heights."
Australia's opposition leader Angus Taylor on Monday also criticised the gaffe as "insulting", and demanded that Albanese make a personal apology.
Several Labor ministers have jumped to Albanese's defence, saying the former envoy and the media have misinterpreted his comments.
Finance Minister Katy Gallagher said the remarks "were not intended to be interpreted the way that our political opponents and some media outlets are reporting".
Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek called it "a completely unnecessary interpretation of what the prime minister said".
"I think people watching it for themselves can make their own minds up," Plibersek told Australia's Channel Seven.
Plibersek had earlier defended Albanese's controversial remarks about Minogue as nothing more than a sign that he was a fan.
The prime minister drew a wave of condemnation early last month after Osborne asked him on the podcast whether he would "shag, marry or date" Kylie Minogue, actress Nicole Kidman or entertainer Rhonda Burchmore, to which he replied "Kylie, clearly... all of the above".
Albanese later issued a public apology, saying: "I apologise unequivocally for the comments".
Osborne, who is best known for posting crude comedy sketches on YouTube, launched her podcast series earlier this year. Her podcast site describes her as a "wildly inappropriate journalist" who asks "questions no one else would dare".

title: London Heathrow no longer Europe's busiest airport
summary: Istanbul overtakes Heathrow whose passenger numbers on Middle East routes fell 20.2% year-on-year.
full_text:
London Heathrow no longer Europe's busiest airport
- Published
Heathrow has lost its position as Europe's busiest airport to Istanbul, new figures show.
The west London airport said 7.86m passengers passed through its four terminals in July, whereas its Turkish counterpart recorded 8.15m passengers.
The US-Israel conflict with Iran has had an impact on Heathrow's passenger traffic with Middle East routes in July down 20.2% year-on-year.
Annual figures from trade body Airports Council International show Heathrow was Europe's busiest airport from 1996 to 2019. It lost that title in 2020 amid coronavirus travel restrictions before regaining it in 2023, holding it ever since.
Heathrow continues to operate its two runways at near-full capacity and is seeking government permission to build a third.
- Heathrow Airport sees 1.8% fall in June passengers 
  - Published13 July
- Heathrow rail services disrupted as tunnel closes 
  - Published22 hours ago
An expansion proposal by the airport's owners would enable it to accommodate 150m passengers per year. Heathrow said "the case for expansion has never been clearer".
In a statement, it added: "Our plans will ensure the country gets the infrastructure it needs to stay competitive and will deliver all-important economic growth."
The airport recorded 84.46 million passengers in 2025 and said 19 July was its busiest day of the year so far as many schools broke up for summer, with 267,000 passengers passing through.
It added that several new airlines began serving the airport last month, which demonstrates "clear demand for access to Heathrow".
Last month, it was revealed Heathrow will be allowed to charge airlines more for its services to recover money spent on the early stages of its third runway project.

title: How a murder case fuelled a culture war
summary: How Luigi Mangione's case became a battleground in America's culture wars
full_text:
Episode details
Available for over a year
Since the shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, the case against Luigi Mangione has become about more than just the evidence that will be tested in court. Across politics, social media and the news media, competing groups have sought to frame the story through their own lens, linking it to debates about left-wing violence, Antifa, healthcare, political extremism and public anger at powerful institutions. In this episode, BBC journalist and extremism expert Mike Wendling helps untangle the claims, examining what terms such as "far left" and "Antifa" actually mean, why some commentators have associated them with the case, and what evidence exists about Mangione's political views. The episode also explores how a high-profile criminal case can become a political symbol, even when the facts are disputed and a trial has yet to take place. Host Jordan Dunbar also looks at parallels from Japan following the assassination of former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, asking how public reactions to shocking acts of violence can evolve into wider debates about social grievances, political division and systemic change. Luigi Mangione denies all charges against him. So how did a murder case become a culture war, and what happens when politics starts shaping the story before a jury hears the evidence?

title: Rescue efforts intensify as quake devastates western Colombia towns
summary: Rescue teams rush to find survivors as western Colombia grapples with deadly earthquake devastation.
full_text:
In Pictures
Rescue efforts intensify as quake devastates western Colombia towns
Rescue teams rush to find survivors as western Colombia grapples with deadly earthquake devastation.
Search and rescue teams are racing against time across western Colombia after a powerful earthquake killed at least 132 people and left thousands missing, authorities say.
The magnitude 7.4 quake struck on Monday, rattling Cali, Quibdo, Pereira and dozens of other cities and towns. About 1,600 buildings have been reported damaged or collapsed, with soldiers, emergency crews and residents working side by side, passing chunks of concrete by hand as they search for survivors under the rubble.
Families are posting details of missing relatives on citizen-run websites; by Monday night more than 2,700 people had been reported missing. In El Cairo, near the epicentre in San Jose del Palmar, local officials say 80 percent of the town, home to about 7,000 people, has been damaged. Many of its traditional houses, made of sticks and mud, crumpled in the tremors.
President Abelardo de la Espriella, facing his first major crisis since taking office on Friday, has deployed “the entire military and police apparatus”, sending engineers, rescue teams and search dogs into the worst-hit areas. The US has pledged $15.5m in emergency aid, as regional governments also offer support to one of Colombia’s poorest and most isolated regions.

title: Swiatek to face Svitolina in Canadian Open semifinal
summary: Former world no 1 Iga Swiatek cruised past Diana Shnaider to set up a clash with Elina Svitolina in Toronto.
full_text:
Swiatek to face Svitolina in Canadian Open semifinal
Former world no 1 Iga Swiatek cruised past Diana Shnaider to set up a clash with Elina Svitolina in Toronto.
Iga Swiatek swept past Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 on Monday to reach the Canadian Open semifinals, where the Pole will face Elina Svitolina after the Ukrainian rallied past Ekaterina Alexandrova in Toronto.
It was a confidence-boosting display ahead of the US Open for former world number one Swiatek, who won one of her six Grand Slam titles at Flushing Meadows in 2022.
