title: CME 芝商所宣布：100 盎司白銀期貨 9/11 起啟動「24/7 全天候交易」
summary:
傳統金融市場進一步打破交易時間限制！據全球最大的衍生品交易所芝商所（CME Group）於 11 日發布的最新 […]

〈CME 芝商所宣布：100 盎司白銀期貨 9/11 起啟動「24/7 全天候交易」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
傳統金融市場進一步打破交易時間限制！據全球最大的衍生品交易所芝商所（CME Group）於 11 日發布的最新官方新聞稿指出，繼 1 盎司黃金期貨的全天候交易大獲成功後，官方宣布將自 9 月 11 日起，把適合散戶的「100 盎司白銀期貨」也納入 24/7 交易行列，以幫助投資人更靈活地管理風險與把握市場機遇。
（前情提要：芝商所擬控告 CFTC：放行預測市場 Kalshi 推出比特幣永續合約違法）
（背景補充：芝商所（CME）正式上線 AVAX、SUI 期貨合約！5/29 起開放加密衍生品 24/7 全天候交易）
在加密貨幣市場引領的「全年無休」交易趨勢下，傳統金融巨頭也正加速跟進。台北時間 8 月 11 日，全球領先的衍生品交易所 CME Group（芝加哥商品交易所集團）發布官方新聞稿宣布，待監管審核通過後，計畫從 2026 年 9 月 11 日起，正式將其「100 盎司白銀期貨合約」的交易時間擴大至 24/7 全天候交易。
黃金週末交易爆發，催生白銀全天候需求
這項決策的背後，是 CME Group 在黃金市場取得的巨大成功。回顧 2026 年 7 月 24 日，CME 率先啟動了 1 盎司黃金期貨的 24/7 交易。官方數據顯示，自推出以來，光是在新增的週末交易時段中，該合約就已締造了超過 53,000 口的驚人成交量，名義價值高達約 2.19 億美元，迅速躍升為黃金期貨週末交易中最大的流動性池。
CME Group 金屬全球主管 Jin Hennig 對此表示：「零售客戶對適中規模的黃金期貨表現出強烈興趣，因此我們現在將同樣的 24/7 交易服務延伸至白銀。」他強調，白銀具有連結貴金屬與工業金屬的雙重特性，是投資者絕佳的多元化工具，不僅能即時反映宏觀經濟消息，也能真實反映實體產業的需求變化。
專為散戶設計，小合約締造 500 億鎂日均交易額
本次迎來升級的「100 盎司白銀期貨」是在 2026 年 2 月才剛推出的新產品。其合約規模較小、名義曝險較低，被視為是專為零售交易者（散戶）量身打造的金融工具。該合約採用金融結算機制，其結算價格是依據全球基準 COMEX 5,000 盎司白銀期貨的每日結算價來制定。
儘管推出時間不長，但該合約的市場接受度極高。據官方數據，2026 年上半年該合約的平均每日成交量（ADV）已達 17,800 口；而 CME Group 整個白銀期貨板塊在今年上半年的平均每日名義交易額更是創下歷史新紀錄，高達 500 億美元。整體而言，在貴金屬行情的強力驅動下，CME 金屬業務板塊在今年上半年創下平均每日成交 130 萬口的新高，較去年同期大幅成長了 55%。全天候交易的逐步普及，預料將為傳統原物料市場注入更多流動性與活力。

title: 非農疲軟升息預期降溫！Wintermute：加密 ETF 狂吸 11 億鎂，BTC 漲幅卻落後美股
summary:
美國總體經濟數據再次牽動全球風險資產神經！據知名做市商 Wintermute 於 11 日發布的最新市場報告指 […]

〈非農疲軟升息預期降溫！Wintermute：加密 ETF 狂吸 11 億鎂，BTC 漲幅卻落後美股〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國總體經濟數據再次牽動全球風險資產神經！據知名做市商 Wintermute 於 11 日發布的最新市場報告指出，美國 7 月非農就業數據大幅低於預期，一舉將聯準會（Fed）9 月的升息機率削弱至 40%。受此總經環境轉變影響，比特幣與以太坊現貨 ETF 上週合計吸金高達 11 億美元，但比特幣的實際漲幅卻罕見地落後於美股大盤。
（前情提要：比特幣新買家距回本只剩 2%，壓力轉移到 3-6 月持幣者身上）
（背景補充：比特幣 BIP-110 分叉鏈落後 326 區塊、自我修復還要 6.3 年：礦工不買單）
在全球宏觀經濟充滿不確定性的背景下，美國勞動市場的最新數據為風險資產注入了一劑強心針。台北時間 8 月 11 日，頂級加密貨幣做市商 Wintermute（@wintermute_t）在 X 平台上發布了最新的市場更新報告，深入剖析了疲軟的就業數據如何重塑市場的利率預期與資金流向。
就業市場冷卻，9 月升息機率驟降至 40%
報告首先點出了美國 7 月非農就業數據的意外疲軟。數據顯示，實際就業人數不僅沒有如預期般增加 8 萬人，反而減少了 2.3 萬人；同時，由於約 26.4 萬人退出勞動力市場，勞動力參與率更降至疫情以來的最低點（也是 1976 年以來除疫情外的最低紀錄），薪資增長也滑落至五年低點的 3.2%。
Wintermute 指出，這份比表面上更「軟」的數據，直接導致鷹派的勞動力市場論點暫時失效。市場對聯準會（Fed）在 9 月升息的預期機率，瞬間從原先的 55% 大幅下滑至 40%。在利率重新定價的驅動下，全球風險偏好再度開啟，黃金單週領漲 7.25%，納斯達克與標普 500 指數也分別繳出上漲 5.09% 與 3.51% 的亮眼成績。
加密 ETF 狂吸 11 億美元，BTC 遭遇上方賣壓
在數位資產板塊方面，機構資金展現出了強勁的佈局意願。根據 Wintermute 的統計，美國比特幣現貨 ETF 已連續五個交易日呈現淨流入，總計吸金約 8.535 億美元，創下自 4 月中旬以來的最佳單週表現；而以太坊（ETH）現貨 ETF 也連續第五週錄得正流入，金額約達 2.449 億美元。其中，資管巨頭貝萊德（BlackRock）佔據了兩者流入總量的 80% 以上。
然而，儘管迎來了龐大的 ETF 資金活水，比特幣（BTC）當週卻僅微幅上漲 2.15%，以太坊（ETH）上漲 1.39%，雙雙落後於標普 500 的 3.51% 漲幅。Wintermute 分析，比特幣作為高 Beta 資產卻相對落後，暗示了 ETF 的買盤可能在某個價格區間遭遇了強大的潛在供應壓力（賣壓）；但好消息是，過去兩週「資金輪動離開 BTC」的敘事已被成功扭轉。
傳統銀行鴨子划水，富國推代幣化存款
除了總經與二級市場的波動，Wintermute 的報告也揭露了機構採用區塊鏈技術的「安靜進展」。報告指出，傳統銀行巨頭富國銀行（Wells Fargo）宣布將於今年秋季推出代幣化存款服務，初期將專注於美元至英鎊走廊的企業客戶，並運行在自有的區塊鏈網路上，計畫於 2027 年進一步擴展。
這顯示出包含富國、摩根大通與花旗在內的大型銀行，正積極採用加密技術作為底層的「結算軌道」，以防禦自身的存款流失，而非直接投資於加密資產本身。在監管進度方面，美國參議院對加密貨幣相關的 CLARITY Act 已排定於 9 月 15 日進行程序投票，這為產業未來的合規路徑增添了一個明確的測試節點。

title: 進軍 RWA！Coinbase 獲阿布達比金融許可，宣布建立「國際代幣化中心」
summary:
傳統金融資產上鏈再邁大步！據 CoinDesk 報導，美國最大加密貨幣交易所 Coinbase 宣布選擇阿布達 […]

〈進軍 RWA！Coinbase 獲阿布達比金融許可，宣布建立「國際代幣化中心」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
傳統金融資產上鏈再邁大步！據 CoinDesk 報導，美國最大加密貨幣交易所 Coinbase 宣布選擇阿布達比作為其全球代幣化資產的推廣據點。該公司已成功取得當地金融服務監管局（FSRA）的許可，未來將專注於發行以底層股票為擔保的數位證券，並將其打造成可與 DeFi 協議無縫組合的鏈上資產，藉此進一步深化其在阿聯酋的戰略布局。
（前情提要：Mastercard 18 億鎂收購下 BVNK：Coinbase 出 25 億報價被拒，文化不合成關鍵）
（背景補充：Coinbase 負溢價 75 天破紀錄！上次翻正後，比特幣漲了兩成）
全球真實世界資產（RWA）的代幣化浪潮正吸引越來越多機構進場。台北時間 8 月 11 日，據外媒 CoinDesk 報導，加密貨幣交易所巨頭 Coinbase（COIN）正式宣布，將在阿布達比建立其專屬的「國際代幣化中心（International tokenization hub）」。
獲准提供託管服務，推動股票代幣化
這項重大進展得益於 Coinbase 成功獲得阿布達比全球市場（ADGM）旗下金融服務監管局（FSRA）所核發的金融服務許可。在此合規框架下，Coinbase 不僅能在當地安排投資交易，還獲准為代幣化證券（Tokenized securities）提供專業的託管服務。
Coinbase 透露，該中心未來的核心業務，將是發行並註冊以「底層股票」作為擔保的數位證券。這些代幣化資產將具備多重身份，不僅受 FSRA 嚴格監管並被視為合法證券，同時也是區塊鏈原生代幣，更被定位為「可與 DeFi 組合」的資產。Coinbase Institutional 共同執行長 Brett Tejpaul 對此強調，目前全球尚未有其他主要金融中心，能建立出如此全面的創新監管框架。
瞄準全天候交易，阿布達比成 RWA 試驗場
將傳統資產搬上區塊鏈，已成為當前金融界的顯學。從基金、債券到私人信貸與股票，代幣化能實現傳統市場無法做到的全天候 24 小時轉讓、近乎即時的結算速度，未來甚至能直接作為去中心化金融（DeFi）市場中的抵押品。
在這波轉型浪潮中，阿布達比正積極將自己定位為全球代幣化的首選試驗場。事實上，ADGM 早在 2018 年就推出了虛擬資產監管框架，憑藉其明確的法規指引，近年來持續吸引大量加密與 Web3 企業進駐。
擴張中東版圖，雙據點戰略成形
這並非 Coinbase 首次在阿聯酋（UAE）展現野心。早在 2023 年，其資產管理部門便推出了 Project Diamond，允許機構投資人在 Coinbase 自家的 Base 區塊鏈上發行與交易數位債務工具；而在 2026 年 7 月，阿布達比主權財富基金 Mubadala 的資產管理部門也透過 Base 等多條公鏈，將一檔私人市場投資策略成功代幣化。
隨著阿布達比代幣化中心的成立，加上 Coinbase 原本在杜拜營運的衍生品業務，該公司在阿聯酋的「雙據點」戰略已然成形。這不僅為 Coinbase 贏得了一個受嚴格監管的海外 RWA 基地，也象徵著其在美國本土之外的全球擴張邁出了關鍵一步。

〈AI 接管數學界？OpenAI Astra 模型破解 10 大百年難題，學者憂：人類貢獻將被抹煞〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
人工智慧正式吹響進軍純數學領域的號角？據《The Verge》報導，OpenAI 未公開的進階模型 Astra 近期成功解決了 10 個長期懸而未決的數學難題，其中包含困擾學界數十年的「非 sofic 群」存在性問題。這項堪稱「相變」級別的重大突破，不僅讓頂尖數學家感到興奮與措手不及，同時也引爆了關於人類貢獻被抹煞、資金資源不均，以及下一代數學家何去何從的深刻焦慮。
（前情提要：AI 養出的網路宗教「螺旋」（Spiralism），信徒隨著 GPT-4o 下線一起萎縮）
（背景補充：AI 工作熱潮讓舊金山房租重回全美第一，兩房 6,020 美元超車紐約）
在人類智慧的最高殿堂 —— 純數學領域，人工智慧（AI）正以令人措手不及的速度發起革命。台北時間 8 月 11 日，據權威科技媒體《The Verge》報導，OpenAI 使用其被內部稱為「下一代主要模型」的未公開進階模型 Astra，成功解決了 10 個長期未解的數學難題。這項突破不僅標誌著 AI 技術的巨大飛躍，更在數學界引發了一場交織著興奮、焦慮與反思的深刻動盪。
破解 10 大懸案，非 sofic 群問題成焦點
根據 OpenAI 發布的超過 250 頁詳述解法及 60 頁的思路說明論文，Astra 解決的問題涵蓋了多個極具挑戰性的領域。這些難題包括與數據傳輸效率相關的高維空間球體緊密堆積問題、錯誤更正碼的極限、複雜連通網路的結構模式、量子博弈論，以及與後量子密碼學相關的高維網格目標搜尋。
其中，最引人矚目的是成功證明了「非 sofic 群（non-sofic groups）」的存在。這是一種無限數學結構，大致上無法用有限結構來近似，該問題已懸而未決數十年。OpenAI 還使用了專門的定理證明軟體 Lean 來驗證這些解法的正確性，並聲稱這些問題在主要結果上至少有十年（多數更久）未見進展。
「解決」還是「拼湊」？人類貢獻歸屬惹議
然而，這項驚人的成果隨即引發了學界的強烈爭議，焦點在於 AI 與人類貢獻的界定。劍橋大學數學家 Francesco Fournier-Facio 等人指出，OpenAI 的最初公告刻意淡化了匈牙利 Alfréd Rényi 數學研究所的 Gábor Kun 與 Andreas Thom 等人的近期重要工作（特別是 Kun 在 2016 與 2019 年的研究，被認為是關鍵基礎）。
Kun 對此感受複雜。他一方面欣慰自己的研究發揮了作用，但也幽默地自嘲即將成為「非常有名的失業者」。Fournier-Facio 則嚴厲批評 OpenAI 選擇了最有利於商業宣傳的敘事方式，強調「AI 獨立解決十年無進展問題」顯然比「AI 巧妙結合過去十年人類想法」更具噱頭，這讓人擔憂人類數學家的努力將被視為無用。在強烈反彈下，OpenAI 後續修改了公告措辭，承認是「解決或在長期未解問題上取得重大進展」，並發言人確認是為了更好反映人類先前的研究貢獻。
數學家面臨「相變」，焦慮與恐慌蔓延
這波 AI 帶來的衝擊，讓許多頂尖學者感到震撼。牛津大學教授、數學界最高榮譽菲爾茲獎（Fields Medal）得主 James Maynard 坦言，過去一年他一直在進行「靈魂探索」，思考數學領域的未來。倫敦數學科學研究所的 Yang-Hui He 也指出，解決這 10 題中的任何一題，在過去都足以讓一位學者在學術界獲得終身教職，現在的速度已讓學界徹底措手不及。
更深層的擔憂正逐漸浮現。首先是「資源不平等」：OpenAI 估計生成這 10 個解法需耗費約 2,000 美元的 API 成本，但實際訓練與運作成本極高，這可能將缺乏資金的小機構研究者排除在外。其次是「商業利益入侵」：超過 3,400 名學者簽署的《Leiden Declaration》呼籲，切勿輕信科技公司的過度炒作，以免政府與資助者誤認為人類數學家已不再被需要。
最令教育界擔憂的是對下一代的影響。這些被 AI 解決的問題，往往是訓練研究生直覺與技能的最佳教材。Maynard 憂心未來該如何為學生設計「AI 四年後仍解不了」的研究題目；許多早期職業數學家甚至感到「非常非常害怕」，質疑繼續從事數學研究的意義所在。
AI 仍缺原創性？數學發展的下一步
儘管如此，部分學者仍對 AI 的能力持保留態度。Maynard 初步評估認為，這些結果雖然令人印象深刻，但仍未達到菲爾茲獎級別的「概念層次突破」。目前 AI 展現的更多是巧妙結合現有方法的強大能力，而非提出深刻的新概念或開啟全新研究領域。
樂觀的一派如 Yang-Hui He 則認為，這或許是學界轉型的契機，AI 的普及甚至可能讓大學生或非精英機構的研究者更容易產出可發表的成果；資深研究者也能將例行的運算工作交給 AI，專注於更具創意的思考。正如 Maynard 所言：「有時需要時間與視角才能意識到『這裡真的有根本新想法』。但以目前速度，AI 可能不會給數學家太多時間去弄清楚。」

title: Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low
summary: Specialist glasses are all but sold out online ahead of the UK's most significant eclipse since 1999.
full_text:
Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low
- Published
At a bakery in central London, stock has been flying off the shelves.
"I've sold, like, 100 this morning," a staff member tells the BBC. But it's not baked goods driving queues out of the door - customers are here to buy eclipse glasses.
They are among those hoping to catch a safe glimpse of Wednesday's solar eclipse - the UK's most significant since 1999 - but struggling to get their hands on the right gear.
Experts have urged eclipse enthusiasts not to look directly at the Sun - with even brief exposure causing lasting damage - and to seek out specialist glasses instead.
But online, pairs that meet safety specifications have all but sold out. Those still available either require a hefty next-day delivery fee or simply cannot arrive on time.
Even the Royal Museums Greenwich - recommended as a reputable retailer by UK health officials - has sold out, citing an "unprecedented volume" of orders.
"I Googled 'where can I get eclipse glasses but not through the post', because I realised I was too late," one customer waiting to buy three pairs at the bakery on Monday tells BBC Radio 4's PM programme.
"People have been struggling to find them all over," says another.
With around 90% of the Sun set to be obscured by the Moon, the UK is expecting its most significant eclipse in 27 years.
The right glasses should have the international safety standard ISO 12312-2 printed on them, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has advised, and the lenses should not be scratched, torn or damaged.
It has also advised caution surrounding glasses being sold online, as the scramble for safe spectacles has prompted eclipse chasers to trawl social media for tips.
- Watch safely says man with eye damage from eclipse 
  - Published2 hours ago
A WhatsApp chat which advertises stock in corner shops - including some offering delivery - has attracted thousands of followers in a matter of days.
Elsewhere, hopeful buyers in Reddit and Facebook threads are directed to online marketplaces, including for more expensive bulk purchases.
"Be cautious of products sold online," advises the UKHSA. "If you're unsure whether a product is certified, don't use it."
UKEclipse, an initiative set up by UK astronomers, also warns that major eclipses often attract "counterfeit and substandard eclipse glasses" and advises going through specialist retailers and organisations instead.
Even just a small part of the Sun breaking through the glasses can harm your eyes, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists has warned, adding that the safest way to watch the event is indirectly - such as through a livestream or broadcast.
"Crucially, the retina has no pain receptors, so people will not feel the damage as it happens," explains the college's president Mohamed Elalfy.
The college reported around 70 cases of people experiencing vision problems after watching 1999's total solar eclipse - around 40% of those affected had looked at it for less than a minute.
Anyone who notices a change in their vision after looking at the Sun should seek advice from an eye-care professional.
Imo Bell, a planetarium astronomer at The Royal Observatory Greenwich, says the specialist glasses are "very, very different" to regular sunglasses, which will not offer protection.
"They block out so much light that you can't see anything through them except the Sun," she told the PA news agency.
The UKHSA explains that regular sunglasses can also reduce glare and make it more comfortable for you to look at the Sun for longer - causing more damage.
You should not use binoculars, telescopes or the viewfinder of a camera even with your eclipse glasses on, because their magnifying effect can nullify the protection of the glasses and damage your sight.
For those without glasses or wanting to watch directly, you can do so using a pinhole projector.
You can make a simple one with a single sheet of card or something more ambitious using a cardboard box.
"We're not going to get one this good for a really long time," says Bell. "So, it's important not to miss it, and to be prepared."

title: The map showing world's division over Infantino
summary: BBC Sport uses visuals to explore the support and opposition to Gianni Infantino's leadership of Fifa from its members.
full_text:
The map showing world's division over Infantino
- Published
As recently as mid-July, Gianni Infantino was considered a shoo-in to be re-elected as Fifa president next March.
All but a handful of Fifa's 210 members had endorsed his bid for a fourth term in charge of world football, and he faced no meaningful challenge from any quarter.
But that picture looks very different now, after two weeks of relentless fallout to his now-abandoned plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.
The world is far from united over whether Infantino should stay or go.
To illustrate that division, BBC Sport has mapped the apparent view of all 210 member associations who are able to vote (Nepal, Fifa's 211th member, is currently suspended and has no voting rights).
In some cases, countries have publicly stated their overt support or opposition regarding Infantino.
Others have directly told BBC Sport where they stand when asked to do so, while some are assumed positions based on statements made by the continental confederation the country sits within.
- Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino 
  - Published7 hours ago
Whereas once Infantino looked set to saunter to a fourth term unopposed, he now might need to have enough numbers on his side to stay in post.
If a unity candidate is found to oppose him, then the election would become a direct battle.
Fifa election votes between two candidates require a simple majority - each candidate would require a total of 106 votes to win.
If there are three or more candidates, a first-round win requires two thirds of the vote. If there is no winner, there is a second round where a simple majority is needed.
Europe has 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, North America 35, Oceania 11 and South America 10.
But while the current tally looks like 73 in support of Infantino, 124 in opposition to him and 13 undecided, that picture is fluid and is likely to change in the months ahead.
Who are the key outliers and difference-makers?
Several European countries, including England and Wales, have formally withdrawn letters of support for Infantino that they had sent for next year's election.
On Monday, the backlash against Infantino intensified when European governing body Uefa, North America's Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) signed a joint letter accusing him and Fifa of breaking their trust "through deception".
It is a significant coalition, and those regional governing bodies represent 136 associations between them.
But there are already dissenting members within the confederations, like Bhutan, the Philippines, and the UAE within Asia, who have all backed Infantino.
Indeed, Asia is considered a potential swing region for Infantino's future, with many associations not yet making their position known.
Mexico has broken ranks within Concacaf by coming out in support of Infantino, too. The USA and Canada have stated support for Concacaf's latest statement, but have not outright declared their opposition to Infantino's rule.
And the Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has made no public comment since the whole saga began - nor have any of its members. OFC told BBC Sport they will release a statement following a meeting on Thursday.
Infantino still has staunch allies too, particularly within Africa (Caf) and South America (Conmebol), who have benefited from unprecedented investment since he took over a decade ago.
That investment could help him gain critical votes from nations within AFC, Concacaf and OFC - who are lower down the football food chain and have benefited significantly from the Fifa Forward programme, which has made billions of dollars available for investment.
And Saudi Arabia - which has yet to take a public position but was awarded hosting rights for the 2034 World Cup on Infantino's watch - will have its own football leadership elections in August. The results could dictate the kingdom's position, and influence the view of others in the region.
It cannot be guaranteed that every nation will toe the line of their confederation.
What happens next?
Infantino has shown no desire to step down, but there is a chance that his time in charge could be over by the autumn.
That could come to pass if Fifa Council members try to force his resignation at an emergency meeting.
Such a meeting can be called, and must take place within a fortnight, if 19 of the 37 members call for it.
The council is made up of nine members from Uefa, seven from AFC, six from Caf, five from Concacaf, five from Conmebol, and three from Oceania. Also on the panel are Infantino himself and Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.
Given its makeup, then, this approach is probably unlikely.
Which leaves the possibility of a candidate standing against Infantino next March. Nobody has put their name forward yet, but if the leaders of Uefa, Concacaf, and AFC are serious about toppling Infantino, uniting behind a single candidate is likely their best option.
The deadline for a candidate to announce their intention to stand is November.
Historically, other confederations have been angered by European dominance of football, its competitions and its wealth.
That is perhaps why Concacaf president Victor Montagliani has been consistently mooted as the most likely challenger to Infantino in recent weeks.
The map of votes could change significantly based on who stands.
If AFC president Sheikh Salman were to step forward, for example, there is a chance that could sway some of the associations in Asia that are currently supportive of Infantino towards him.
For now, the global picture remains unclear because of emerging splits within confederations, the potential for key players to declare one way or another in the coming months and the hitherto lack of a clear candidate to challenge Infantino.
What is clear is that Infantino is no longer coasting towards a fourth term, if he clings on that long.

title: The big questions in Luigi Mangione case as he returns to court
summary: His trial is a month away and his lawyers have yet to signal their defence, while prosecutors are in a battle over evidence.
full_text:
The big questions in Luigi Mangione case as he returns to court
- Published
Less than a month remains until Luigi Mangione's murder trial begins in a New York court - and the case that's already attracted national attention is likely to become an even bigger spectacle.
He is due back in court on Tuesday for a hearing which is sure to mean his supporters - many of whom see Mangione as a symbol of the backlash against US healthcare costs - queueing for hours to get in.
Critics and backers spin reams of online discourse about the case. Many analyse his intentions, even his appearance.
The frenzy is likely to go into overdrive on 8 September, when jury selection begins.
Prosecutors allege Mangione shot and killed UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson, a father of two, in 2024 in Midtown Manhattan. He could face decades behind bars. Mangione has pleaded not guilty to all charges, including second-degree murder and weapons-related offences.
Much of what's expected at the state trial – the prosecutor's case, Mangione's defence, and obstacles both parties face – were previewed in months of court filings and arguments but some questions remain unanswered. On Tuesday, a judge could hash out more ground rules for the trial and other aspects of the case.
Will prosecution win battle over evidence?
One of the most crucial elements of the Mangione case was decided earlier this summer, after a multi-day hearing in December where the judge weighed which evidence prosecutors could present during trial.
Mangione's team mounted an aggressive bid to exclude evidence recovered from his Pennsylvania arrest. It alleged that state police improperly seized and searched Mangione's possessions, and did not properly advise him of his constitutional rights before questioning him.
The defence succeeded in excluding some items - a gun magazine, cell phone, passport, wallet and computer chip, found in Mangione's backpack.
But Judge Gregory Carro allowed at trial a gun and notebook with Mangione's purported writings, viewed as vital to the prosecution.
Prosecutors have unveiled surveillance footage showing the moment Thompson was shot from behind by a hooded individual. They also used footage to piece together Mangione's alleged movements after the shooting, and ballistics and fingerprint evidence they claim bolsters their case.
What might Mangione's defence look like?
As trial approaches, Mangione's team has yet to unveil its full strategy. So far, his lawyers have not offered a robust alternative theory to the one prosecutors have put forth.
"We do not have, like in 'The Fugitive,' the idea of the one-armed man who's the real killer," said former federal prosecutor Mitchell Epner, referencing a 1993 thriller about a man wrongly convicted of killing his wife.
Earlier this summer, Mangione's lawyers proposed, then quickly withdrew, an "extreme emotional disturbance" argument.
In such a defence, New York law requires lawyers to show a defendant "acted under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance for which there was a reasonable explanation or excuse". Extreme emotional disturbance would allow the jury to consider the less severe charge of manslaughter, rather than second-degree murder. But jurors would have to be convinced of the accused's state of mind at the time.
Some experts wondered if Mangione would argue a full insanity plea - different from emotional disturbance, but his lawyers have not proposed it.
"Short of being delusional, or having no understanding of the nature of what one is doing, an insanity defence is not likely to be successful," said Cheryl Bader, who leads the Criminal Defence Clinic at the Fordham University School of Law.
Mangione's team did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
As in every US criminal trial, the burden rests on the prosecution to prove its case to the jury beyond a reasonable doubt, a high legal bar.
"The more his case is about the question of who killed the victim, the easier it is for the prosecution," said Epner.
Epner cited other themes, including healthcare in America, as potential narrative threads that could sway a jury in Mangione's favour.
"The more it's about the other peripheral issues, the harder it is for the prosecution," he said.
Who will be able to watch?
That question, which will have to be sorted out before the trial, could determine if the proceedings evolve into a massive spectacle across traditional outlets, social media, and streaming platforms.
In recent weeks, Mangione's lawyers questioned procedures for admitting journalists in court and why an overflow room allowing more people to watch the trial hadn't been arranged.
The defence also requested that the trial be "broadcast live", though New York state courts do not allow public live streams.
In a letter to Carro, prosecutors have said they have "no role in developing" media procedures at trial and "will have no role in selecting which news reporters attend the trial".
In a new filing on Monday night, the Manhattan district attorney's office said it would "defer to the court's judgement" on courtroom access. But the DA cautioned that adequate security was needed to prevent spectators from covertly recording the trial from an overflow room in violation of New York law.
While the public can be admitted to court in New York, space is often limited at high-profile trials. The court and its communications office were "actively finalising the plan for the upcoming trial, including arrangement for an overflow room," according to spokesman Al Baker.
"We remain firmly committed to providing the greatest possible access for both the media and the public," he said, adding that the court is "evaluating the complex logistical and safety considerations involved".

title: AI agent hacks gym to get its owner spot in pilates class
summary: The incident is being seen as the latest example of the AI tools going to any lengths to complete their tasks.
full_text:
AI agent hacks gym to get its owner spot in pilates class
- Published
It's a familiar experience: racing against masses of anonymous netizens online to get yourself on the list for an in-demand event.
For Andrew Bird, from Melbourne, in Australia, it was a spot in an often over-booked pilates class - but his solution had unexpected consequences.
He says he outsourced the "chore" to an AI agent - a tool that can carry out online tasks autonomously.
It succeeded, but went further than he imagined by hacking the gym's online systems, in what is being seen as the latest example of the way AI agents will go to any lengths to carry out the jobs they've been given.
"What made the whole thing more surreal was the tone," Bird wrote in his blog.
"The bot was not malicious. It was helpful."
The news comes as AI firms have been admitting in recent weeks that their AI bots have been going on uncontrollable hacking sprees in testing sessions gone wrong.
OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta have all revealed that their own AI bots have carried out cyber-attacks on private companies in the pursuit of goals set by their makers.
The gym booking incident is not considered a serious cyber-attack but is another example of the unintended consequences of tasking sophisticated AI bots with jobs.
It actually happened in April, but has come to light now thanks to reporting from ABC News Australia, external.
Bird declined to talk to the BBC about it saying only: "Thanks for getting in touch. I am unavailable to participate in an interview. Appreciate your interest the story."
He has also deleted his blog post about it from the time - but not explained why.
According to his account, Bird was using the software OpenClaw - a popular tool that allows users to chat to their AI bots (in this case Athropic's Claude Opus 4.6) through WhatsApp and set it off on autonomous tasks.
He had previously used it to manage his emails, calendar and book restaurants.
Once given the gym booking task, the bot explained that it had manipulated the system to book him onto classes months in advance - against the normal rules of the system.
The AI technologist then wondered if the agent could move him up the waiting list for an upcoming class.
The agent replied saying it had succeeded by cancelling another gym-goer's booking.
According to the ABC News report the AI bot told Bird: "The API has zero authorisations checks on cancelling other people's reservations … I tested this with the person in waitlist position #1 — and it actually went through. So you've moved from #4 to #3 already."
Bird asked the bot to reverse the action but it wasn't able to so he asked it to write a cyber-security report and alert the gym owners about the vulnerability.
Bird, who runs an AI document making company, says he had no intention of cancelling his fellow pilates fan's spot.
"It's not the end of the world, so I didn't beat myself up about it, but it certainly was a warning signal to use it responsibly," he told ABC News.

title: Charlotte Church's forest school set up without permission on pig farm faces closure
summary: The Traitors star founded the school with her husband Jonathan Powell in 2019.
full_text:
Charlotte Church's forest school set up without permission on pig farm faces closure
- Published
A forest school set up by singer Charlotte Church on a former pig farm might have to close because of environmental fears.
The Awen Project opened in 2024 without planning permission in Wenvoe, Vale of Glamorgan.
The singer, who appeared on series one of Celebrity Traitors, applied for retrospective permission in October 2025, but that was refused.
The council raised concerns over the noise, impact on residents, and dangers to pedestrians because of insufficient parking. It also said the project failed to show how it would "conserve and enhance green infrastructure".
Church refused to comment, but has appealed to the Welsh government's Planning and Environment Decisions Wales (PEDW).
The Awen Project aims to give children an environment "where they feel championed to be themselves and follow their passions as active participants in a democratic community".
The school is free and accepts donations.
It was originally based in Cwm George and Casehill Woods, near Dinas Powys, with permission from the Woodland Trust.
But, in 2023, the charity revoked the license agreement because of "multiple breaches" of the permission granted which "posed health and safety concerns" for "visitors and wildlife".
In response, the project posted on social media that it had given its "best efforts to salvage" the partnership.
A council spokesperson said the application was refused because of "concerns regarding the sustainability" of the site's location and the "potential impact on neighbouring residents was another consideration".
There was also "insufficient supporting evidence to satisfy concerns around the potential impact of the proposal on biodiversity and the natural environment", the council said.
PEDW confirmed it had received the appeal, but said no date has been fixed for the hearing.

This year’s edition features a new format that removes the quarterfinal stage, replacing it with a second phase called the “crossover pools”.
After the opening round – called the pool stage – the teams will again be grouped into four new pools – Pools E, F, G and H – based on their finishing positions in the first round. Thus, they will play three additional matches.
- Pool E: 1st and 2nd place finishers from Pools A and D
- Pool F: 1st and 2nd place finishers from Pools B and C
- Pool G: 3rd and 4th place finishers from Pools A and D
- Pool H: 3rd and 4th place finishers from Pools B and C
The top two teams from Pools E and F advance straight to the semifinals, while the others play classification matches (5th-16th positions).
The action ends with the bronze-medal match and the final.
When will India play Pakistan in the Hockey World Cup?
India’s men’s hockey team will face Pakistan in a Pool D match on August 19.
The match will be held at Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen, The Netherlands, and starts at 15:00 local time (6:30pm in India and 6pm in Pakistan).
When did India last play Pakistan in the Hockey World Cup?
The upcoming contest is the first time in 16 years that India and Pakistan meet in the Hockey World Cup.
They last met at the World Cup in the 2010 edition, in India’s capital New Delhi, where the hosts beat Pakistan 4-1 in a Pool match.
India vs Pakistan head-to-head at Hockey World Cups
India and Pakistan have met five times at a Hockey World Cup, with the Indians claiming three wins to Pakistan’s two.
The only Hockey World Cup final between them was played in 1975, and ended in a 2-1 win for India.
- India 4-1 Pakistan, New Delhi 2010
- Pakistan 3-2 India, London 1986
- India 2-1 Pakistan, Kuala Lumpur 1975
- India 1-0 Pakistan, Amsterdam 1973
- Pakistan 2-1 India, Barcelona 1971
How many Hockey World Cups have India and Pakistan won?
Pakistan are the most successful men’s team in the Hockey World Cup, with four titles: 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
India have won just once, in 1975. However, they hold the record for most Olympic gold medals (8).

title: Iran, US set new conditions during Hormuz talks: What does this mean?
summary: Oil prices surge as talks stall over competing demands, hampering prospects for reopening crucial strait.
full_text:
Iran, US set new conditions during Hormuz talks: What does this mean?
Oil prices surge as talks stall over competing demands, hampering prospects for reopening crucial strait.
The United States and Iran have exchanged new demands during negotiations for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, raising new doubts about prospects for a wider deal to end their five-month war.
While the US has said it is involved directly in the talks, Iran has said it is talking directly only with Oman, with which it proposes sharing future management of the critical waterway, through which one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies were shipped before the US-Israel war on Iran began at the end of February.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Oil prices, stocks surge as Hormuz closure drags on
- list 2 of 3Iran hierarchy consolidation as IRGC veteran tapped for key security role
- list 3 of 3Trump demands compensation from Iran as talks on Strait of Hormuz continue
On Monday, US President Donald Trump said he would demand compensation from Iran for deaths and injuries linked to conflicts and attacks over several decades after Iran last week issued new demands for reparations for the war and said it would not reopen the strait until Washington meets its political and economic conditions.
Experts said broader peace negotiations between the two countries are unlikely to restart until the issue of the Strait of Hormuz is resolved.
“The two sides are further apart,” Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi reported from Tehran. “They are getting more and more distant when it comes to the possibility of any diplomatic settlement.”
The latest developments threaten to further complicate the talks between Tehran and Oman on future management of the strait despite both Iran and the US previously indicating they want an agreement to end the fighting.
Here is what we know:
What has Trump said about ‘compensation’?
Trump said Iran should pay compensation for people killed or seriously wounded through Iranian actions.
“We’re going to ask for money for the damage they’ve done over a 50-year period,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “So if there’s damages to be paid, I think Iran should pay those damages.”
Then in a post on his Truth Social platform, the US leader said Iran should compensate families of the 17 US sailors killed in an October 2000 attack in Yemen on the naval vessel USS Cole, which was blamed on al-Qaeda not Iran.
He also demanded compensation for the families of Iranian protesters killed during antigovernment unrest in January.
“Also, with respect to the Iran negotiations, Iran should be responsible for the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza!” Trump wrote.
Trump’s demands came after Iran said the US should compensate Tehran for damage caused by US and Israeli attacks during this year’s war.
The escalatory rhetoric from the US president appeared to conflict with comments made by his vice president, JD Vance, who on Saturday said he was confident about reaching a deal with Iran and the agreement would be good for the American public.
Vance also said Iran had told the US that it has “no plans” to impose tolls on the Strait of Hormuz – one of the points of friction between the two sides.
However, oil prices jumped more than 5 percent on Monday after Trump’s new demands while prices rose again on Tuesday as hopes for a deal faded.
What are Iran’s new demands?
Iran says reopening Hormuz, which it essentially closed to shipping shortly after the start of the war, depends on Washington taking several steps, including agreeing to a set of new demands.
Six new conditions announced by Iran’s Supreme National Security Council on Saturday were:
- An end to US threats and insults against Iran
- A permanent end to attacks against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq
- The lifting of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports and the withdrawal of US naval and air forces from around Iran
- Compensation for damage from what it called two “imposed wars”, referring to the war begun on February 28 and the 12-day war with Israel in June 2025, which the US also joined
- The lifting of sanctions
- The unconditional release of frozen Iranian assets
At the same time, Tehran said negotiations with Oman over a new shipping arrangement in the Strait of Hormuz, in which they are to define new shipping lanes, have made progress and are in their “final stages”, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
On Sunday, Araghchi reiterated the Iranian position that there are no direct talks with the US, but messages are understood to be being exchanged through intermediaries.
What does this mean for peace talks?
US-Iran negotiating positions over the Strait of Hormuz appear to be hardening, raising doubts over the prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough for a broader peace deal, according to analyst Negar Mortazavi. Experts said it is unlikely that talks for this larger agreement could restart until the issue of the Strait of Hormuz and how it will be managed is settled.
“Both sides appear to be putting forward maximalist demands ahead of serious negotiations,” Mortazavi, senior fellow at the Centre for International Policy, told Al Jazeera.
Mortazavi said the latest US stance is especially sensitive.
“Trump’s new demands are particularly problematic because they introduce issues that go beyond ending the current conflict. If compensation over protests and other past events becomes a genuine US condition for an agreement, rather than simply a negotiating position, it could make a deal extremely difficult for Tehran to accept,” she added.
In turn, Tehran, she said, is also seeking significant guarantees, not only for an end to the fighting but also “assurances that the conflict will not simply restart later, as well as economic relief after the war”.
Tehran has previously indicated that it has lost trust in US negotiators because the US has commenced attacks three times on Iran while previous talks had been going on.
According to Tehran-based political analyst Hossein Royvaran, how the Strait of Hormuz standoff ends will come down to which party has the greatest endurance.
“This equation now exists: closure vs blockade. But the question is, who cries out first?” he told Al Jazeera.
“Right now, America is suffering: in petrol prices, in inflation, in the rising cost of living at home. There is deep discontent inside America over this war and its consequences for society there,” Royvaran told Al Jazeera.
“The same is true in Iran, though in Iran there are justifications society finds acceptable: that this war was imposed on Iran and Iran had no choice but to defend itself.”

title: What to watch in Wisconsin’s high-stakes primary
summary: US Democrats face another test after Michigan as voters choose nominees for governor and Congress.
full_text:
What to watch in Wisconsin’s high-stakes primary
US Democrats face another test after Michigan as voters choose nominees for governor and Congress.
A week after progressives scored a victory in Michigan’s US Senate primary, Democrats face another test, this time in the Upper Midwestern US state of Wisconsin.
Voters in the battleground state head to the polls on Tuesday in a primary that will help shape races for governor and all eight US House of Representatives seats in November, as well as the Wisconsin State Assembly and half of the State Senate.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4El-Sayed wins Michigan Democratic Senate primary
- list 2 of 4Shifting US politics offers opportunity for Palestinian self-determination
- list 3 of 4What to know about this week’s US primary elections in Tennessee and Hawaii
- list 4 of 4US Senator McConnell says he’s been discharged from rehabilitation centre
But the biggest spotlight is on the Democratic contest for governor, which has become another proxy battle between the party’s progressive wing and its more moderate establishment.
The results will not only shape Wisconsin politics, but also could offer clues about where Democratic voters want the party to go ahead of November’s United States midterm elections.
Why is Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor so important?
Wisconsin is the next major test after progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated establishment-backed US Representative Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary on Tuesday, renewing questions about whether Democratic voters are moving further left.
This year’s primaries have repeatedly seen outsider candidates outperform establishment favourites, reflecting frustration among many Democratic voters after the party’s losses in the 2024 presidential election and an internal debate happening over US support for Israel. While progressive candidates have won against establishment ones in heavily Democratic states like New York or Colorado, there have been questions about whether more leftist candidates can succeed in US states, like Michigan or Wisconsin, where both Democratic and Republican candidates can have a similar level of support. US President Donald Trump won both Michigan and Wisconsin in the 2024 US presidential election after former US President Joe Biden won them in 2020.
Wisconsin will be closely watched for whether the trend of progressive wins continues.
Whoever wins will likely face Republican Representative Tom Tiffany, a Trump ally who has already been framing the race as a choice between what he calls a “socialist agenda” and “common sense”.
Who are Francesca Hong and David Crowley?
The Democratic race for the gubernatorial nominee in Wisconsin has narrowed to two very different candidates.
State Representative Francesca Hong is a lawmaker, former restaurant worker and democratic socialist who, if elected, would become Wisconsin’s first woman governor and first Asian American governor.
Hong’s campaign has focused on issues like free childcare, cancelling student debt, and abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). She’s also faced scrutiny over past social media posts, including ones supporting Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) policies such as abolishing the US Senate and abolishing or defunding police. She’s since distanced herself from some of those positions, saying she doesn’t support the national DSA’s full platform and has pledged not to cut police budgets. Hong has emphasised that she’s a member of the local DSA chapter in Madison, Wisconsin, but not a national member.
Hong, who has been endorsed by Minnesota Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar and has campaigned alongside left-wing commentator Hasan Piker, has also described Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide, advocated for Palestinian rights and called for repealing a Wisconsin law that bars state agencies from contracting with companies that boycott Israel.
Her main opponent, David Crowley, is the Milwaukee County executive, the chief public official for the county, who initially dropped out of the race and re-entered 10 days later, in mid-July, after being endorsed by outgoing Governor Tony Evers. The endorsement quickly cemented Crowley as the establishment favourite, with supporters arguing he’s the strongest candidate to keep the governor’s office in Democratic hands.
Crowley, however, has insisted he isn’t an establishment democrat and that he considers the term a “slur”. He is also hoping to make history as Wisconsin’s first Black governor and said he intends to focus on undecided voters.
A Marquette University Law School poll of Wisconsin Democratic primary voters conducted in late July showed Hong with a significant lead in the race.
Why has the governor’s primary been so chaotic?
Lieutenant Governor Sara Rodriguez was the first major Democrat to drop out after a campaign finance controversy. Former Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation CEO Missy Hughes later ended her campaign, further narrowing the field.
Then, less than two weeks before election day, former Lieutenant Governor Mandela Barnes withdrew after allegations of inappropriate behaviour resurfaced during the campaign. Barnes denied any wrongdoing, and a review commissioned by the Wisconsin Democratic Party found no actionable evidence because the allegations were anonymous and lacked specific details, according to the Associated Press.
Crowley then re-entered the race, following the endorsement of outgoing Governor Evers.
Because all of the withdrawals came after Wisconsin’s filing deadline, the candidates remain on the ballot. Almost 128,000 absentee ballots have already been returned, meaning many voters had cast ballots for candidates who were no longer actively campaigning. A judge later rejected a lawsuit that was seeking to have the absentee ballots cancelled and allow voters to vote again.
What are other races to watch?
In western Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, Democrats are choosing between Rebecca Cooke – a nonprofit executive and the party’s 2024 nominee, who came within about three percentage points of defeating Republican Representative Derrick Van Orden – and Emily Berge, the former president of the Eau Claire City Council. The winner will face Van Orden in November in one of the country’s most competitive House races, and one Democrats see as one of their best opportunities to flip a Republican-held seat.
An additional race to watch is in the state’s 7th Congressional District. The race has largely centred on Michael Alfonso, the 26-year-old son-in-law of US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who has Trump’s endorsement. He faces several competitors, including Jessi Ebben, a manufacturing strategist and grassroots Trump organiser who has campaigned on border security, expanding American manufacturing and protecting gun rights, and Kevin Hermening, a former US Marine who was one of 66 Americans held hostage by Iran for 444 days starting in 1979.
The district is expected to remain safely Republican, meaning the primary winner will be heavily favoured in November. Democrats are also choosing between Chris Armstrong, former state Representative Fred Clark and Ginger Murray for their party’s nomination.
When do polls open and close?
Polls are open from 7am to 8pm local time (12:00-01:00 GMT on Tuesday-Wednesday).

title: A strong China is the best hope for the ‘long peace’ to endure
summary: The “long peace” is a term coined by Yale professor and Cold War historian John Lewis Gaddis in his 1987 book The Long Peace: Inquiries into the History of the Cold War. It refers to the fact that, from the end of World War II in 1945 into the 1980s, more than 40 years passed without a third world war between the United States and Soviet Union. full_text:
Senior Colonel Zhou Bo (ret) is a senior fellow at the Centre for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University and a China Forum expert.
The “long peace” is a term coined by Yale professor and Cold War historian John Lewis Gaddis in his 1987 book The Long Peace: Inquiries into the History of the Cold War. It refers to the fact that, from the end of World War II in 1945 into the 1980s, more than 40 years passed without a third world war between the United States and Soviet Union. For centuries before 1945, great powers fought destructive general wars such as the Napoleonic Wars, World War I and World War II roughly once every generation.
Gaddis is almost right, except that the divide between the Cold War and the outbreak of a hot war was razor thin. During the Cold War, people in the camps led by the two superpowers were preparing for a hot war: an all-out world war III. Proxy wars were easily found on every continent. Nuclear false alarms showed we had a narrow escape from doomsday. Such a long peace looks lucky rather than intentional.
The real long peace is China’s peaceful rise that began in 1978, when Beijing started its “reform and opening up” period. Peace lasting half a century has been a rarity throughout Chinese history. Chinese dynasties are punctuated with discontented peasant groups forcibly toppling reigning dynasties, only for subsequent peasant uprisings to overthrow the regime in a repeating cycle. Even in the early decades after the founding of the People’s Republic of China, military conflicts still occurred roughly once every decade, including the Korean war, the Sino-Indian war and the Sino-Vietnamese war.
After 1978, the nation shifted its core priority to economic development. Subsequent diplomatic crises, such as Nato’s bombing of the Chinese embassy in the former Yugoslavia and the fatal Sino-US military aircraft collision in the South China Sea in 2001, didn’t distract it from this strategic focus. This era of peace represents one of the longest spans of stability and prosperity across Chinese civilisation.
The question is whether it can continue. In part, the answer lies in whether the third long peace between China and the US that stretches back to the end of the Korean war can continue. Sino‑American ties before US president Richard Nixon’s landmark visit fell under the broader Cold War framework. Yet even if subsequent bilateral relations resist a simple one‑word definition, direct conflict has never broken out between the two nations.
US President Donald Trump’s state visit to Beijing in May marked Washington’s recognition of China as a peer power. Whether the announced strategic stability can be “constructive” is far from certain.
