Continue reading...
full_text:
Thailand has suspended firearms licences after last week’s deadly school shooting, as the bodies of the teenage attacker and the grandparents he killed were cremated.
The prime minister, Anutin Charnvirakul, said he had ordered the interior ministry and police to stop issuing licenses to possess, purchase and carry firearms, and called for “tighter controls and decisive penalties”.
On Friday, a 14-year-old boy shot dead the grandparents who raised him at their home in Nonthaburi, north of Bangkok, before killing six others at his school and then turning the gun on himself.
The white caskets of the couple were laid out at the Tem Rak Samakkhi Buddhist temple on Tuesday, alongside their portraits, ahead of their cremation capping a funeral lasting several days.
The boy’s smaller casket was placed to the side at the same temple, surrounded by white flowers.
Among the mourners was Tawee Piewphong, who paid tribute to his brother-in-law – the grandfather – as “a man of few words, but a very kind person”.
Tawee expressed shock at the killings, saying he had no idea what motivated the teenager – but also offered compassion.
“I want to tell him that being 14 is just a small fraction of your entire life, and every problem has a solution. Not everything is the end of the world,” the 70-year-old said.
Investigators are still seeking a motive for the shooting, but police said on Sunday the boy had watched violent videos online and once brought an air gun to school.
Officials said previously that he faced academic-related stress, and a classmate said he was bullied.
“Of course I feel bad for the innocent people who were killed,” said Somjai Poosod, whose grandchildren attend the school attacked, “but I feel there is an issue of mental health that we may need to address to prevent incidents like this from happening again.”
The shooting has resonated across the country, with the king and Charnvirakul leading an outpouring of grief.
On Monday, the attacker’s father told the Guardian he still does not understand why his son did what he did, but he is left to reckon with the violence his own flesh and blood had committed.
“I’m experiencing so many emotions all at once. I feel guilty and heartbroken because I’ve suffered a loss too. I’ve lost my child, as well as my parents.”
The shooter used his grandfather’s gun to kill his grandparents before heading to the school.
There, he shot dead five teachers and staff and wounded a 12-year-old girl, who died in hospital on Saturday.
Thailand has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region, and past promises of tightening gun laws have not prevented repeated shootings.

title: Cook Islands election: PM Mark Brown speaks on the diplomatic crises that defined his year
summary:
The prime minister tells the Guardian that last year’s diplomatic rift with ally New Zealand could be on voters’ minds as they head to the polls

As voters in the Cook Islands prepare to head to the polls in a high-stakes general election, they will have much to reflect on. Over recent years, politics in this small island nation has been defined by fierce debates about deep-sea mining, diplomatic rifts with ally New Zealand and a major reshaping of the country’s foreign partnerships.

In an exclusive interview with the Guardian, days before Wednesday’s poll, Cook Islands prime minister Mark Brown defended his four-year term and the decisions he made that have seen this South Pacific nation of 17,000 people pushed into the international limelight, turning it into a battleground for influence between Beijing and western powers.

Continue reading...
full_text:
As voters in the Cook Islands prepare to head to the polls in a high-stakes general election, they will have much to reflect on. Over recent years, politics in this small island nation has been defined by fierce debates about deep-sea mining, diplomatic rifts with ally New Zealand and a major reshaping of the country’s foreign partnerships.
In an exclusive interview with the Guardian, days before Wednesday’s poll, Cook Islands prime minister Mark Brown defended his four-year term and the decisions he made that have seen this South Pacific nation of 17,000 people pushed into the international limelight, turning it into a battleground for influence between Beijing and western powers.
In 2025, Cook Islands struck strategic partnership deals with Beijing, sparking severe alarm in Wellington. The rift was formally patched after the signing of a new bilateral agreement with New Zealand in April.
Brown acknowledged the diplomatic fallout “does have bearings” on voters, saying “our people are quite mindful and aware of what happens in the geopolitical space”.
“For us in the Cook Islands, it’s important that these engagements are on our terms … and that their collaboration with us is on areas that we’ve identified as priorities for the Cook Islands.”
According to a poll conducted by Cook Islands News, Wednesday’s election will be a close race between Brown’s Cook Islands party and challenger the Cook Islands United party, led by Teariki Heather, who organised a public protest against the partnership agreement with China last year.
That partnerships agreement significantly affected Cook Islanders at home and in New Zealand, Heather said, adding that Brown should have been transparent from the start about the documents signed on behalf of the country.
“What prime minister Mark Brown did has upset the people. It is not the way to act,” Heather said. “For us, the Cook Islands people, humility is most important. We respect that relationship with New Zealand – it has been set in concrete since 1965.”
The economy and cost of living pressures are key issues for voters. When Brown took office in 2020, the Cook Islands faced major economic uncertainty amid the Covid-19 pandemic. Two years later, as he led his party to victory in the 2022 general election, the country was still reeling from border closures that decimated its primary economic engine – tourism – which traditionally accounts for roughly 70% of GDP. Debt swelled as the government struggled to “keep things alive, keep businesses going”.
“Today our economy is the strongest it’s ever been in its history,” Brown said. “We’ve managed to halve the debt that we took on in 2022. We’ve had significant year on year growth exceeding 10% per annum.”
Like other small island states in the South Pacific, the Cook Islands has been hit hard by inflation and global energy shocks caused by chaos in the Middle East.
“When this fuel price spike occurred as a result of the conflicts in Iran, immediately we saw the impacts of that with unstable fuel supply, huge spikes and increases,” he said. The administration established a fund to absorb extreme swings in energy prices.
Brown’s foreign policy moves have also triggered intense domestic debate and ruffled feathers across the Pacific.
After Cook Islands struck deals with China in 2025, New Zealand – which maintains constitutional “free association” ties and provides citizenship to Cook Islanders – temporarily halted millions in aid. Wellington accused Rarotonga of a lack of transparency, and Brown called the reaction patronising.
However, he said the signing of the Defence and Security Agreement “really allayed a lot of fears that people had about our relationship with New Zealand”.Brown insists that establishing defence boundaries with New Zealand allows the Cook Islands to freely pursue economic relationships elsewhere without compromising security ties.
“In matters of security and defence, our partner is New Zealand – that’s clear in everybody’s minds, not just our people, but internationally as well.”
Developing relationships with other countries “and not relying just on one country is important for us as a country, to maintain and build our economic resilience”.
China remains a cornerstone of that strategy, particularly for infrastructure programmes, alongside expanding engagements with India, South Korea, Japan and the United States.
“China remains an important partner, not just for the Cook Islands, but right across the Pacific,” Brown said.“It’s the largest trading partner of Australia and New Zealand and some of our other Pacific Island countries.”
He said China has a “huge development programme” which supports many countries in the Pacific, including in infrastructure.
The deep-sea mining question
The US is showing heightened strategic and economic interest in the country’s deep-sea polymetallic nodules, which are rich in critical minerals needed globally for the transition to renewable energy technologies.
Environmental groups and some regional leaders warn that seabed extraction could cause irreversible damage to fragile marine ecosystems. Brown, however, maintains that research must precede any definitive verdict.
“The exploration phase is still being undertaken,” Brown said. “There is no mining that is taking place right now. And there will be no mining that takes place until and unless we can be satisfied that its impacts will not affect our marine environment.”
Brown said ongoing research is building a significant body of data that is attracting interest from global research institutes. This knowledge, he noted, will deepen understanding of the deep ocean, facilitate potential mineral extraction to diversify the economy and position the Cook Islands within the global transition toward renewable energy.
Cook Islands political analyst William Numanga said the outcome of the election would be closely watched by international partners, particularly New Zealand and China.
However, he emphasised that the election should not be seen simply as the Cook Islands choosing between the two.
“New Zealand remains our closest constitutional partner, with deep family, historical and economic ties, while the Cook Islands will continue to build relationships with China and other international partners where they support our national interests,” Numanga said.
He said the challenge for the next government will be to maintain the relationship with New Zealand while pursuing an “independent foreign policy that puts the interests of Cook Islanders first.”

title: Bondi shooting hero Ahmed al Ahmed cleared of assault charges
summary:
Ahmed, who maintains his innocence, was accused of putting his father in a headlock in March

The man who disarmed one of the gunmen allegedly responsible for the Bondi Beach massacre has had an assault case against him tossed out.

Ahmed al Ahmed, 44, had been accused of putting his father in a headlock on 9 March and intimidation over an alleged incident in June.

Continue reading...
full_text:
The man who disarmed one of the gunmen allegedly responsible for the Bondi beach terror attack has had an assault case against him tossed out.
Ahmed al-Ahmed, 44, had been accused of putting his father in a headlock on 9 March and intimidation over an alleged incident in June.
He pleaded not guilty to both charges in an appearance at Bankstown local court on 24 June, before prosecutors confirmed on Wednesday they had withdrawn both counts.
An apprehended domestic violence order protecting his father will remain in place for 12 months, court documents show.
In June, his lawyer, Mohamad Sakr, emphasised al-Ahmed would maintain his innocence.
“It is a family situation he never expected, one would never want to expect, and it must be really difficult for him,” he said.
“He is a heroic man and his honesty and dignity should be maintained until these matters are ultimately determined.”
When the charges were initially laid, al-Ahmed alleged members of his family were seeking a cut of the $2.5m raised on his behalf after he garnered international attention for his actions during the massacre.
“This situation is untrue, it’s extortion ... and my two brothers have been harassing me, abusing me and pushing to get money from me,” he told Sydney radio 2GB in June.
His brothers, Sameh and Hozifa, were granted conditional bail in June after pleading not guilty to charges of using a carriage service to menace or harass, regarding claims they tried to extort $200,000 from their brother.
An interim domestic violence prevention order prohibits the pair from going within 100 metres of their brother, his home or workplace.
The tobacconist made headlines around the world after video footage of him disarming a gunman during the Bondi massacre went viral.
He was shot in the arm multiple times during the incident and was visited in hospital by the prime minister, Anthony Albanese.
He was awarded the keys to the city of Canterbury-Bankstown, where he lives, and Waverley, where the attack took place.

title: A ‘body’ found in a suitcase was actually a sex doll. How did NSW police get it so wrong?
summary:
Officers – correctly – may not have fully unzipped the bag containing the lifelike doll to avoid destroying evidence, one expert says

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Revelations that a “body” found inside a suitcase was actually a sex doll may have been embarrassing for police, but experts say officers followed the correct procedure.

New South Wales police on Sunday were called to Oallen, a town near Goulburn, after two members of the public found a suitcase containing what they believed to be human remains, dumped on the side of the road.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Revelations that a “body” found inside a suitcase was actually a sex doll may have been embarrassing for police, but experts say officers followed the correct procedure.
New South Wales police on Sunday were called to Oallen, a town near Goulburn, after two members of the public found a suitcase containing what they believed to be human remains, dumped on the side of the road.
A police statement released on Sunday said the body was believed to be female, and the bag was sent to the forensic medicine laboratory.
But after forensic examinations on Monday morning, it was confirmed the “body” was actually a life-like doll dressed in clothes that had hair, a nose piercing and markings that resembled bruises and grazes.
While former NSW police officer Vincent Hurley said the discovery was “amusing in hindsight”, investigators had done the right thing.
“Police have been blamed over the years, and rightly so, for tunnel vision,” Hurley, a criminologist, told Guardian Australia.
“Can you imagine if it was a real body and they just go unzip the bag and say, ‘we’ll have a poke’?
“They did the right thing, it’s embarrassing, yes, but they followed procedure.”
When police arrive at a reported crime scene, they generally try not to contaminate it, Hurley said.
This means they may not have unzipped the bag the entire way to confirm a potential body, because doing so could destroy any fibres or blood that may have been on the zipper.
The best practice for investigating potential bodies inside things like wheelie bins and suitcases is not to open it, but to X-ray it, Paola Magni, a Murdoch University forensic science associate professor, said.
Even after realising they had a doll, forensic examiners likely would have had to fully continue inspecting it for traces of evidence like semen or other DNA in case it was associated with another suspicious case.
“It’s a doll, but if it’s connected to another crime, they can use that opportunity to link it to something suspect,” said Magni, an expert in decomposition.
“Any potentially suspicious situation has to be treated with the best practice in forensic investigation.
“They did the right thing, they investigated it step-by-step.”
Hurley also said objects like sex dolls could be “incredibly lifelike” and noted the bodies of real murder victims were often found in confined places like car boots, suitcases and barrels.
“It’s not unusual to be in a suitcase, it’s just unusual that it turned out to be a plastic doll,” he said.
Crimes around sex dolls are generally rare, but in Australia possessing a child-like sex doll is an offence and police have previously charged people after intercepting air cargo found to contain such items.
However, the one discovered on Sunday is not believed to be childlike and police investigations into it have concluded.
At her press conference on Monday, Supt Linda Bradbury maintained police had “no regrets”.
“Our police have undertaken the processes that we do to maintain integrity in such serious crime, to a T, and I do commend people for that,” she said.
Bradbury confirmed the members of the public who discovered the suitcase had made the right decision by pulling over, peeking inside, and calling as soon as they believed it was something suspicious.

title: July’s Heat Made History. Trump’s Cuts Could Leave Us Less Prepared for What Comes Next
summary: The federal agencies that monitor and forecast extreme weather are operating with fewer people and an uncertain funding future.
full_text:
July was the hottest month on record in the contiguous United States, with an average temperature of 76.9°F—the highest average ever recorded by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), going back to 1895. The previous record was shared by July 1936, during the Dust Bowl, and July 2012. Every state was at least 1 degree above its 20th-century average.
This type of observation can help communities prepare for and respond to extreme heat events. They can then take informed steps to prevent serious health issues that the World Health Organization (WHO) links to high temperatures, like heat stroke and cardiovascular disease, or even death.
But NOAA relies on federal funding in order to keep historic records, observe weather patterns, and produce informed forecasts.
The Trump Administration reduced NOAA’s workforce in 2025, and subsequently proposed steep cuts to the agency’s funding, hampering its ability to monitor weather conditions, analyze patterns, and provide forecasts.
The National Weather Service (NWS), which operates under NOAA, lost roughly 600 employees—about 15% of its workforce—through layoffs, buyouts and retirements. It must now respond to increasingly severe weather events—like hurricane season and wildfire season—with reduced resources. As a result, it announced last year that it was scaling back the tools used to track weather patterns, such as weather balloons.
The administration later proposed cutting NOAA’s overall budget by $1.6 billion, or roughly 26%, compared with fiscal year 2025.
“A leaner NOAA that focuses on core operational needs, eliminates unnecessary layers of bureaucracy, terminates nonessential grant programs, and ends activities that do not warrant a Federal role, will provide better value to the American public,” its budget summary stated.
The United States will likely continue struggling to reconcile diminishing resources with increasing extreme temperatures, as the United Nations World Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned Tuesday that periods of extreme heat will become more frequent, intense, and longer-lasting as climate change warms the planet.
How we know when heat is becoming dangerous
The NWS tracks weather in multiple ways—including the installation of surface stations at over 900 airports that provide 24/7 real-time surface weather observations, as well as weather balloons, marine buoys, and satellites.
Those observations feed forecast models that help meteorologists understand developing weather patterns and anticipate dangerous conditions.
“Extended periods of high day and nighttime temperature conditions create cumulative stress on the human body, increasing the risk of illness and death from heat exposure,” according to the WHO. In the United States, the NWS considers heat the leading weather-related killer. Globally, studies estimate that heat was associated with roughly 489,000 deaths annually between 2000 and 2019.
The health effects of heat waves were felt acutely this summer. Maryland’s Department of Health said that 2026 was its deadliest heat season on record, with a total of 50 heat-related fatalities since May. The state also recorded over 1,300 heat-related illnesses in that period. At the national level, the Washington Post reported that there were at least 70 deaths related to heat domes in July. And in Europe, officials said that there were more than 10,000 excess deaths during the continent’s record-breaking heat wave in June.
The NWS communicates the danger that high temperatures pose using a Heat Index that describes the “feels like” temperature to the human body based on a combination of heat and humidity. For consistency, it uses what’s called “apparent temperature,” referring to the temperature that the body “feels” in shady locations. Exposure to direct sunlight can increase values by up to 15°F.
With information from the NWS, local governments are better able to prepare infrastructure and warn vulnerable communities. At the same time, the agencies are better equipped to create and distribute useful resources, such as guidance on how to stay cool during heat waves.
But less accurate data, and less data collected overall, can prevent experts from accurately anticipating future events. Agencies might be less prepared to inform vulnerable communities or cooperate with local and state governments to ensure outreach and preparedness. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, this is more likely to impact people with chronic medical conditions, children, and adults over 65.
What happens when weather agencies have fewer resources?
Cuts at NOAA and the Federal Emergency Management Agency have left the U.S. more vulnerable to the effects of extreme weather.
In May, for instance, lawmakers expressed concerns over the NWS’s failure to launch 75% of the weather balloons typically sent aloft in Kansas to help measure atmospheric conditions. These balloons carry a device called a radiosonde that is used to collect upper-atmosphere temperature, humidity, pressure, and wind information to support forecasting. NWS blamed staffing shortages, but Kansas Rep. Sharice Davids pointed out that those disruptions were occurring during tornado season.
“Kansans deserve transparency about what’s happening, why it’s happening and what’s being done to fix it,” Davids said in a statement. “Kansans deserve confidence that the systems meant to keep them safe are fully operational during tornado season and meteorologists deserve the reliable data they need to do their jobs.”
In order to preserve its work with fewer resources, NOAA has continued to evolve its use of technology. It has long used artificial intelligence and machine learning for “weather forecasting, climate modeling, and environmental monitoring.” And it announced a partnership with Google Cloud in July, explaining how the move is expected to “result in a modeling system that is more flexible and easy to update.”
That same month, China debuted Fenghe, an open-source large language model (LLM) for meteorological services. The government announced that the LLM “is trained on 50 million tokens of meteorological service data and integrated with authoritative weather datasets to support weather forecasting, risk assessment, and meteorological services.”
As NOAA faces an uncertain funding future, such tools could become increasingly important to its efforts to maintain forecasting capacity for an increasingly hot planet.

title: Saber denies replacing Rideshare Stimulator’s writers with ChatGPT
summary: After a former lead writer claimed Saber "replaced me with ChatGPT," CEO Matthew Karch now claims, "Neither Saber nor Unigine have replaced any writers with AI," for the Rideshare "Stimulator" game announced last month, developed by Unigine. The writer, Stella Sacco, says differently, however, posting on Bluesky that "I was lead writer on this one! […]
full_text:
After a former lead writer claimed Saber “replaced me with ChatGPT,” CEO Matthew Karch now claims, “Neither Saber nor Unigine have replaced any writers with AI,” for the Rideshare “Stimulator” game announced last month, developed by Unigine.
Saber denies replacing Rideshare Stimulator’s writers with ChatGPT
Saber’s CEO says the game’s story was ‘written entirely by real people’ except for one experimental mode.
The writer, Stella Sacco, says differently, however, posting on Bluesky that “I was lead writer on this one! And Saber replaced me with ChatGPT midway through development. All the passenger voices were AI too. Either they changed direction at some point or they’re not disclosing it on Steam.”
Saber describes Rideshare “Stimulator” as an “immersive driving simulation game that puts you behind the wheel as a rideshare business owner,” and the segments shown in a teaser trailer appear to include AI-generated writing and audio for the simulated riders who are being picked up. The game’s Steam listing does not currently include any disclosure about using generative AI.
A statement from Karch provided to The Verge says, “The game will also feature an experimental, free-ride mode that by necessity incorporates AI as the number of passengers in the game is infinite. We are firm believers in using AI tools to improve or enhance gameplay experiences and improve NPC behavior as we have done since Saber was founded in 2001,” it continued, also claiming that “As the industry has continued to contract, Saber continues to hire. None of our 3000+ employees have to worry about being replaced by AI.”
Sacco replied to Karch’s statement in a message sent to The Verge. “My indignation at being called a liar by that statement aside, you can’t meaningfully say both ‘writers wrote the story’ and ‘computers wrote the text,’” Sacco says. “If rides I wrote are in there, and also rides AI wrote or will write are in there, then AI was still used, and I was still replaced, just as Saber told me they were doing in December 2023. They’re trying to have it both ways. You can’t win on the labor part of the statement while you admit you took work away from labor in the next part. It’s ridiculous.”

title: XRP bridge drained for $200,000 after software mistook fake deposits for real ones
full_text:
XRP bridge drained for $200,000 after software mistook fake deposits for real ones
An attacker created unbacked XRP on another blockchain, then exchanged it for real XRP held in reserve. The bridge has been halted and its operator has filed a complaint with the FBI.
- Nearly 200,000 XRP, worth about $200,000, were drained from a bridge linking the XRP Ledger to the tx blockchain after an attacker exploited a software flaw.
- The bug let the bridge register non-existent deposits as real, issuing unbacked bridged XRP that the attacker then used to withdraw genuine XRP from the reserve wallet.
- Tx says it has halted the bridge, patched the vulnerability, hired blockchain forensics experts and filed an FBI complaint, but has not yet explained how affected holders will be compensated.
An XRP bridge lost nearly 200,000 XRP, worth about $200,000 at current prices, after a software flaw let an attacker claim deposits that were never made, then withdraw real tokens against the fake balances.
The bridge connected the XRP Ledger to Coreum, a separate blockchain which rebranded this March as tx, a U.S.-based outfit focused on tokenizing real-world assets. The tokens XRP left the bridge's reserve wallet in 97 minutes on Aug. 9 before the system was halted.
A bridge is supposed to work like a vault with a receipt system. A user sends XRP into a reserve wallet on the XRP Ledger, and the bridge creates an equivalent amount of bridged XRP on the other chain. Returning those tokens lets the user withdraw the real XRP held in the reserve.
The attacker found a way to make that system issue the receipts without putting anything into the vault.
According to tx, the bridge's software registered transactions as deposits even though they never delivered XRP to the bridge. That gave the attacker bridged XRP on the tx chain without the real XRP that was supposed to back it. Those unbacked tokens then went back through the bridge, and the attacker withdrew real XRP from the reserve.
The drain began at 19:16 UTC. Each payout was authorized by 17 of the bridge's 28 relayers, a majority signing off exactly as designed, because the bridge's own records told them the deposits were real.
Relayers are programs that watch both blockchains and approve transfers when the bridge's records say a withdrawal is owed.
The specific failure sat one layer down, however, as the relayer code processed payments carrying the bridge's memo without first verifying the destination address.
tx confirmed the deposit-detection flaw in an update, saying the attacker exploited software that incorrectly recognized transactions that delivered no XRP to the reserve.
An update on the XRPL bridge incident.
On August 9, the tx XRPL bridge was exploited and XRP was drained from the bridge's reserve wallet on the XRP Ledger. The bridge has been halted, the vulnerability has been identified, and all potential remedies are being evaluated. This…
The project added it has identified and fixed the vulnerable code, engaged blockchain forensics specialists and filed a complaint with the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center. It has not said how affected holders will be made whole.
Meanwhile, the stolen XRP did not stay put. Onchain tracking shows most of it moved onward within hours through several other addresses.

title: Ravencoin hits record low as network exploit puts transactions at risk
summary: Mining pools controlling most of Ravencoin’s hash rate are building a competing chain that could trigger a three-day reorganization.
full_text:
Ravencoin hits record low as network exploit puts transactions at risk
Mining pools controlling most of Ravencoin’s hash rate are building a competing chain that could trigger a three-day reorganization.
Ravencoin dropped to an all-time low on Wednesday as an exploited consensus vulnerability left several days of transactions at risk and prompted exchanges to suspend RVN transfers.
According to CoinGecko, the cryptocurrency dropped to $0.002754, about 22% below its 24-hour high of $0.003529. Trading volume climbed above $18 million during the sell-off before easing to about $9.6 million, while RVN recovered to around $0.00284, at the time of writing.
On Tuesday, Ravencoin said the exploit caused vulnerable nodes to accept invalid blocks, with the first known instance appearing at height 4,487,776 on Friday. Similar invalid blocks appeared after the flaw was demonstrated on the mainnet, it added.
Mining pools 2Miners and RavenMiner, which Ravencoin said control a majority of the network’s hash rate, are building a competing chain that excludes the exploited branch from that block onward.
If the miners’ chain becomes dominant, the network could undergo a reorganization spanning approximately three days. Ravencoin warned that transactions confirmed after block 4,487,775 could be reversed and may not automatically return to the mempool or be mined again.
The project recommended that exchanges halt deposits and withdrawals until the chain stabilizes. Upbit and Bitget suspended RVN transfers, although Upbit left trading available.

title: India’s Yulu raises $93M as quick-commerce boom fuels e-bike demand
summary: Yulu aims to have a fleet of 200,000 bikes in the next two years and faster electric two-wheelers, aiming at new logistics use cases.
full_text:
As India’s quick-commerce platforms race to deliver everything from groceries to smartphones in minutes, electric mobility startup Yulu has seized the boom, raising $93 million in fresh funding.
The Bengaluru‑based startup offers electric two‑wheelers on weekly subscription plans, so delivery drivers can jump straight into the platform, without buying their own vehicle. With around 50,000 electric vehicles in its fleet, Yulu reports that it logs about 1.6 million miles each week and powers more than 750,000 deliveries a day. The new funding will let Yulu grow that fleet to 200,000 bikes in the next two years and launch faster electric two-wheelers aimed at different logistics use cases.
The Series C round comprised $63 million in equity led by GEF Capital Partners and $30 million in debt financing. About $5.5 million of the equity component was used to buy shares from seed investors whose funds were nearing the end of their investment life, co-founder and CEO Amit Gupta said in an interview.
The deal valued Yulu at about $170 million post-money, people familiar with the matter told TechCrunch. Gupta declined to comment when asked about the valuation and did not dispute the figure.
Existing investors Bajaj Auto and Magna International did not participate in the round after waiving their pre-emptive rights, allowing GEF to acquire its target ownership stake, Gupta said. He added that the startup expects this to be its final equity fundraising before an eventual public listing, with future fleet expansion financed primarily through debt and lease financing.
The business moves toward becoming profitable before interest and taxes next year, after achieving positive EBITDA last financial year, Gupta told TechCrunch. The startup also saw its revenue growing seven-fold between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2026, he said, without sharing specifics.
The COVID shift
Founded as a bike-sharing startup for urban commuters in 2017, Yulu found its biggest opportunity during the COVID-19 pandemic as demand for food and grocery deliveries accelerated.
Today, Gupta told TechCrunch that about 95% of Yulu’s revenue comes from renting electric bikes to gig workers on weekly subscriptions, while the rest is generated by its station‑based rental service in Bengaluru. The startup has also dropped an earlier plan to sell bikes directly to consumers.
To fuel its next growth phase, Yulu is introducing a full-sized, higher‑speed electric scooter, called Yulu Express. This is designed for longer‑haul e‑commerce deliveries, bike taxis, and express parcel services — the areas its slower fleet could not previously cover.
About a third of the planned 200,000‑vehicle fleet will be made up of this new model, Gupta said.
While Yulu’s current low‑speed fleet is built by Bajaj Auto, the new high‑speed scooter comes from a different Indian manufacturer — Gupta declined to name it.
About 500 of the new bikes are already running in Bengaluru and are being trialed in three additional cities, Gupta told TechCrunch.
Currently, Yulu operates in 12 Indian cities, running its own operations in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi‑NCR, and Hyderabad, while partnering with franchisees in eight other markets. The startup, Gupta said, aims to reach roughly 20 cities within the next year, with Chennai and Pune among the key targets for expansion.
Gupta stated that Yulu partners with almost every major quick‑commerce, food‑delivery, and e‑commerce platform — including Amazon and Walmart-owned Flipkart — though its customers are the gig workers who rent the bikes, not the platforms themselves. He compared Yulu’s role to “the AWS of mobility,” supplying the infrastructure that lets delivery workers operate without the platforms taking a cut.

（前情提要：非農爆冷「8 月 12 日 CPI 成關鍵」，押注 Fed 升息交易員或集體投降）
（背景補充：高盛估 7 月核心 CPI 漲 0.19% 低於共識，油價已重返 87 美元）
今晚台灣時間 20:30，美國勞工統計局（BLS）將公布 7 月 CPI（消費者物價指數），在上週的非農爆冷之後，這一次 CPI 格外受到關注。今晚公布的 CPI 有 4 個數字要盯緊：整體 CPI 月增、核心 CPI 月增、整體 CPI 年增、核心 CPI 年增。
道瓊斯調查機構預估，整體 CPI 年增率落在 3.4%，核心年增率落在 2.5%，兩者都比 6 月的 3.5% 與 2.6% 回落 0.1 個百分點，但仍明顯高於聯準會 2% 的長期目標。
6 月的基期不算低：當月整體 CPI 月減 0.4%，核心 CPI 月持平，能源價格回落與住房成本降溫是主因。
美國銀行畫出的三道門檻
美國銀行在報告中設下一套具體的判斷框架：若聯準會關注的主要通膨指標，未來兩個月平均月增率落在 0.25% 以上，9 月幾乎確定升息；若平均低於 0.2%，升息時程可能被推遲；若卡在 0.2% 到 0.25% 之間，9 月的決策形同拋硬幣。
今晚市場共識的核心 CPI 月增 0.2%，恰好落在美國銀行畫出的中間地帶。
RSM 首席經濟學家 Joseph Brusuelas 表示，如果今晚數據符合預期，連續兩個月溫和的通膨讀數，會讓聯邦公開市場委員會（FOMC）有更多時間觀察，「委員會將在今年剩餘時間內繼續按兵不動」。
高盛（Goldman Sachs）的估計更保守，預期 7 月核心 CPI 月增僅 0.19%，低於市場共識，但高盛同時提醒，油價已重返每桶 87 美元，通膨降溫的路徑未必平坦。
鴿派敘事還沒完全成立
不過，把今晚數據直接解讀成「升息無望」還太早。7 月 FOMC 會議上，已有 3 名委員投票支援立即升息 25 個基點；聯準會理事庫克（Lisa Cook）也表態，若通膨數據不配合，她會認為升息有其必要。
市場目前反而把 10 月或 12 月視為升息機率相對更高的時間點，而不是完全排除今年升息。
矛盾之處在於：7 月非農數據爆出淨減 2.3 萬人的歷史首見負值，失業率彈升至 4.1%，平均時薪年增率滑落至 3.2%，創 2021 年 5 月以來新低，勞動市場走弱，理論上該讓聯準會更謹慎；但通膨讀數若同時降溫，兩股力道方向一致，反而讓「按兵不動」的理由更充分。
真正的風險是兩者背離：如果今晚 CPI 意外偏熱，聯準會就會同時面對「就業轉弱、通膨不降」的兩難局面。
比特幣卡在 6.3 萬與 6.5 萬之間
撰稿當下，比特幣約在 63,750 美元，24 小時跌幅約 0.5%；以太坊約 1,884 美元。
若今晚核心 CPI 落在 0.2% 附近或更低，符合甚至優於市場共識，等同印證美國銀行門檻規則裡的延後升息路徑，對風險資產是短期利多，比特幣有機會挑戰 65,000 美元壓力區；若核心 CPI 意外落在 0.25% 以上、疊加油價回升的敘事，9 月升息機率會快速回升，屆時比特幣能否守住 63,000 美元需求帶，將是觀察市場情緒的第一道防線。

title: Manus 脫離 Meta 恢復獨立營運，誰贏了，誰輸了？
summary:
Meta 買下 Manus，半年後又被要求吐回來。20 億美元繞了一圈，每一方付的代價都不一樣。 （前情提要： […]

〈Manus 脫離 Meta 恢復獨立營運，誰贏了，誰輸了？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Meta 買下 Manus，半年後又被要求吐回來。20 億美元繞了一圈，每一方付的代價都不一樣。
（前情提要：Manus 告別 Meta 重獲自由！宣布恢復獨立營運，急籲用戶完成資料備份）
（背景補充：騰訊傳擬以 20 億美元從 Meta 手中買回 Manus，躍居最大股東）
一場 20 億美元的併購，走完整個流程之後，又被監管一紙命令走回頭。但這不是單純的「回到原點」，因為併購重啟、資料刪除、股權轉手，每一步都已經留下代價，只是代價落在不同人身上。
Meta 賠的不是那 20 億
2025 年 12 月 29 日，Meta 以約 20 億美元收購 Manus，是祖克柏強化代理型 AI 布局的一步棋。數月之後，這筆投資被中國監管機關全數撤銷。
據多家外媒報導，主導回購的騰訊、真格基金與 HSG（原紅杉資本中國）財團，是以與 Meta 當初買入相同的價格，也就是不低於 20 億美元回購。換句話說，Meta 的本金基本上拿得回來，不是認賠出場。
真正賠掉的：是增值。Manus 被收購前年化營收約 1 億美元，在 Meta 手上半年，靠著流量挹注與廣告管道整合，衝到 4 至 5 億美元，翻了四到五倍。也就是說，Meta 是用原價，把一家營收已經放大四五倍的公司，賣回給對方，這才是這筆交易裡最貴的損失。
同時賠掉的還有時間，與一條原本想補上的產品線。Meta 實質持有 Manus 的時間，從 2025 年 12 月 29 日算到雙方營運分離，約五個半月。據瞭解，分離已在 2026 年 6 月 11 日完成，資料共享管道被切斷，員工也被禁止在內部使用 Manus 工具。
這樣算下來，Meta 這局是有輸有贏：拿回本金，輸掉增值、時間，以及一次補位機會（但半年的時間中獲得的 Manus 資料，也是一項稀缺的智慧財產）。
不要控制權，是這局的重點
北京監管這邊，動作本身就不尋常。中國國家發展和改革委員會（NDRC）下設的審查機制，是在交易完成之後才出手，要求撤銷一筆已經生效的跨境併購。通常監管機關會在交易前擋下爭議收購，事後強制解除並不多見。
規模夠大、技術夠敏感、時間點又卡在中美科技競爭最緊繃的階段，讓 Manus 成了罕見卻好用的示範案例。
真正接手的，是以騰訊為首的中國投資人陣營。股權結構繞了一圈，重新回到中國投資人主導的位置，Manus 也將繼續以獨立公司營運，基地設在新加坡。
但真正值得觀察的，是知情人士透露的說法：交易完成後，騰訊即使成為單一最大股東，仍將維持少數股東身分，不尋求控制權。
一家公司剛從外資手中被監管強制收回，主導買回的一方卻主動聲明不要控制權，值得玩味未來的後續發展。
唯一沒得談的輸家
這場清算裡，真正沒有籌碼、沒有談判空間、也拿不回任何東西的，恐怕只有用戶。
Manus 把界線設在 2025 年 12 月 29 日，也就是 Meta 完成收購的當天。這天之後產生的用戶資料，將在 8 月 23 日至 24 日（新加坡時間）之間刪除。受影響的用戶必須在期限前，自己動手用備份工具存下資料，之後還要忍受兩天無法登入帳號，直到 8 月 25 日還原入口重新開放。
用 Apple ID 或 Facebook 帳號註冊的用戶更被動，Manus 沒有他們的 email，連通知都只能靠 app 內推播提醒。
而 Manus 自己這筆帳，其實也算不清。重獲獨立意味著不用再背負「外資控股」的監管標籤，官方也表示正準備一系列新功能；但代價是一批用戶資料被整批清除，用戶對產品的信任也被消耗了一輪。
這場交易走了一圈，金額沒有變，20 億美元還是 20 億美元。監管拿回了主導權，騰訊拿到不情願張揚的股權，Meta 保住本金卻賠掉增值與五個半月的時間，Manus 換了身分卻賠上一批用戶的信任。

title: 法國祭出電話行銷禁令：未經同意撥打最重罰千萬，台灣能跟上？
summary:
法國自 8 月 11 日宣布全面禁止企業未經同意撥打行銷電話，一通最高罰 37.5 萬歐元（約新台幣 1,35 […]

〈法國祭出電話行銷禁令：未經同意撥打最重罰千萬，台灣能跟上？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
法國自 8 月 11 日宣布全面禁止企業未經同意撥打行銷電話，一通最高罰 37.5 萬歐元（約新台幣 1,350 萬元），終結法國人每週被推銷電話轟炸的日常。
（前情提要：全球青少年「社群禁令」浪潮加速，台灣會跟上嗎？）
（背景補充：法國封殺預測市場 Polymarket！全面封鎖網域，違法宣傳最高罰 10 萬歐元）
法國從 8 月 11 日起，正式向「未經同意的推銷電話」宣戰。根據法國國會於 2025 年 6 月 30 日通過的新法，企業日後撥打行銷電話前必須先取得消費者同意，違者最高可被罰 37.5 萬歐元（約新台幣 1,350 萬元），個人違法撥打電話則最重罰 7.5 萬歐元（約新台幣 270 萬元）。
這項由馬克宏政府力推的新法，被視為法國近年消費者保護立法中最強硬的一次出手。
從「你可以拒絕」到「你要先答應」
法國《世界報》在報導中引述法國競爭、消費暨反詐欺總署幕僚長 Alice Vilcot 的說法：「企業未經消費者事前同意，不得主動聯絡消費者。」她強調，這項同意「隨時可以撤回」。這代表法國從過去的「選擇退出」制度，徹底翻轉為「選擇加入」，過去是消費者要主動掛號拒絕，現在變成企業要先問過你才能打。
法律仍留了兩道口子：消費者可以主動勾選同意欄位，選擇接收行銷電話；企業若與消費者已存在契約關係，也能就新的商業方案聯絡對方。換句話說，買過一次東西的老客戶，店家仍能持續行銷，但陌生開發電話全面禁止。
過去法國人若不想被推銷電話騷擾，得自行到政府的 Bloctel 名單註冊拒接；但消費者團體長年抱怨，不少電話行銷公司根本不理會這份名單。Vilcot 指出，一家愛爾蘭公司去年就因撥打 Bloctel 名單上的號碼、違反舊制規定，被重罰 600 萬歐元（約新台幣 2 億 1,600 萬元）。
民眾日後若還接到違法推銷電話，可透過政府網站直接檢舉。
四分之三法國人每週被騷擾
官方統計顯示，法國約有四分之三的民眾每週至少接到一通不請自來的推銷電話，不少人一週收到的還不只一通。
2024 年，11 個消費者保護團體發布聯合聲明，直指「消費者的市話與手機不斷遭到無數不受歡迎的電話行銷騷擾，這種侵擾已經成為他們日常生活的一部分」，要求政府全面禁止。這份聯署，被視為推動這次修法的關鍵民意基礎。
摩洛哥示警：法國新法恐震盪 5 萬個飯碗
新法在法國國內普遍受消費者歡迎，不過在直線距離不到 2,000 公里的摩洛哥卻掀起焦慮。
摩洛哥就業部長 Younes Sekkouri 今年 3 月公開示警，法國這項新規可能讓該國客服產業 4 萬至 5 萬個工作機會陷入風險，原因是法國市場貢獻了摩洛哥電話行銷產業超過八成的營收，法國消費者少接一通電話，可能就是摩洛哥某個客服人員少一次上工機會。
放眼全球，各國對付推銷電話騷擾的態度並不一致。鄰國德國早在 2009 年就實施類似的事前同意制度；但美國、加拿大、英國目前仍是「選擇退出」邏輯，美國民眾可登記全國「請勿來電」名單，加拿大有自己的謝絕來電名單，英國則靠電話偏好服務把關。
在英國，企業撥打已登記謝絕來電名單的號碼，最重可罰 50 萬英鎊（約 67 萬美元）。
台灣呢？個資法有雛形，但罰則差了近百倍
回頭看台灣，同樣的問題並不陌生，只是台灣的因應腳步慢了不少。
台灣其實已經有法源雛形。《個人資料保護法》第 20 條第 2、3 項規定，非公務機關以行銷為目的利用個資，必須在「首次行銷」時提供消費者免費表達拒絕的管道；消費者一旦表示拒絕，業者就應立即停止利用其個資行銷。
問題是，台灣採用的仍是「選擇退出」的老邏輯，跟法國修法前的舊制如出一轍，法國正是因為證明「選擇退出」防不了騷擾，才會轉向「選擇加入」。
真正的落差在罰則。台灣違反個資法第 20 條，主管機關依第 48 條規定只能先「限期改正」，業者逾期不改才處新台幣 2 萬元以上、20 萬元以下罰鍰，還可以按次處罰。
對照法國一通電話最高罰 37.5 萬歐元（約新台幣 1,350 萬元），台灣的罰鍰上限連法國的 2% 都不到，而且還得「先勸導、後開罰」，嚇阻力道天差地遠。台灣也沒有像法國 Bloctel、美國 Do Not Call、英國 TPS 那樣的全國性拒接名單，消費者想閃避推銷電話，只能靠自己一支一支手動封鎖。
台灣要不要跟進法國走向「選擇加入」，法源架構其實已經有了。只要立法院願意把個資法的罰鍰上限拉高到足以讓企業肉痛的等級、比照法國建立全國性拒接名單，並把行銷電話從「事後拒絕」翻轉成「事前同意」。
台灣不是做不到，只是金融業長年倚賴電話行銷通路，修法勢必要先過產業遊說這一關，這跟摩洛哥客服業者面臨的處境，本質上是同一道難題的兩個版本。

title: ChatGPT、Codex 桌面版終於登陸 Linux，市占最小卻是最貴的戰場
summary:
OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT 與 Codex 的 Linux 桌面版，補上落後 Anthropic 一個 […]

〈ChatGPT、Codex 桌面版終於登陸 Linux，市占最小卻是最貴的戰場〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT 與 Codex 的 Linux 桌面版，補上落後 Anthropic 一個月的進度。Linux 桌面市佔僅 4.4%，卻觸及全球 78.5% 的開發者，這場仗搶的是開發機。
（前情提要：OpenAI 開源 Codex Security 掃描工具怎麼用？10 分鐘上手）
（背景補充：Claude Code 預設改為 Auto Mode 開啟，因為人類只會按 yes）
桌面作業系統的世界裡，Linux 只佔全球約 4.4% 的市佔率，等於每 100 台電腦裡不到 5 台裝的是 Linux。但若轉向開發者的電腦，Linux 卻出現在 78.5% 人的機器裡。
ChatGPT 桌面版 Linux 應用程式，8 月 11 日以 preview（預覽版）形式全球同步上線。OpenAI 這次想補上的，就是早就被開發者攻佔的機器。
敲了很久的門終於開了
其實 Linux 用戶要求 OpenAI 推出官方版本，早已在 OpenAI 官方開發者論壇上請願多時。官方的說法是：「Linux 一直是桌面應用最多人敲碗的平台之一，這次上線讓 ChatGPT 與 Codex 覆蓋了所有主要的桌面作業系統。」
這款應用程式讓 Linux 用戶可以在同一個介面裡使用 ChatGPT、ChatGPT Work 與 Codex 三項服務，還內建一個嵌入式瀏覽器。
Now in preview: The ChatGPT desktop app for Linux.
Use ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex where you already work and build, with your projects and browser workflows on supported Linux systems. pic.twitter.com/OtsPt5N5QC
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) August 11, 2026
官方支援的發行版是 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS 與 26.04 LTS 桌面版、Debian 13、Fedora 43 與 44，套件格式涵蓋 DEB 與 RPM，架構支援 x64 與 ARM64。Arch Linux 用戶目前只能靠社群自製的 AUR 套件安裝，並非官方版本。
安裝過程中，OpenAI 會在系統裡加入官方軟體庫。簡單來說就是，電腦裡多一個 OpenAI 自己管理的軟體來源，之後更新不用重新下載安裝檔，直接透過 apt 這類套件管理工具就能升級，跟平常更新系統軟體是同一套流程。
這種做法在 Linux 世界裡再平常不過，卻是 OpenAI 第一次把自己放進這套開發者早已熟悉的更新機制裡。
Codex 才是真正的主角
如果只是把 ChatGPT 網頁包裝成一個桌面視窗，這次更新不會值得特別寫。真正的重點在 Codex。
過去 Codex 在 Linux 上只有命令列介面跟 IDE 擴充套件可用，這次是它第一次在 Linux 上擁有圖形化、以專案為中心的工作區。開發者可以直接開啟並編輯本機專案、操作 Git 儲存庫、存取本機資料夾與終端機，以自己的用戶權限執行指令，再檢視變更、跑測試，整套流程不必再離開視窗切換到終端機。
用戶可以從左上角選單在 ChatGPT 與 Codex 之間切換，兩者各自保留獨立的歷史紀錄與工作區，等於一個應用程式裡裝了兩套完全不同的使用情境：一邊是對話助理，一邊是開發環境。
這也呼應一個常被忽略的事實，AI 產業的競爭，從來不是只比誰的模型論文寫得漂亮，而是工程師密度、算力與資料三者相乘出來的結果。Codex 能不能被工程師天天開啟來用，遠比它在跑分表上多拿幾分更重要。
慢了一個月
OpenAI 不是第一個補齊 Linux 桌面版的大型 AI 實驗室。Anthropic 早在大約一個月前就推出了 Claude 桌面版的 Linux beta，支援 Ubuntu 22.04 以上與 Debian 12 以上，覆蓋範圍甚至比 OpenAI 這次的官方清單更寬。
換句話說，OpenAI 這一步棋，是跟在對手後面補課，而不是搶先卡位。開源與閉源之爭吵得沸沸揚揚，但兩家公司在這件事上做的判斷完全一致：想留住開發者，就得先住進開發者天天開機的那個作業系統。

title: CFTC 動用緊急權力挺 Kalshi：不用管紐約檢察總長關門令，繼續正常營運
summary:
美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）8 月 11 日動用緊急權力，下令預測市場交易所 Kalshi 無視紐約州檢 […]

〈CFTC 動用緊急權力挺 Kalshi：不用管紐約檢察總長關門令，繼續正常營運〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）8 月 11 日動用緊急權力，下令預測市場交易所 Kalshi 無視紐約州檢察總長 Letitia James 的關門要求、繼續正常營運。
（前情提要：紐約起訴 Kalshi！預測市場遭控「無照賭博」，CFTC 也出馬擋人）
（背景補充：CFTC 力挺加密貨幣與預測市場！主席 Michael Selig：美國應追求「金融創新」而非國際監管共識）
美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）8 月 11 日發布官方新聞稿，宣布動用「緊急權力」，依《商品交易法》核心原則，直接命令預測市場交易所 KalshiEX, LLC 繼續正常營運，等於公開表態：聯邦監管機構不甩紐約州檢察總長 Letitia James 對 Kalshi 提出、求償金額超過 360 億美元的關門訴訟。
CFTC 在公告中主張，《商品交易法》要求委員會提供「全國統一的衍生品市場」，一旦市場出現重大中斷，就會妨礙價格發現機制與公眾信心，因此有義務出手維穩。
360 億美元訴訟怎麼來的？
紐約州檢察總長 James 的訴訟在 7 月 31 日提出，地點是曼哈頓的紐約州最高法院，與紐約州長 Kathy Hochul 辦公室聯手出擊。
訴狀指控 Kalshi 經營一個「無照賭博平台」，讓紐約居民（包含未滿該州法定賭博年齡 21 歲者）針對體育賽事、選舉與文化事件下注，總計列出 8 項訴因，涵蓋違反紐約州憲法賭博禁令、莊家行為、持有賭博紀錄、無照行動體育投注，以及聯邦《電信法》（Wire Act）。
360 億美元這個數字的組成分成三塊：沒收 Kalshi 從紐約用戶身上取得的獲利、對下注者作出賠償、再加上三倍獲利罰金。真正把總額推高的，是訴狀主張「每一筆無照投注嘗試罰 10 萬美元」，這個逐筆計算的機制，讓求償金額直接衝上天文數字。
Selig 的「鐵幕」說
CFTC 主席 Michael S. Selig 在新聞稿中措辭強硬表示：
紐約打算讓事件合約衍生品，在法院有機會做出最終裁決之前，就先在該州博弈法的鐵幕之下枯萎凋零。
他接著點名國會授權的核心爭點：
國會從未打算讓衍生品交易所被一套各州拼湊而成的博弈法規管。這些是提供金融工具、跨州營運的金融交易所，它們把一州居民的買單，跟另一州居民的賣單撮合起來，再送進為全國客戶交易提供擔保的清算所。
紐約無權監管這些跨州金融市場。委員會依法有義務確保這些市場秩序，而這正是我們今天所做的事。
才被法官打槍，CFTC 馬上自己動手
真正讓這起事件變得尖銳的，是時間軸上的落差。James 提告後數小時，CFTC 就搶先在聯邦法院提訴，試圖阻止紐約州的案子繼續進行。
但 8 月 4 日，紐約南區聯邦地區法院（SDNY）法官 Jed S. Rakoff 駁回了 CFTC 的緊急聲請，理由是 CFTC「未能證明其勝訴可能性，也未證明若紐約訴訟繼續進行會遭受立即且無法彌補的損害」。法院檔案顯示，CFTC 原本還可以在 8 月 7 日向另一位法官 Victor Marrero 重新提出聲請。
換句話說：CFTC 在司法途徑上先踢到鐵板，短短一週後，8 月 11 日就改用自己手上的行政緊急權力，直接下令、繞過法院裁決的不確定性。
這不是 CFTC 第一次這樣做，今年 7 月，CFTC 就曾動用同一套緊急權力，要求 Kalshi 不理會密西根州法院要求取消已成交交易的命令，被外界視為聯邦監管機構與州司法權對撞的前一波升級。
CFTC 也不只跟紐約一州交手。新聞稿指出，各州持續在州法院與聯邦法院對 CFTC 監管的指定合約市場發動執法行動，為了捍衛國會授予的管轄權，CFTC 已對亞利桑那、康乃狄克、伊利諾、肯塔基、明尼蘇達、新墨西哥、紐約、羅德島、威斯康辛等 9 個州提告，另外向美國第六與第九巡迴上訴法院、以及麻薩諸塞州最高司法法院提交了法庭之友意見書。
Kalshi 怎麼說？
面對紐約州的訴訟，Kalshi 把它定調為「政治秀」，主張州政府不能用自己的法院去關閉一個已經領有聯邦牌照的金融交易所。Kalshi 發言人以一個類比說明後果：「如果 Nasdaq 在紐約被關閉，流動性會枯竭、價格會飆升，全國各地的人買賣股票與其他金融工具都會變得困難、甚至不可能。」
總結來說：紐約州認為，至少體育類的預測市場符合賭博的法律定義，理應受州級監管管轄；CFTC 則堅持這些平台提供的是聯邦監管的交換合約（swaps），管轄權專屬聯邦，不容各州插手。
隨著 9 州訴訟同時進行、上訴法院意見書陸續遞出，這條對整個預測市場產業、乃至於與加密資產高度重疊的事件合約商業模式，都是一個需要持續盯緊的變數。

title: 馬斯克 Grok Bot 公測上線：24 小時不停工的 AI 同事，值得從 Claude、Codex 跳槽嗎？
summary:
SpaceXAI 推出 Grok Bot 公開測試版，每個代理人配一台專屬雲端電腦，直接操作軟體介面完成整套工 […]

〈馬斯克 Grok Bot 公測上線：24 小時不停工的 AI 同事，值得從 Claude、Codex 跳槽嗎？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
SpaceXAI 推出 Grok Bot 公開測試版，每個代理人配一台專屬雲端電腦，直接操作軟體介面完成整套工作流程，繞開 API 這道瓶頸。
（前情提要：馬斯克旗下 SpaceXAI 正式推出最強模型「Grok 4.5」！攜手 Cursor 猛攻 AI 編碼代理，完美整合 Office 辦公軟體）
（背景補充：馬斯克放話：Grok 4.6 兩週後上線、4.7 四週後上線，2 兆引數硬碰 Kimi K3）
8月 11 日，SpaceXAI（原 xAI）推出 Grok Bot 公開測試版。每一個 Bot 都配有一台專屬雲端電腦、是能直接操作軟體介面的 AI 代理人。SpaceXAI 把它定位成 24 小時不停工的「AI 同事」。
Grok Bot 在做什麼
Grok Bot 的核心賣點是三件事：記憶、協作、學習。
記憶指的是它跨對話保留脈絡，會回頭把沒做完的工作接著做，隨時間學會用戶的習慣；協作指的是多個 Bot 可以同時跑不同子任務，在群組對話裡互相交換脈絡，只有真的需要人做決策時才升級給人類；學習指的是用戶只要示範一次，Bot 就把整套流程存成可重複使用的 routine。
SpaceXAI 公布的內部使用案例包括：過夜跑潛在客戶研究與評分、Demo 前的環境檢查與修資料、維護 CRM 與組織圖、從 email 抽取報帳收據、重現並修復程式錯誤，目前已部署在工程、成長與行銷部門。
平台支援桌面版（macOS、Windows、Linux）與 iOS，Android 版本即將推出，等於先卡住生產力工具最集中的辦公場景。
繞過 API
要讓 AI 操作一套軟體，軟體廠商得先開放 API，或是接上 MCP。但問題是，大多數企業內部系統、老舊後台根本沒有乾淨的 API 可接。
Grok Bot 選擇了另一條路：直接操作用戶介面，登入 App 與網站、填表單、跑多步驟流程，跟真人員工的操作方式一模一樣。這代表它不需要等軟體廠商開放介接，對沒有 API 的舊系統也能上手。
首波開放僅限三種訂閱者：SuperGrok Heavy（每月 300 美元）、Cursor Ultra（每月 200 美元）、Cursor Teams Premium（每人每月 120 美元）。企業客戶目前只能排候補名單。馬斯克表示，更大規模的開放會綁在本週稍晚發布的 Grok 4.6。
有競爭力嗎？
不過「直接操作介面」這件事，Grok Bot 不是第一個做的，甚至不算早。
Anthropic 在 2024 年 10 月就推出 Claude Computer Use，直接控制整個桌面、操作任何人類能操作的應用程式；OpenAI 在 2026 年 4 月 23 日發布的 GPT-5.5，也已把電腦操作能力內建進模型本身，其 Operator 在複雜瀏覽器任務評測拿到約 87%；Google 的 Project Mariner 在 WebVoyager 拿下 83.5%，同一套能力也併進 Gemini API。
簡單來說，繞過 API 不是 Grok Bot 的專利，而是 2026 年代理人產品的入場券。
真正該問的是跑分。衡量電腦操作能力的 OSWorld-Verified 上，Claude 系列包辦前三，Mythos Preview 85.4%、Fable 5 85.0%、Opus 4.8 83.4%，GPT-5.5 是 78.7%，Gemini 3.5 Flash 78.4%，而 Grok Bot 到目前為止，沒有公布任何一項電腦操作的評測成績。
所以它的差異化不在「能不能操作介面」，而在三件事：每個 Bot 配專屬雲端電腦，用戶離線後工作繼續，以及 Cursor 這條現成的付費開發者通路。這場戰役目前 Grok Bot 是後發，不是先發。

title: 又一名 OpenAI 高管離職：從財務長幹到營運長的 8 年老臣在 IPO 前夕退場
summary:
OpenAI 營運長布萊德・萊特凱普宣布離職，卸下他一手打造的財務、法務、政府關係等營運骨架。此時正值 Ope […]

〈又一名 OpenAI 高管離職：從財務長幹到營運長的 8 年老臣在 IPO 前夕退場〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 營運長布萊德・萊特凱普宣布離職，卸下他一手打造的財務、法務、政府關係等營運骨架。此時正值 OpenAI 衝刺兆美元估值 IPO 的關鍵時刻，高層異動已是今年第三波。
（前情提要：OpenAI 已遞交 IPO 申請！繼 Anthropic、SpaceX 後叩關華爾街）
（背景補充：OpenAI 產品合併戰線！Greg Brockman 同時接管 ChatGPT、Codex 與開發者 API）
又一名任職 8 年的 OpenAI 高階主管，選在公司衝刺兆美元 IPO 的關鍵時刻離開。長年擔任營運長的布萊德（Brad Lightcap）於當地時間週二在 X 上公開一封寫給全體員工的信件，宣布自己即將卸任，「去開始一件新的事」。
這是 2026 年以來，OpenAI 第三波高層異動。4 月同一天，前產品長、後轉任科學部門負責人的 Kevin Weil 與 Sora 負責人 Bill Peebles 相繼離職；7 月，被視為公司二號人物、主導 AGI 開發的 Fidji Simo 宣布卸下全職角色。
i shared the message below with the openai team this morning. these decisions are never easy, but the talent and mission orientation of the openai team make me more optimistic than ever. 🤍
###
Team, it is bittersweet to share that I’ll be moving on from OpenAI to start…
— Brad Lightcap (@bradlightcap) August 11, 2026
八年，蓋好一間公司的骨架
萊特凱普 2018 年加入 OpenAI，先任財務長 4 年，2022 年升任營運長，今年稍早在一波高層職務調整中，轉任「特殊專案」負責人。在加入 OpenAI 之前，他與現任執行長 Sam Altman 在創投公司 Y Combinator 共事過。
在信中，他細數自己一手打造的部門：「我有幸建立了我們大多數營運與商業團隊的第一版，從財務、法務、人資、公司安全，到政府關係、合作夥伴，還有更多。」他說，這段旅程中最有成就感的部分，是看著這些團隊在優秀的主管手上逐漸成熟。
萊特凱普沒有交代下一步要做什麼，只寫下「過去幾個月，我一直在思考下一個階段，以及什麼可能擋在使命成功的路上」，並預告「會有更多訊息很快公布」。他強調自己「比任何時候都更相信 OpenAI」，只是換一個位置繼續參與。
根據外媒轉述他本人說法，他會於公司再留幾週才正式離開。
為什麼是現在
OpenAI 與競爭對手 Anthropic 已於 2026 年 6 月前後遞交機密 IPO 申請，外界預期 OpenAI 掛牌估值將站上 1 兆美元。但 IPO 意味著公司必須從一間靠故事融資的實驗室，變成一份能被公開市場檢驗的財報：董事會治理、法遵、揭露義務，一項都少不了。
而這些東西，恰好就是萊特凱普過去 8 年一手搭起來的骨架。演算法能力可以靠堆算力換到，但把一個模型實驗室變成一間扛得住投資人放大鏡檢視的公司，靠的是人，是財務、法務、政府關係這些看似無趣卻決定上市能不能過關的部門。
誰在補位？
Altman 至今沒有公開回應這波離職潮，OpenAI 官方也未說明萊特凱普卸任後，財務、法務、政府關係等業務會如何重新分工。
不過一間公司衝刺 IPO 前的人事穩定，通常是投資人審查的第一道題。萊特凱普選在這個時間點交棒，市場很難不解讀成某種訊號，無論是他個人職涯規劃使然，還是公司內部對上市路徑的判斷出現分歧，都值得後續觀察 OpenAI 如何在招股書公開前補齊這塊空缺。

title: ETF 狂吸金、比特幣卻漲不動！礦商、企業賣壓抵銷買盤，CPI 能否打破僵局？
summary:
儘管比特幣現貨 ETF 持續吸金，但來自礦工、企業大戶的獲利了結賣壓卻如影隨形，導致比特幣近期走勢橫盤悶局，連續約 5 周維持區間震盪，市場正等待新的催化劑打破僵局。

〈ETF 狂吸金、比特幣卻漲不動！礦商、企業賣壓抵銷買盤，CPI 能否打破僵局？〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
儘管比特幣現貨 ETF 持續吸金，但來自礦工、企業大戶的獲利了結賣壓卻如影隨形，導致比特幣近期走勢橫盤悶局，連續約 5 周維持區間震盪，市場正等待新的催化劑打破僵局。
過去 24 小時內，比特幣微幅下滑 0.6%，來到 63,500 美元附近。更值得注意的是，這款全球市值最大的加密貨幣，整個夏季幾乎都被困在 62,000 至 66,000 美元的狹幅區間內，難以動彈。
Wincent 資深主管 Paul Howard 表示，比特幣近期的價格走勢，基本上是 ETF 的穩定買盤，與礦工及 Strategy 場外交易（OTC）賣壓，兩股力量互相抵銷的結果。
Paul Howard 指出，加密貨幣整體交易量已萎縮至約 3 年低點，市場缺乏足夠的資金動能，來推動比特幣朝任何一個方向做出決定性突破。
Bitfinex 分析師也觀察到類似的資金流向。分析團隊表示，現貨 ETF 與專注投資比特幣的企業，雖然是市場上「對價格不敏感（無論漲跌皆持續買進）」的兩大穩定買盤，但近期礦企、囤幣公司企業增加賣出，抵銷了 ETF 部分買盤。這也充分解釋了為何在 ETF 大舉吸金、且全球風險性資產普遍反彈的環境下，比特幣上周卻僅僅擠出約 2% 的微弱漲幅。
CPI 成破局關鍵
市場下一個焦點落在美國通膨數據。美國將於周三公布最新消費者物價指數（CPI），很可能將成為打破比特幣盤整格局的關鍵。
STS Digital 管理合夥人 Jeff Anderson 表示，目前市場多空雙方的信心都不強，夏季流動性低迷更進一步放大觀望情緒。由於交易員等待貨幣政策方向，以及美國《數位資產市場明晰法案（CLARITY 法案）》後續進展，選擇權市場隱含波動率已大幅降至低檔。
這也意味著，一旦比特幣突破現有的震盪區間，無論向上或向下，都可能會引爆劇烈的單邊行情。 Jeff Anderson 指出，周三即將出爐的 CPI 將成為市場下一個嚴峻考驗，這也是聯準會（Fed）7 月會議後，主席 Kevin Warsh 就通膨議題發表談話以來，市場迎來的首個重要通膨數據。
展望後市，Paul Howard 預期，若無重大基本面利多刺激，這波盤整恐將延續至 9 月中旬；若《CLARITY 法案》取得進展，則可能成為下一個推動市場突破的重要因素。
此外，從衍生品部位來看，投資人目前仍維持相對充分的避險配置，顯示市場並未大舉押注比特幣即將突破，交易員整體仍偏向等待確認訊號。
如果比特幣遲遲無法脫離目前區間，接下來的季節性因素可能更加不利。
Jeff Anderson 指出，9 月向來是比特幣表現最疲軟的月份。 CoinGlass 數據顯示，自 2013 年以來，比特幣在 9 月份的平均跌幅達 4% 。

title: Trump says he switched planes after Nato summit because of possible threat
summary: But the president says the jet he boarded instead was at "greater risk" than the decoy Air Force One.
full_text:
Trump says he switched planes after Nato summit because of possible threat
- Published
President Donald Trump has confirmed that he secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month due to a possible threat.
"I go by Secret Service and the military. They wanted me to go in a different flight, different plane," Trump told reporters. "I just have to do what they say."
The revelation comes after reports that Trump boarded Air Force One on 8 July in view of television cameras before being transported to a military aircraft with the help of a catering truck.
The last-minute switch has raised questions about whether those left on the decoy plane were placed in danger, but Trump maintained on Tuesday the military jet he boarded instead was at "greater risk".
Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The New York Times reported that US intelligence had information of a person near the Nato summit who had been seen with a shoulder-fired missile.
Journalists and some White House staff on board did not know the US president had been smuggled out as part of an elaborate ruse in response to a possible Iranian threat.
Trump has previously said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara.
"I guess there was a threat out there," the president said during a visit aboard Air Force One to an event in Ohio on Tuesday. "I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats."
He added: "I have a lot of threats that you don't know about."
- Trump's dramatic plane swap hints at personal stakes of Iran war 
  - Published4 hours ago
- Inside the Secret Service 'shell game' to hide US presidents in plain sight 
  - Published8 hours ago
The clandestine manoeuvre last month came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war.
Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake".
On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport.
But according to the Washington Post, he slipped off Air Force One on to a catering truck that had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded.
He was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice-president.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs in an effort to make the flight appear normal, according to the newspaper.
Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board.
A media pool producer who was on the plane said they found it unusual when they were told to keep the window shades down. A photographer briefly opened a shade and reportedly was quickly told to close it.
The producer's comments were detailed in a report from the White House Correspondents' Association on Tuesday.
They also noted there appeared to have been two catering trucks at both the front and back of the plane when the press arrived, and that the media van had been too far back in the motorcade at the airport be able to take a photo of the president boarding.
Technically "Air Force One" is the call sign for any aircraft carrying the US president.
But on this occasion, the C-32A used the call sign "Reach 18", while the aircraft carrying the journalists continued to use "AF1" in order to keep up the ruse.
Remaining on the original aircraft were members of Trump's cabinet, according to the New York Times. The outlet, citing two anonymous officials, reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were on board.
Trump then flew to the UK en route to the US, where he reboarded the old Air Force One and was seen descending from the aircraft after it landed at RAF Mildenhall.
It is unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the legacy jet.
The president then transferred to the new Qatari-donated Air Force One to travel back to Washington.
During that flight, Trump spoke to reporters on board where he noted the threats posed by Iran but did not mention the earlier plane swap.
Asked why reporters had been told to lower the window shades on the plane from Turkey, Trump said at the time: "Because you're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags we have to deal with."
He said he had a "threat all the time" on his life, and that he is "number one" on Iran's "list".
Jose Zamora, regional director for the Americas for the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a statement that the Trump administration "has a responsibility to ensure that journalists covering the president are not unnecessarily exposed to danger".
"Reporters should be informed of credible security threats so they can make informed decisions about their safety," he added.
Additional reporting by Jessica Rawnsley

title: PM admits cost of living help is not enough and hints at further support
summary: The PM has announced a rake of measures to help people since taking office three weeks ago.
full_text:
PM admits cost of living help is not enough and hints at further support
- Published
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he accepts his announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.
Burnham told BBC's Wake up to Money he will deliver an "accumulation of smaller things" that "combine to take the pressure down" on household budgets.
He spoke of an overhaul of train fares and "more public control" of energy, water and housing but did not give details on how he would bring this about.
Burnham has made a number of announcements to help people with the cost of living since taking office, including the removal of VAT from domestic energy bills and bringing forward an already planned end to 'subscription traps'.
Asked whether the changes he had announced were not significant to people struggling, he said: "I can accept criticism that this isn't enough, because I wouldn't say it's enough.
"But I take an approach to politics where I do what I can, when I can. Just take that little bit of pressure off and address an issue that you know needs addressing.
"It's not the end of the story," he added.
The prime minister, who is embarking on a tour of the UK while Parliament is in recess, said he believed "more public control of essential services" such as water, energy and housing, "would mean we could get to a more substantial answer to the cost of living crisis".
On water, he said it would not be easy to reverse the privatisation of water companies in England and Wales that took place in the 1980s.
"But very much, I'm looking at what can be done. Same with energy."
He also said that, following the return of rail operators to public ownership, he wanted to "remodel the rail fares so that we can get more public benefit for people".
Burnham said he has asked Chancellor John Healey to look at what the government can do further on the cost of living in the upcoming Budget, on 28 October, and that Healey has said it will be his "main focus".
Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" – which will limit how much the government has to spend.
One major think tank recently warned that he will have to raise taxes or cut spending to meet Burnham's pledges on defence and the cost of living.
Labour's manifesto pledge was to not increase taxes for working people — including income tax, VAT and National Insurance Contributions (NICs) - which Burnham has said he will uphold.
He will likely face pressure to address rising costs for businesses, after previous budgets under Rachel Reeves saw employer's national insurance and minimum wages go up.
Last month Burnham said pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England would be given a 20% cut to business rates from April, calling it a "first step" to help the industry.
He told the BBC he accepted the national insurance hike had added pressure on businesses, and that the government would look at business rates "more broadly".
Burnham said: "I would like to bring down the cost of doing businesses. I want to make high streets more vibrant across the country. I know that cannot be done by simply wishing it."
But he said he did not want to "at this point, start making commitments".
"Those are for the Budget."

title: British driver who broke sound barrier sets new speed record
summary: Andy Green set the fastest time ever recorded in a hydrogen-powered car, reaching 406mph (654km/h).
full_text:
British driver who broke sound barrier sets new speed record
- Published
A British driver who was the first person to break the sound barrier in a car on land has set a new speed record, this time in a hydrogen-powered vehicle.
Andy Green, a 64-year-old retired Royal Air Force pilot, reached a speed of 406mph (654km/h) at the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, the fastest a hydrogen-powered car has ever travelled.
Green's record was measured as an average of two runs in a car powered by two hydrogen internal combustion engines, with a combined 1,600 brake horsepower (bhp).
In 1997, Green drove the jet-powered ThrustSSC across Nevada's Black Rock Desert at 763mph (1,228km/h), making him the first, and still the only person, to break the sound barrier on land.
Twenty years ago, Green also set a world land speed record for a diesel vehicle in the JCB Dieselmax, attaining a speed of over 350mph (563km/h).
The new record, set in JCB's Hydromax vehicle, surpassed the previous official hydrogen combustion title set in 2004 (185.5mph) by more than double the speed.
"Setting a world land speed record with hydrogen power, 20 years after Dieselmax, is a huge privilege. This record is a huge achievement by a world class team and superb technology," Green said.
Last month, Green said his wife's encouragement was crucial in persuading him to accept the challenge after getting a call from JCB chairman Lord Anthony Bamford.
Lord Anthony said: "Twenty years ago we came to Bonneville with JCB Dieselmax and showed what British engineering could do with diesel power. Today we have done it again - this time with engines powered by hydrogen."
The company had developed the Hydromax car in an attempt to set a new record for a hydrogen-powered vehicle.
In May, the Hydromax reached 208mph (335km/h) during testing at RAF Wittering in Cambridgeshire.

title: Oil prices rise as attacks dent hopes for Strait of Hormuz reopening
summary: Brent crude climbs as renewed violence dampens hopes for a return to stability in energy markets.
full_text:
Oil prices rise as attacks dent hopes for Strait of Hormuz reopening
Brent crude climbs as renewed violence dampens hopes for a return to stability in energy markets.
Oil prices have jumped as attacks on shipping in the Middle East cast doubt on prospects for a breakthrough in negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent crude rose more than 2 percent overnight into Wednesday, taking the international benchmark to close to $90 a barrel.

- list 2 of 4Cargo ship in flames after Houthi attack in Bab al-Mandeb strait
