title: Home Depot CEO taking temporary medical leave, two top execs to run the retailer
summary: Home Depot's CEO Ted Decker is taking a temporary medical leave of absence that's expected to last a few months.
full_text:
Home Depot CEO Ted Decker is taking a "temporary medical leave of absence" for the next few months and the company has appointed two top deputies to lead until he returns, the retailer announced on Wednesday.
Ann-Marie Campbell, Home Depot's senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will oversee day-to-day operations while finance chief Richard McPhail will run financial management and the Pro business, the company said.
Lead independent director of the board, Greg Brenneman, will take over as chair of the board during Decker's leave. The board of directors made the appointments but they were "in alignment with Decker's recommendation," the company said.
"The Home Depot has the best management team in retail. Both Ann-Marie and Richard are strong, seasoned executives who have worked together for more than 20 years," Brenneman said in a news release. "We are confident in Ann-Marie's and Richard's ability to lead the company during this time, and we look forward to Ted's return."
The announcement comes just under a week before the company is set to announce fiscal second quarter earnings on Tuesday. Home Depot didn't provide further details on Decker's condition.
Campbell, 61, has worked for Home Depot since 1985, starting as a cashier before working her way up to EVP of stores and operations. McPhail, 56, has been Home Depot's chief financial officer since September 2019 and joined the company in 2005.
Both of the executives aren't receiving additional pay for taking on the increased responsibilities, according to a securities filing.

title: Everything announced at Made by Google ’26: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag, and tons of Gemini features
summary: From the Pixel 11 series and a brand new competitor to Apple’s AirTag, here are all the announcements from the Made by Google 2026 event.
full_text:
Google is holding its Made by Google 2026 event on Wednesday, unveiling the Pixel 11 series, the Pixel Watch 5, and even a competitor to Apple’s AirTag. The tech giant also used the event to show off new Gemini-powered features across its devices.
Gemini gets more useful on Pixel
Google spent a good portion of the event talking about Gemini and other AI features coming to its devices.
One of the more notable accessibility updates is an expansion of “Live Transcribe” to support American Sign Language. Using the Pixel Camera, users can have sign language translated into text, giving people another way to communicate without relying on typing.
Google also introduced “Rambler,” a new voice-input feature designed to better understand the way people actually talk. Rather than requiring carefully phrased sentences, Rambler is designed to handle run-on sentences, filler words, and less structured speech while still figuring out what the user is trying to say.
There are a few smaller additions, too. “Circle to Search” can now be accessed more directly from the Pixel Camera, allowing users to identify objects, search for things in the distance, translate text, or ask questions about what’s around them without leaving the camera experience.
Pixel 11
The standard Pixel 11 gets a redesigned camera bar that is thinner than the one on the previous generation. Google says the new camera bar is more than 40% thinner and now uses an all-glass surface that stretches across the width of the phone. Google is also increasing the base storage to 256GB, doubling the previous starting capacity.
The starting price for the new model is set at $899, reflecting a $100 increase compared to the Pixel 10. This price hike comes with the decision to drop the 128GB storage option. Plus, the ongoing RAM supply shortage plays a part in this increase.
The Pixel 11 will be available in Frost, Hibiscus, Pistachio, and Obsidian.
Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL
Google is making durability a bigger part of the Pro lineup. The company says the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL have improved drop resistance and a new anti-scratch display coating that provides more than twice the scratch resistance of the Pixel 10 Pro models.
The Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099, compared to $999 for the Pixel 10 Pro.
The phones are available in Canyon, Fog, Olive, and Obsidian. Notably, this year’s Obsidian option gets an all-matte finish.
Pixel 11 Pro Fold
Google says the new foldable is nearly 10% lighter and almost 1mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. It also has slimmer bezels, a 48-megapixel main camera, and 30x Super Zoom.
The company is also building on the IP68 water and dust resistance introduced with the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold uses a glass-fiber composite back cover designed to better withstand cracking, while a redesigned hinge offers additional protection for the inner display. Google says the changes make the model three times more durable than its predecessor.
The Pixel 11 Pro Fold comes in Olive and Obsidian.
Google takes aim at Apple’s AirTag
Google finally has its own tracking tag. Called Pixel Tag, the small device is designed to help people keep tabs on things such as keys, wallets and luggage. It connects to Android’s Find Hub network, allowing users to see the tag’s location through the Find Hub app (similar to Apple’s Find My).
The tag, priced at $29 (or $99 for a four-pack), can also be located from a Pixel Watch. Pixel Buds users can ask Gemini to find or ring a Pixel Tag, adding a voice-controlled option for tracking something down.
Pixel Watch 5
The Pixel Watch 5 is getting several health-related updates. The Google Health app will provide monthly summaries of blood pressure trends, with the goal of helping users notice patterns over time. It will also provide monthly summaries of insulin resistance trends.
The 41mm Pixel Watch 5 starts at $399, while the 45mm version starts at $429. Google is also offering a Stephen Curry edition for $579, with an exclusive design built for workouts. (This is featured in the image above.)
Meanwhile, the Pixel Buds Pro is arriving in a new Olive color.

title: Google’s Quick Share adds a tap-to-share mode
summary: Google's Quick Share feature is getting a tap-to-share mode for quickly exchanging contacts, photos, videos, and more.
full_text:
Alongside its Pixel 11 product launches on Wednesday, Google announced it is making fast sharing between its devices easier, with an improved version of Google’s Quick Share feature (similar to Apple’s AirDrop), rolling out now.
The feature will now allow Android users to send their contact information, photos, videos, and more with a tap.
To use the new version of Quick Share, you’ll bring your Android device close to another compatible Android device for what Google calls an “instant, two-way exchange.” Plus, you’ll be able to share photos or videos from the phone’s Share Sheet, then tap devices together to make the exchange.
The addition brings the Pixel lineup more on par with the iPhone, as it follows the launch of the NFC-powered NameDrop feature in Apple’s iOS 17, which similarly allowed iPhone users to share contacts, photos, or videos by touching phones.
The Quick Share update is rolling out starting on Wednesday on Pixel 6 and newer devices, and will soon arrive on the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8, and Flip8 as well. More devices will be supported by year-end, Google says.

title: Google’s Pixel 11 lineup offer fewer hardware changes, but much more Gemini
summary: Google Pixel 11 Series starts $100 costlier than the last year, but offers 256GB base storage
full_text:
For the last few years, Google’s Pixel has been a showcase of new AI features, with few hardware changes from the previous year’s devices. Similarly, the Pixel 11 series isn’t too different in design and internals from its predecessor.
However, this year’s devices have more Gemini features to complete tasks in the background, including a new Wispr Flow-like transcription feature, a live translation feature that works across content, and a new camera feature that captures the right frames.
AI advances on the Pixel 11
With this year’s Pixel 11 series launch, Google is thinking more agentic AI to complete your tasks. With Gemini, U.S.-based users will be able to order groceries, book rides, or get coffee, for instance. Plus, Gemini can call businesses on users’ behalf for table reservations or appointments. Google said that users can take over or stop tasks at any point in time and also review transcripts for AI-operated calls.
Over the next few weeks, a new slate of connected apps will be able to work with Gemini to get things done, including Granola, Otter.ai, Wix, Fever, Get Your Guide, Localiza, OpenTable (UK), Ticketmaster, iHeartRadio, Pandora, Angi, Thumbtack, and Zocdoc.
The company has also evolved the “Magic Cue” feature from last year to use Gemini, which proactively surfaces contextual information, to now display information from across your apps to help you find suggestions for things like a dinner spot or show.
In May, Google announced a dictation product called Rambler to take on competitors like Wispr Flow and Aqua. Now, that product is making its way to the Pixel phones.
The new Pixel series phones have some other helpful features that might be handy for daily usage, too. First, the device can translate videos, podcasts, and voice messages in the target language. The company is also making its “Circle to Search” gesture-based feature available directly in the camera, something that Apple also did in iOS 27 by making Siri available in the camera.
What’s more, Google is adding an accessibility feature to the camera, which uses Gemini to translate sign language into text to help people communicate with others who have hearing impairments. And the company has redesigned the live transcribe interface for improved communication.
Camera features
Google also added a few AI tricks embedded into its camera. One feature is called “Magic Capture,” which picks the best frames out of hundreds of frames it captures between when users press start and end. The idea is to take a video and get photos as a byproduct. Google said that the feature also auto-crops and unblurs the frames to make them ready for sharing.
The company has upgraded its super zoom from 100x to 120x for Pro phones, and from 20x to 30x for the base Pixel 11. With the new devices, users will be able to create custom looks for the camera, which are specialized filters that appear when users are snapping images.
The Pro phones are also getting faster capture with a feature called “Instant Night Sight,” which takes 4.5x less time than the previous-gen phone’s Night Sight. Google enhanced video shooting, too, with support for 8K resolution with video boost and better stability.
For creators, Google added a “creator suite” mode in video settings, which lets you use Pixel 11 devices as a teleprompter while shooting clips. When you are done shooting, the clip is saved in a dedicated folder, making it easier to find for editing.
Hardware upgrades
All the Pixel phones now run the latest Tensor G6 processor, which has 20% better power efficiency and 
allows for 25% faster browsing, as per Google. Plus, it lets users take faster low-light photos with Night Sight Instant. 
The new image signal processing on the chip also enables 120x magic zoom on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. The company said that the new processors run the latest models with lower latency, but didn’t offer any specific metrics.
The display size on all phones is the same, but the Pro models get a slightly brighter display, which could be helpful in the daylight.
Google said Pro models get an updated main camera sensor that takes higher-quality photos than the previous generation without specifying any numbers. It also said the new telephoto sensor allows for 32% more light while capturing an image.
London-based startup Nothing made its phones recognizable by Glyph bars and then a Glyph interface. Google is not that extravagant, but it has now placed an LED light on the back, which is built around the flashlight. This acts as an indicator for calls or messages from favorite contacts when Gemini is thinking or listening.
All these devices are available to pre-order starting today and will start with a base storage of 256GB.
The Pixel 11 starts at $899, the 11 Pro starts at $1,099, and the 11 Pro XL starts at $1,299. (The prices of the Pixel 11 and the Pixel 11 Pro are the same as last year’s 256GB models, but you could buy a 128 GB model at that time with a $100 lower price tag.)
With the rising prices of components, the company has bumped the price of the top model by $100 compared to the Pixel 10 XL.
A new lineup of Pixel 11 accessories is also arriving alongside the phones, including new Pixelsnap cases (which now include clear) and Pixelsnap Ring Stand colors.

title: Google unveils the Pixel Watch 5 with a smarter Gemini and advanced health monitoring
summary: The new smartwatch, which starts at $399, can track blood pressure patterns and insulin resistance, as well as deliver personalized help and better sleep tracking.
full_text:
At its Made by Google event on Wednesday, Google will unveil the Pixel Watch 5 with a smarter Gemini experience, as well as advanced fitness and health monitoring. The new smartwatch, which starts at $399, can track blood pressure patterns and insulin resistance, as well as deliver personalized help and better sleep tracking.
Google says it’s designed the watch to deliver personalized and proactive help right when it’s needed. For example, the watch will proactively suggest relevant actions or information based on a text message’s context, like instantly pulling up a smoothie place your sister sent you.
You can raise your wrist to ask Gemini a question, handle requests like finding a nearby lunch spot with navigation, or use Gemini offline to manage timers, alarms, and workouts with your voice.
The watch will also dynamically surface timely updates right at the bottom of the watch face, like flight info, ETAs, and other helpful reminders.
As for the new health features, the tech giant says the smartwatch uses sensors and machine learning to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart. Google says the feature was tested against 24-hour blood pressure monitors and uses an advanced waveform model trained on more than 1 billion minutes of data from over 500,000 people.
The insulin resistance feature is designed to identify changes in metabolic health that may be associated with insulin resistance and an increased risk of developing prediabetes or type 2 diabetes. The feature combines signals from sleep, heart rate, physical activity, and other health data. A large sensor model then analyzes these signals over time to identify long-term changes in insulin resistance.
Google will give users a summary of their blood pressure and insulin resistance trends every month.
There’s also a new feature that can detect a persistent drop in oxygen saturation and will contact emergency services if the watch determines that a breathing emergency may be occurring. This feature is launching in select European countries before expanding to additional regions.
Additionally, the watch’s sleep-stage tracking is 15% more accurate and there’s also a new bedtime watch face that reduces nighttime distractions. A new “Smart Wake” feature wakes users at an optimal point in their sleep cycle, while a new sleep breathing quality metric tracks minute-by-minute changes in blood oxygen levels.
As for fitness, Google says the Pixel Watch 5 delivers its most accurate GPS route tracking yet, with route mapping that’s two times more accurate than previous generations. The improved accuracy is designed to provide users with more precise workout and running data, including a closer match between your recorded route and the actual course.
The Pixel Watch 5 features the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 platform and has 12% more CPU performance and 50% more RAM than the previous platform. Google says the Watch 5 is 20% faster overall.
The Pixel Watch five supports up to 40 hours of battery life and is available in new colors, including Canyon Fog and Olive. The 41mm version starts at $399, while the 44mm starts at $429. The smartwatch is available for pre-order starting Wednesday and will be available on August 20.

title: Google takes on AirTag with the new $29 Pixel Tag
summary: Google’s new Pixel Tag taps into its Find Hub network to help users track lost keys, bags, and other items.
full_text:
Alongside its announcement of a new lineup of Pixel 11 smartphones, Google on Wednesday introduced its answer to Apple’s AirTag. At its Made by Google ’26 event, the company will unveil a new product designed for keeping track of your valuable items: the $29 Google Pixel Tag.
Similar to how Apple’s AirTag leverages its network of iPhones to find lost devices, the new Pixel Tag uses Google’s Find Hub network, which taps into Android devices around the world. Android users can add the tag to their phone’s built-in Android Find Hub, which is already used to help users find their lost Android smartphones and other devices, similar to Apple’s Find My.
Helpfully, you can locate and ring your Pixel Tag directly from your Pixel Watch, too, not just your phone.
Where the Pixel Tag differs from AirTag is in its look and feel.
Apple’s lost-item finder is small, round, and engravable; Google opted for a slimmer, elongated device instead. Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1 inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8 inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height).
By weight, the two competitors are comparable, as the Pixel Tag weighs 0.4 ounces with the battery, and the AirTag comes in at 0.39 oz.
Both are also rated IP67 for splash, water, and dust resistance, meaning they can withstand submersion in a maximum depth of 1 meter for up to 30 minutes.
Taking other cues from AirTag, the Pixel Tag offers connectivity via Bluetooth and Ultra Wideband for precision finding; however, it doesn’t include NFC. Pixel Tag has a built-in speaker to help you find the lost device when nearby, and it’s powered by the user-replaceable CR2032 coin cell battery — the same used by the AirTag. This allows the Pixel Tag to work for roughly a year before the battery needs to be replaced.
Designed to be attached to items like keychains and bags, the Pixel Tag will cost $29 for a one-pack and $99 for a four-pack when it becomes available for purchase on November 11, 2026.

title: Google’s new Pixel 11 Pro Fold offers a stronger build and brighter screens
summary: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold will cost $1,899
full_text:
Samsung’s short and wide foldable is the talk of the town, but Google is not experimenting with its design with today’s unveiling of the new Pixel 11 Fold, which appears largely unchanged on the outside. The company said that the new foldable is stronger and lighter than the previous-gen phone, but it’s also costlier.
Google said that it developed a new, stronger hinge for this year’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold. It’s also adding a Super Actua display to the outer display with 3,600 nits of peak brightness. Both the inner and outer displays are 20% brighter than its predecessor, according to the company.
There is a bit of a battery downgrade, however, as it now offers a 4,750 mAh capacity battery instead of 5,015 mAh from last year’s model. On the plus side, this is probably the reason why the phone is 1mm thinner and roughly 20 grams lighter.
Another small upgrade on the charging front is that the new foldable supports 25W wireless charging.
The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is getting an updated 48-megapixel sensor that pulls in more light for more detailed photos in different lighting conditions. Because of the new G6 Tensor chip and the updated image processor, the phone can digitally zoom at 30x, up from 20x.
The device will be available in both the Olive and Obsidian colors, and will cost $1,899.

title: Google reveals 2026 hardware lineup: Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, and Pixel Tag
summary: Google focuses more on AI and curated experiences than spec upgrades in 2026.
full_text:
Google has revealed its Pixel phone hardware for 2026, and you won’t be surprised. The Pixel 11 series looks a lot like last year’s lineup, featuring an evolution of the design Google adopted with the Pixel 9. There are some minor tweaks, a few new hardware goodies, and yes, even more Gemini-powered AI. The new phones are joined by an updated Pixel Watch 5 with much the same story, as well as Google’s first in-house tracker device, the Pixel Tag. And you can place orders for all of Google’s new hardware today.
The Pixel 11 series is clearly the star of the show—you might even call it the highlight… erm, sorry, HiLight. Just as the leaks predicted, Google’s most notable hardware innovation for the 2026 Pixel phones is the return of the notification LED (sort of).
HiLight is available on the Pro phones, so the base model Pixel will remain unilluminated. HiLight consists of a ring of RGB LEDs inside the flash assembly on the back of the phone. It lights up when you’re talking to Gemini, so you don’t have to look at the screen of your phone to know you’ve been heard or that the AI is working. Thus, it makes the most sense when the phone is lying face down.
The multicolored LEDs can also alert you to an incoming call from specific contacts. This works for both standard phone calls and voice calls in WhatsApp. But it’s only those apps. It sounds like you can’t use HiLight for any other kind of notification for other apps—not even for a text in Google Messages. Notification LEDs can be useful, but the ones we had years back were infinitely more configurable. HiLight is locked down in modern Google fashion, and I wouldn’t be surprised if we see more HiLight features drip-fed in future Pixel Drops.
You may also notice the camera bars are a bit different this year. Google is keeping this distinctive design element, but the bar has shrunk considerably on the base model. The Pixel 11’s bar now rises just a couple of millimeters above the back of the phone, making it a bit less awkward to drop in your pocket. All the bars now have edge-to-edge glass, dropping the metal inlay that previously housed the flash and thermometer. The latter, unsurprisingly, is gone this year.
The displays on this year’s Pixel phones are brighter. While the base model remains at 3,000 nits, the Pro phones have all risen to 3,600 nits. Google also says it has new glass on the phones that is twice as resistant to scratching.
It’s not all upgrades, though. For the past few years, Google’s battery capacity has been inching upward, but the Pixel 11 series bizarrely reverses that trend. The three flat phones all have slightly lower capacity. It’s not a huge difference—under 100 mAh for each—but that’s still moving in the wrong direction when one of the primary complaints about Pixel phones is the middling battery life. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is even stranger, dropping a full 200 mAh of capacity to land at 4,806 mAh. However, it is a little lighter and thinner.
For what it’s worth, Google is claiming the same “24+ hours” of total battery life on the new phones. There is at least a new “Extreme Charging Mode” that keeps charging wattage higher for longer. This generates more heat, but the chipset will slow down to compensate so you don’t overheat.
Google probably figured it could get away with smaller batteries because the new Tensor G6 uses less juice. The company claims a 20 percent boost in power efficiency, along with 25 percent faster browsing and 15 percent faster app loading. However, this is really all Google is saying about Tensor G6—there are no official chip specs. Based on leaks, Tensor G6 is most likely a custom seven-core Arm chip, which has one fewer CPU core than the Tensor G5 had.
Google’s Pro phones continue to have an ultra-wideband radio, and Google finally has a product that can take advantage of it with the $29 Pixel Tag. It’s a location tracker like the Apple AirTag or any number of similar but less popular products on the Android side. This Bluetooth beacon uses the Find Hub network of Android phones to report its location, which has been slow to improve compared to Apple’s network. Devices with ultra-wideband, like the Pro Pixels, can use that signal for more precise finding when the tag is nearby.
The new Google phones will run Android 17 with the customary seven years of updates (not that Google likes to talk about versions much anymore)—it’s much more interested in talking about all the things Gemini can do on Android. Google has expanded the slate of apps that support automation, allowing you to task Gemini with things like ordering a ride or shopping. Gemini can also place calls to businesses on the Pixel 11, and you’ll get a transcript of the conversation to keep tabs on the robot.
Rambler, which Google announced a few months ago, will be front and center on the Pixel 11. This voice-to-text feature is steeped in generative AI. It doesn’t directly transcribe your words, but rather will summarize to clean up repetitions, streamline corrections, and remove the occasional “um” or “uh.”
The camera experience is where Pixels really shine, and Google has paid some attention to that with the 2026 lineup. The Pixel 11 and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold have a new primary sensor. It’s the same resolution at 48 MP, but it’s slightly larger to collect more light. Google also expanded digital zoom on those phones to 30x. The Pro versions have been boosted to 120x digital zoom.
There are some new software camera features, too. Magic Capture takes the guesswork out of when to press the shutter button. When activated, this mode will automatically take a video and a high-quality still photo at the right moment, leveraging the phone’s image processing to crop and remove blur. The Pro phones also lean on the Tensor G6’s enhanced AI processing to power Instant Night Sight. It’s not clear how “instant” it will be, but the gist is that low-light photos will be faster.
Camera Looks is probably the most interesting addition to the Pixel camera. Google’s HDR+ processing is generally great, but Pixels don’t include many customization options. Camera Looks will allow you to create styles that change the aesthetics of your photos. There will be some pre-crafted looks on the phone, and you can create your own. These aren’t just filters applied to the photos after processing—Camera Looks are implemented in the HDR+ processing pipeline. Google also notes that Camera Looks still support Real Tone, so no one’s skin will look out of whack even with highly stylized looks.
You’ll pay a little more for the new Google phones, but that’s par for the course in 2026. The prices are up $100 across the board, starting at $899 for the Pixel 11 and going up to $1,899 for the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. You can preorder now, and phones will ship on August 20. The Pixel Tag won’t launch until November 11.
Pixel Watch 5: More AI and health tracking
Google’s new wearable isn’t reinventing the wheel, either. It looks identical, and the battery capacity is just a smidge larger. The dimensions are identical, the charger is unchanged (thankfully), and it still comes in both 41 mm and 45 mm sizes with domed “Actual 360” OLED screens.
The watches run the Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated, which is similar to the non-accelerated version from last year’s watches. Google says the new watches are about 20 percent faster, and, unsurprisingly, it’s using that extra speed to do more on-device AI processing.
Google is leaning into proactive insights with the Pixel Watch 5, which can suggest actions or content based on the notifications that arrive. The watch might suggest locations or reminders based on messages. Some of the new watch faces can also display Gemini-powered content, like flight info or arrival times based on your data. You can also use Gemini offline to manage basics like timers and workout tracking by voice.
Google also promises a big improvement to health and fitness tracking with the Pixel Watch 5. The wearable can tr

title: Researchers found a way to hijack devices through Zoom screen sharing
summary: A public AI tool found the dangerous Zoom flaw in under 20 prompts.
full_text:
As AI models gain advanced capabilities to find vulnerabilities in software, develop ways to exploit them, and even carry out autonomous hacking sprees, researchers offered a sobering new example on Tuesday, disclosing vulnerabilities in the video conferencing platform Zoom that could have been exploited to take over targets’ devices. Anyone on a call that involved screen sharing, whether participants or the host, would have been vulnerable to a silent attack that could be carried out with no indication and no interaction from the victim.
Researchers from the digital defense firm A Security say the bug was discovered in early June using publicly available AI models, and that it took fewer than 20 prompts to uncover the vulnerabilities and create a working attack. Zoom issued a security advisory on Tuesday, including details about fixes the company has already begun rolling out to address the flaws, which affected devices running all operating systems that Zoom supports—Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android.
“What is interesting for us and what we believe is dangerous is the democratization of these capabilities—the barrier to entry is dropping rapidly,” A Security cofounder Omer Gull told WIRED ahead of the disclosure. “Before it would have taken a team of five people maybe six months with a lot of refining and iteration to find this. Now people can reach the same results with under 20 prompts. And Zoom is an important type of target because people assume trust when using it. They don’t see it as a threat.”
The vulnerabilities were specifically in the protocol used to facilitate real-time annotation during screen sharing. The researchers say that their AI bug hunting systems specifically delved into this component because, like human bug hunters, they have been trained that convoluted and obscure functions often contain overlooked vulnerabilities. This is particularly true with proprietary, closed-source software. An established company like Zoom presumably does extensive code review and vetting on all components and functions, but without the benefit of public, open review, esoteric yet complex features like annotation are more likely to contain mistakes.

title: Formula E finds a new home on Disney+, ESPN+
summary: The deal starts with the arrival of the GEN4 car and 2026/2027 season this December.
full_text:
Formula E is set to make a big change in terms of visibility when season 12 gets underway this December. It has signed a new multiyear deal to broadcast the sport on Disney+ and ESPN+ in 144 countries, with live coverage of each entire ePrix, from practice through qualifying to the race. The new media deal means that here in the US, Formula E will be shown on ESPN+ from next season; since 2023, the sport has been shown live on Roku.
“This is a landmark moment for Formula E and reflects the incredible momentum behind our Championship,” said Formula E’s CEO Jeff Dodds. “Disney’s unrivaled global reach and storytelling will introduce Formula E to millions of new fans while bringing them closer than ever to the drama, innovation, and excitement of electric racing. As we enter the GEN4 era, this provides an exceptional platform to accelerate our global growth and continue building one of the world’s most exciting sports properties.”
Actually, the new deal will mean fewer eyeballs on the sport, at least here in the US. More than 100 million US households subscribe to Roku (as of April this year), whereas ESPN+ has been losing subscribers since peaking at the end of 2023 and is now down to roughly 24 million households in the US.

title: Google’s Pixel Watch 5 Can Now Detect Breathing Emergencies
summary: The company is also adding blood pressure and insulin resistance trends as proactive monitoring tools in the Google Health app.
full_text:
Google's first smartwatch debuted just 4 years ago, and at the time, the company went to great lengths to stress the accuracy of the Pixel Watch's heart rate sensor. Even if Google was late to the wearable party compared to peers like Apple and Samsung, that focus on heart rate seems to be paying off with new features that are yet to be seen on competing products.
On Wednesday, Google introduced the latest generation of its smartwatch, the Pixel Watch 5 (alongside the Pixel 11 smartphone family). The hot new health feature? Breathing Emergency Detection. Similar to the first-of-its-kind Loss of Pulse Detection feature introduced on the Pixel Watch 3, this new capability can be triggered by a variety of factors, like drug toxicity, accidents, severe pneumonia, and choking.
“Using a combination of data from the advanced sensors, including a PPG, accelerometer, and barometer, we've designed an AI-based algorithm running on device to detect a persistent drop in oxygen saturation and then call Emergency Services for you and even share your location,” says Francis Hoe, a product manager on Google's Pixel Watch team.
This feature hasn't been cleared by the Food and Drug Administration, which is why it's not launching in the US at the moment; Google says it's working with regulators to expand availability. It will only be available in select markets in the European Union to start. Google also says it's not intended for people with preexisting respiratory conditions and isn't designed to diagnose or treat medical conditions.
You also don't need a new Pixel Watch 5 to take advantage; Google's bringing this feature to the Pixel Watch 4 as well. And two other big new capabilities are also coming to older devices: blood pressure and insulin resistance trends. These are coming to the Google Health app, and will be available for anyone with a Fitbit Air, Pixel Watch 3, Watch 4, or Watch 5 later this fall.
“It might have felt strange—why are we harping about heart rate accuracy so much—back then,” Sandeep Waraich, senior director of Wearables at Google, tells WIRED. “We kept investing in that, and now it's very improved, because all these large sensor models can detect these signatures, insulin resistance, blood pressure trends—but underneath, they need a really capable raw signal.”
Google is placing these features into a new umbrella category called Health Guardian, which includes existing features such as irregular rhythm notifications, high/low heart-rate notifications, Loss of Pulse, and Sleep Breathing Quality. The idea is to put these capabilities in a place where users can easily see what they have turned on, similar to Google's Personal Safety app on Pixel phones, which shows features like Emergency SOS, Safety Check, and Car Crash Detection in one place.
Many of these Health Guardian features will deliver monthly reports based on the 24/7 passive monitoring, with Google then offering suggestions on what you can take action on to improve your health. You can either consult its new AI-powered Health Coach, or send your data to your physician.
The blood pressure and insulin resistance trends features are meant to help people proactively monitor these potential health issues before it's too late—high blood pressure is the leading risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Last year, Apple debuted hypertension notifications—when the watch detects high blood pressure—for select Apple Watch models, and Samsung offers blood pressure monitoring on its smartwatches as well (it requires monthly calibration with a cuff).
“We've been collecting, opt-in for many years with Fitbit, a large model of the PPG signals that are coming through from the user, and we have an understanding of different conditions that users have,” says Rishi Chandra, vice president for Google Health. “If we have data of people who have elevated levels of blood pressure, there's a unique signature marking that, and we can match it to, for example, an arm cuff for prediction of high blood pressure.”
Daniel Jones, former president of the American Heart Association, says there are no wrist devices the AHA recommends for monitoring blood pressure. Arm cuffs remain the gold standard for diagnosis and guiding medication; however, the AHA noted late last year that cuffless devices like smart rings and smartwatches “show great promise” as alternatives and have “the potential to transform” hypertension care.

title: 4 New Camera Tricks on Google’s Latest Pixel 11 Smartphones
summary: From Magic Capture and Instant Night Sight to a built-in teleprompter, here’s a look at a few camera features on Google’s new Pixel 11 series.
full_text:
Google's Pixel Camera chief, Isaac Reynolds, thinks year-to-year upgrades to smartphone cameras are still critical, even though some detractors think they’re passé.
“A person who is a casual photographer and desperately wants to be a hobbyist—they're never going to break that ceiling unless you give them the tools," he says. "The features that others call ‘meh’—for some people, those features are life-changing."
Take the 30X Super Res Zoom on the Pixel 7 Pro from 2022, which uses machine learning to stitch together multiple frames in a digitally zoomed photo to give you a result that’s much sharper than you're used to. Reynolds says that because of this feature, Google now sees people using 30X zoom dramatically more than before.
The new Pixel 11 Pro, announced today, can zoom up to 120X, though in addition to the digital stitching, it relies on AI-generated pixels to fill in some details. Reynolds says maybe having that capability is enough to get someone interested in, say, wildlife photography. After experimenting on their phone, they’d be ready to invest in a professional camera and a big zoom lens.
“There's a reason I work on low light and zoom every single year," he says. "Because no matter how much I do it, when I do the user study with thousands of respondents, people always want more."
Every year, Google debuts a new Pixel phone, and every year, there's a slew of new camera tricks—largely powered by software wizardry—to deliver better photos than ever before. Last year, there was the Pro Res Zoom, which bumped up digital zoom on the Pixel 10 Pro to 100X. Two years before that, Google introduced “Add Me,” which lets two people take a group photo together without asking a stranger to take the pic for them.
For the Pixel 11 series, Google has demonstrated a handful of upgrades that can drastically alter the look of your photos, and even take some of the work out of capturing photos. Here's a closer look at a few top new camera capabilities on the Pixel 11 series.
Magic Capture
So you want to capture a video of an important event—a concert of your favorite band, singing happy birthday to a loved one as a waiter brings a cake over, or your kid's recital. Too often, you see people holding their phone up during these milestones, trying to capture the moment, instead of being present. That's the problem Google's new Magic Capture feature is trying to solve.
This is a new mode that sits next to the Photo/Video tab in the Pixel camera app. Select Magic Capture, and it will kick off a two-minute video recording. Then, rather than keeping the phone planted in front of your face, hold or prop the phone up so it’s pointing at your subject, then ignore the phone. The idea is to let Google's Gemini artificial intelligence models capture the scene and take photos on your behalf, so you can actually pay attention to what's happening in front of you.
The result? You'll get access to the full video (it's restricted to 1080p, but anyone with a Pixel 11 Pro can use Google's Video Boost technology to bump that to 4K). More important is the handful of photos you'll get—in full quality—as if you tapped on the shutter button yourself during the best moments. Reynolds says Gemini does a remarkable job of identifying “peak” occurrences in the scene, analyzing more than 500 frames to find perfect shots you'll want in your photo library.
I gave it a whirl during a demo with some live dancers. Indeed, all I had to do was hold the phone to the side—not in my face—and after the dance was over, I looked at the camera roll and found some surprisingly well-composed shots. It even cropped images with light edits based on what Gemini thought was a better composition. It's very much reminiscent of Google's Clips, a 2018 camera that ultimately flopped but similarly used AI to capture family moments. Magic Capture feels more intentional, and perhaps more useful.
“I do think the dream is: ‘I don’t have to deal with it; AI can look at a hundred times as many frames as I can, let the models handle this,'” Reynolds says. “That is sort of the dream of so many people who refuse to take their phones out at an event because they don't want their kid to remember their face hidden behind a camera.”
Instant Night Sight
Everyone knows that if you want to shoot a photo in low light, you have to stay as still as possible. Our smartphone cameras take a few seconds to capture multiple images and stitch them together, meaning small movements can end in a blurry mess. But Google says its new Tensor G6 processor on the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL can alleviate this problem by enabling a feature called Instant Night Sight.
Instant Night Sight is 4.5 times faster than the standard Night Sight available on other Pixel phones. Yes, that means there will still be a small shutter delay as the camera captures the photo, but the delay isn’t as pronounced as before. Much of this is thanks to new image-processing models tailored for the G6 chipset, which are bolstered by engine updates to Night Sight.
There are also hardware upgrades to a few cameras on the Pixel 11 series that provide greater light sensitivity, delivering brighter images in low light. Specifically, the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold have an upgraded 48-megapixel primary camera that absorbs 56 percent more light, and the new 48-megapixel telephoto camera on the Pixel 11 Pro has 30 percent more light sensitivity. It's a shame Instant Night Sight is only available to the two Pro candybar Pixels.
Camera Looks
Like Apple is doing with its Photographic Styles, Google is ceding more control to you, the photographer, in how your photos look. The Pixel Camera now features “Camera Looks,” and there are four main pillars: Original, Natural, Shadows, and Vanilla. Natural offers “relaxed details,” whereas Vanilla has a warm, golden glow; Shadow nets you deeper contrast. These aren't just filters like the ones you slap on Instagram—they're calibrated at the sensor level, and you can see what they look like in the camera viewfinder before you tap the shutter button.
From there, you can swipe left to cycle through a handful of additional looks, like Digi, Black Tie, Minimal, Editorial, Classic, and Velvet. And within each of these, you can further customize the settings for things like brightness, contrast, and highlights to tailor the look to your taste.
“People are moving away from what Pixel pioneered 10 years ago, which was that hashtag #nofilter concept,” Reynolds says. “And now, there's a much stronger desire to personalize and be unique, and put yourself into it.”
These Camera Looks must be chosen before you take the photo—not after. Reynolds says his team found that people engage with this feature very differently when it's available before capturing the photo—they think about it another way and enjoy it more—than if it were a filter to slap on in post.
Creator Suite
Arizona State University recently added content creation as an academic major—that's how many people really want to become influencers. So it makes sense then that Google would add some helpful tools to cater to those folks right in the camera app.
The new Creator Suite lives in the Pixel Camera's video settings. Once enabled, you can save videos to specific project folders instead of your main camera library, turn on an audio visualizer so you can make sure the microphone is actually picking up sound, enable Google's Speech Enhancement feature to beef up the video subjects’ voices, and add a social media grid so it's easy to visualize how your video will be framed on different platforms.
But arguably my favorite, as someone who has to make videos for my job, is the built-in teleprompter. You can pop any text into the feed, and it will track your speech as you talk, so the text will match your pace, meaning you never have to worry about the teleprompter’s scroll moving too fast or too slow. title: Google Pixel 11 Series, Pixel Watch 5, Pixel Tag: Specs, Features, Price, Release Date
summary: The Pixel 11 smartphone lineup is here, alongside the Pixel Watch 5 and the all-new Pixel Tag.
full_text:
Google is dialing things up to 11 this year with its Pixel phones. Ahead of its annual Made by Google event in New York City, the company unwrapped the Pixel 11 smartphone family—which includes the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold—alongside the Pixel Watch 5 smartwatch. There's also a new hardware addition: the Pixel Tag, which seems designed to be the AirTag of the Android world.
Here's everything you need to know about the hardware changes and software upgrades on Google’s latest devices. Preorders open today, and the phones and watches go on sale August 20.
The Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold
It was inevitable, but prices are up across the board for Google's Pixel 11 series. The Pixel 11 now starts at $899, and on the highest end of the spectrum, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is now $1,900. This means both devices got $100 price bumps. There's some good news: Google has bumped the base storage up to 256 GB on every device, a move matching Samsung's and Apple's latest handsets.
The Pixel 11 series is powered by Google's Tensor G6 chipset, which the company says is 20 percent more power efficient, 25 percent faster for browsing, and 15 percent faster when loading apps. Many of the camera improvements in the new devices are thanks to an improved imaging signal processor on the chip and a 50 percent more powerful tensor processing unit.
One big design change across the entire Pixel 11 series is on the oval camera bar on the back—it's now an all-glass surface, as opposed to a mix of metal and glass on its predecessors. Google says the camera bar on the Pixel 11 is more than 40 percent thinner, and when you pop on Google's case, the camera bar disappears and is completely flush. The Pixel 11 has the most striking color of the lot—Hibiscus—joined by more muted Pistachio, Frost, and Obsidian.
The Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold share more in common than you'd expect. They now have the same primary 48-megapixel camera, upgraded this year with a larger sensor that can capture up to 56 percent more light for brighter low-light images. The 10.8-megapixel telephoto camera, which has a 5X optical zoom, can now digitally zoom up to 30X. At these higher digital zoom levels, Google's machine learning algorithm puts in the work to clean up the digital noise and deliver an enhanced photo.
Google's folding phone is now 10 percent lighter and 1 mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, with slimmer bezels around the screen, though the phone is still heftier and thicker than Samsung's new Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra. It maintains its IP68 dust- and water-resistance rating, but there's a new glass-fiber composite back cover that Google says is “nearly impossible to crack” and an upgraded hinge that better protects the inner display from accidental drops. All of this, Google claims, makes the device three times more durable than its predecessor. Bold words.
The Fold features HiLight, a glowing LED on the back (excluded on the Pixel 11 but available on the Pixel 11 Pro phones). It lights up when you talk to Gemini, much like the glowing lights on the new Google Home Speaker. You can set it to light up in specific colors when you receive phone calls from your favorite contacts. Google says it's exploring the same capability for text messages, but didn't comment on whether it will enable HiLight for other notifications.
Both phones have been upgraded to 25-watt wireless charging speeds for faster Qi2 charging.
The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL
Even if the Pixel 11 Pro Fold has “Pro” in its name, a few extra upgrades in the candybar Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL elevate them to be the best hardware and software from Google. Both share the same specs outside of screen size, battery size, and charging speeds. They also are seeing $100 price bumps to $1,100 and $1,300, respectively.
The new colors this year are Canyon, Olive, and Fog, but the standard Obsidian (aka black) now has an all-matte finish. The same HiLight glowing LED as on the Fold is on the all-glass camera bar (Google is also bringing back the “Glowbar” on its upcoming Googlebook laptops later this year, so these glowing lights are a big theme for 2026). There's a new anti-scratch display coating that purportedly delivers more than double the scratch resistance of the Pixel 10 Pro.
Google says the main camera for the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL has been upgraded to a new 50-megapixel sensor, and there's a new 48-megapixel telephoto camera that Google claims has 30 percent better light sensitivity. The Pro line now uses this camera for its Pro Zoom feature, which uses generative AI to fill in the gaps of ultra-zoomed-in photos, allowing you to zoom up to 120X compared to 100X on last year's devices.
Thanks to the Tensor G6 chip, there's a big upgrade to Night Sight, Google's low-light photo mode. Exclusive to these two devices, it's now 4.5 times faster and dubbed “Instant Night Sight.” That means your subject won't have to stay super still in dim conditions while the phone captures the shot—it's a little more forgiving. That upgraded image signal processor on the chip also unlocks 4K portrait video for the first time. (It was capped at 1080p before.)
These two Pro Pixels are still the only ones in the lineup to support Google's Video Boost technology. If enabled, your video clips are uploaded and processed on Google's servers to improve brightness and colors, reduce noise, and upgrade stabilization. This year, they'll now be treated to “Pro Stable Video” as well. It will automatically activate for shaky scenes and deliver super-stable footage. Samsung and Apple have been delivering on that front largely through hardware, but it's no surprise that Google's leveraging its software expertise instead.
Pixel Software Smarts
There are a handful of fresh camera features available on all of these phones, from Magic Capture—which lets you hold the phone up while Gemini snap pics and video on your behalf so you can be in the moment—to Camera Looks and even a built-in teleprompter. You can read more about them in this story, where we also interview Google's Pixel camera chief.
These Pixel phones will receive the Gemini Intelligence features that debuted in Android 17, like Rambler, the AI speech-to-text feature. But Google is also highlighting Gemini's “proactive assistance,” which comes in the form of glowing cards that primarily pop up in the messaging app. If someone texts you about dinner plans and suggests a restaurant, Gemini will offer a button that displays a card of the Google Maps listing, giving you a quick look at the star rating and some pictures, and the option to switch to the Google Maps app if you want. It'll do similar tricks for scheduling with Google Calendar, too.
Those kinds of proactive assistance features play nicely into Google's task automation features that it introduced earlier this year. So if a friend asks about booking a table at a restaurant, you'll see a button you can press to hand the job off to Gemini to make the booking on your behalf. (You'll need to confirm it at the end, but Gemini does all but the last step.) One new experience launching in beta will even proactively put a restaurant's name on your lock screen when you're seated—tap it, and you'll be able to glance at Gemini-generated insights from reviews, photos, and top-recommended dishes.
Another feature available on all devices but uniquely more helpful on the Pixel 11 Pro Fold thanks to its folding design: the ability to translate American Sign Language. Using the camera, it can view a person using sign language and translate it into text for faster interactions.
In a similar vein, Google says the Tensor G6 chip allows it to translate any media you watch and listen to on YouTube and select other video and podcast apps, using generative AI to automatically dub audio in real time (much like Meta's AI audio dub feature in Instagram), bringing us one step closer to the universal translator from Star Trek.

title: Double killer and rapist given whole life sentence
summary: Simon Levy, from Tottenham, will spend the rest of his life in prison for the murder of two women and rape of a third.
full_text:
Double killer and rapist given whole life sentence
- Published
A serial sex attacker who had a "morbid fascination" with sex has been jailed for the rest of his life after he was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third.
Simon Levy, 40, killed Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, in March 2025 and 39-year-old Sheryl Wilkins five months later. Earlier that year, he raped a third woman in the same Tottenham car park where Wilkins was later found dead.
At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, Judge Mark Lucraft KC sentenced Levy to a whole life order, meaning he will never be released.
The sentence comes after police and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) apologised over a series of disastrous decisions that left him free to roam the streets.
When Levy carried out the attacks, he was on bail and being monitored by the Met.
The police watchdog is currently examining how he was managed over a four-year period, from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.
Following Wednesday's sentencing, Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the handling of Levy's case was a "whole system failing".
During his trial, the court heard Levy suffocated both women in sexually motivated attacks, with Valencia-Trujillo found in a largely abandoned block of flats on the Aylesbury estate in south-east London, and Wilkins behind a car park wall near Tottenham High Road, north London.
The woman he raped had told the police where he lived but she was not formally interviewed until after Levy had killed.
Sentencing Levy, Lucraft said, external: "You are clearly someone who ruthlessly exploits others for your own personal sexual satisfaction".
Noting his disturbing internet history and collection of press cuttings about sexual crimes, Lucraft said Levy was "someone who appears to have a morbid fascination with sex, rape, and crime".
The judge added the offences reflected "a series of attacks by you upon vulnerable women".
Lucraft added he was "acutely aware that whole life terms are sentences that should be considered for rare cases".
But in this case "the starting point has to be a whole life order", he said, as the aggravating features outweighed any mitigating features and "this cannot be described in any way as a borderline case".
"You will be in prison for life and there will be a whole life order," the judge added.
The court heard victim impact statements from families of the murdered women and the woman he raped.
'Know this, you lose'
Lindsey Hicks, Wilkins' sister, addressed Levy directly, saying: "I hope you rot in prison for the rest of your life."
She added: "You, Simon Levy, have destroyed our lives and we will never get over this. Sheryl was a beautiful soul who you cruelly took away in an evil act of crime.
"We should have been growing old together like sisters do and be there to support each other.
"Instead, I'm having to realise that one day in the near future I will be older than my big sister."
She said the past year had been the "worst of our lives" and concluded her witness statement by telling him: "Know this, you lose."
Wilkins' mother, Mary Wilkins, said she takes a "small measure of comfort" that Levy is now locked up and will never be free again.
She added her daughter "ended your chances of hurting anyone else".
During his trial, jurors heard Levy had a string of convictions for attacking women dating back to July 2018, including one carried out against a prison officer in 2022.
Earlier this year, Levy was also convicted of sexually assaulting 11 other women, 10 of them on trains and the Tube in London between 2023 and 2025.
Levy had declined to give evidence during his trial but pleaded not guilty to the two murders, as well as two counts of rape, grievous bodily harm with intent, and non-fatal suffocation against the surviving woman.
After sentencing, Sir Mark said the Met had apologised for its part.
"The concerning aspect for me is the fact he had been caught, he had been charged with offences," he said.
"He was repeatedly put by police before the courts seeking he be remanded in custody, saying this man is too dangerous to be on the streets, and between the CPS and the courts, they kept bailing him."
The commissioner said it was "not acceptable" for the "struggling criminal justice system" to put dangerous offenders on the street for the police to monitor.
He added: "We are seeing far too many cases day in and day out - knife carrier sex offenders who have been bailed when a few years ago they had been remanded in custody."
Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan said Valencia-Trujillo, Wilkins and Levy's other victims "deserved a system that believed and protected them".
'Institutional failure'
He added: "Time and time again, opportunities to stop him were missed.
"I am appalled by his crimes and the failures across multiple agencies that could have prevented him from harming, and ultimately killing, more women."
He said the "multi-agency failings need a multi-agency review" and that lessons should be learned and acted on.
"No woman or girl should be, or feel, unsafe in London," the mayor added.
In a letter to the director of public prosecution, Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary, wrote: "Levy was free to do this partly because your organisation failed to make the case for this sexual predator to be put back behind bars, in spite of warnings from others."
Former safeguarding minister Jess Phillips told the BBC there had been a "litany of failures".
"Of course it was Levy who undertook that action, but the state could definitely have prevented it so it has to bear that responsibility," she told Radio 4.
The Labour MP added that "an idiot could have seen that [Levy was a risk]".

title: Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death
summary: Lionel Messi says he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football in an emotional tribute after his father's death.
full_text:
Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death
- Published
Lionel Messi said he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football as he posted an emotional tribute after his father's death.
Messi's father Jorge was 68 when he died last week following a long illness.
Jorge had been the Argentina forward's agent since he was 14 and watched him become one of the sport's greatest ever players.
"I don't know what I'm going to do without you," Messi wrote on social media.
"I don't know how to carry on. I used to just play football, and now I'm really not sure if I'll carry on doing it for much longer.
"You were by my side from the very beginning. We were so close to the end. Why didn't you hang in there just a little longer so we could finish this together?"
Messi captained Argentina as they won the World Cup in 2022 and led them to the 2026 World Cup final, which his side lost 1-0 to Spain, before returning to club side Inter Miami.
He returned home with his family after Jorge passed away in a hospital in his hometown of Rosario, Argentina.
A private funeral took place on Sunday at a cemetery in the town of Perez, on the outskirts of Rosario.
"Dad, I still can't believe you're gone," Messi continued. "It hasn't sunk in, or rather, I don't want it to.
"It's so hard for me to imagine that I'll never see you again, that we'll never talk again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much left to enjoy together."
During the World Cup, Messi was brought to tears after scoring the opening goal in Argentina's 3-0 win against Algeria because of a matter he said was "completely unrelated to football". A statement from his family later said Jorge was dealing with a "health-related situation".
Messi added: "You kept asking me to play in one last World Cup, and just days before it started, that's when you took a turn for the worse.
"It was the first time you weren't going to be at a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and that you'd be well enough to travel. I kept telling you that we were going to make it to the final so you could come along.
"Every time a game ended, I'd wait for and miss your message. That's when I realised how bad the situation was.
"Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time to watch a game. We made it to the final, and you couldn't be there.
"I wanted to win it so I could bring the trophy to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs had nothing left. This time I tried to push past my physical limits, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel right."
More to follow.

title: Burnham warned Iran war could hit UK growth next year
summary: The conflict in the Middle East has pushed up oil and fuel prices, and also disrupted supply chains.
full_text:
Burnham warned Iran war could hit UK growth next year
- Published
Andy Burnham has been warned that the UK economy could barely grow next year if disruption in the Strait of Hormuz continues until the end of 2026.
Treasury sources have confirmed that internal modelling presented to the new prime minister and chancellor suggests UK GDP growth could be as low as 0.3% in 2027, as first reported by Bloomberg.
Government officials say they routinely plan for all possible scenarios.
The UK economy saw a strong start to the year, but growth then faltered with the conflict in the Middle East affecting some businesses. The Iran war has pushed up oil and fuel prices, and also disrupted supply chains.
On Thursday, official figures will show how much the economy grew between April and June of this year.
Economists are expecting growth of 0.4% for the three months.
Burnham and Chancellor John Healey were presented with a reasonable worst-case scenario of the Strait of Hormuz remaining effectively closed for the next five months, and no permanent US-Iran peace deal until the new year.
The Treasury modelling for that scenario was that the UK economy would grow by 0.9% over 2026 - slightly under the 1.1% forecast by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March.
The prospect was much dimmer for next year, with just 0.3% growth projected - much lower than the OBR's 1.6% forecast for 2027.
Under the modelling, inflation would peak at 4.3% in the first three months of next year. It currently stands at 2.6%, just above the Bank of England's 2% target.
The prime minister and chancellor will face pressure to use the upcoming Budget on 28 October to ease the financial burden on households and businesses.
Since taking office three weeks ago, Burnham has announced policies including the removal of VAT from domestic electricity bills and bringing forward an already planned end to "subscription traps".
But this week he told the BBC's Wake up to Money the announcements, aimed at tackling the cost of living, are not enough on their own, hinting at further support.
He has asked Healey to look at what more the government can do on the cost of living in the Budget, with the chancellor saying it will be his "main focus".
But Healey has said he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" – which will limit how much the government has to spend.
Burnham has said his government will stick to the party's 2024 manifesto pledges not to increase people's income tax, VAT or National Insurance contributions.
He also promised to follow the fiscal rules imposed by former Chancellor Rachel Reeves, which include a pledge to balance day-to-day spending with tax revenues by the end of the decade.

title: Members of cabinet remained on decoy plane, after Trump's quiet exit
summary: The president boarded a different plane in Turkey during a Nato summit to evade an Iranian threat.
full_text:
Members of Trump's cabinet remained on decoy plane, after Trump's quiet exit
- Published
Two members of US President Donald Trump's cabinet were on a decoy plane that Trump secretly exited before boarding a different flight in Turkey last month, CBS News reports.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent remained aboard what was believed to be Air Force One and did not join the flight provided to Trump over security concerns involving Iran.
After Trump entered Air Force One on 8 July with both officials and members of the press, he hid on a catering truck to be clandestinely transported to a military plane.
The label "Air Force One" applies to any plane the president is on, but in this case the original craft kept the call signal, turning it into a decoy.
According to CBS - the BBC's US partner - Rubio and Bessent remained on board the first aircraft to maintain the line of succession in the event something happened to Trump
In the event that the president dies or is incapacitated, Vice-President JD Vance would take power, followed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate.
The Secretary of State comes next in line, followed by the treasury secretary.
Others who stayed on the initial aircraft designated as Air Force One included White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Steven Cheung, the White House's communications director.
The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

title: Lucy Davis urges women to check their breasts for cancer - here's how
summary: The actress from The Office TV series says her breast lump was tiny and not a 'lump' as such; rather a kind of hard spot.
full_text:
Lucy Davis urges women to check their breasts for cancer - here's how
- Published
Signs of breast cancer are not always a lump in the traditional sense, so what should you look for?
Actress Lucy Davis, who played Dawn Tinsley in the original UK version of the popular TV series The Office, has revealed she has incurable breast cancer.
On Instagram, external, the 53-year-old said it had spread to her bones and it was too late for chemo.
She added: "The initial lump that I felt, wasn't a 'lump' as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny."
Here's how to check yourself at home.
What to look for
The NHS says to check your breasts, external or chest about once a month.
That helps you learn what looks and feels normal for you, making it easier to notice any abnormal changes.
Breasts can naturally look and feel a bit different at different phases of your menstrual cycle, and change a bit as you age.
Instead, pay attention to:
- a lump or swelling in your breast, chest or armpit
- a change in the skin of your breast, such as dimpling (it may look like orange peel) or redness, which may be harder to see on black or brown skin
- a change in size or shape of one or both breasts, or either side of your chest – it's common for breasts to be different sizes, but check for any changes that are not normal for you
- nipple discharge (if you're not pregnant or breastfeeding), which may have blood in it
- a change in the shape or look of your nipple, such as it turning inwards (inverted nipple) or a rash appearing on it (it may look like eczema)
- sores or ulcers on your chest
How to check your breasts
Look at your breasts or chest in a mirror to look for any changes. Start with your arms by your sides and then raise them up.
Feel around each breast or side of your chest in a circular motion all the way up to your collarbone and under each armpit. Use a mix of light and firmer pressure. Do not press so hard it hurts.
Feel around and over each nipple.
When should I see a doctor?
See your GP if:
- you have a lump or swelling in your breast, chest or armpit
- you have any changes in your breasts, chest or nipples that are not normal for you
- you have pain in your breast or armpit that does not go away

title: Estonia rejects proposals to take prisoners from UK jails
summary: Estonia's justice minister rules out a deal with the UK after Reform and the Conservatives suggested renting prison space abroad.
full_text:
Estonia rejects proposals to take prisoners from UK jails
- Published
The Estonian government has rejected the idea of taking prisoners from the UK to help ease the overcrowding crisis in British jails.
Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta told the BBC Estonia would not rent jail cells to other countries while it was housing criminals from Sweden in its half-empty Tartu prison under a deal signed last week.
The Conservatives and Reform UK have both suggested renting cells in foreign prisons, including in Estonia, to free up space and prevent the early releases of some offenders in England and Wales.
The Labour government also explored the idea in 2024 but talks with Estonia came to nothing.
Pakosta said Estonia had received no proposals to rent its prison space from the UK, adding that if one was to be made "our answer would be unequivocal - in Margaret Thatcher's famous words: No. No. No."
She added: "Such a proposal would not merely be mistaken, misguided or unacceptable; it would deserve to be rejected outright."
Thatcher memorably repeated "no" three times in 1990 speech, as she fiercely rejected calls for deeper political and economic integration of the European Community, which later evolved into the European Union.
In 2024, the Labour government, when Sir Keir Starmer was prime minister, held talks with Estonia to discuss the Baltic state's policy to house some prisoners from abroad.
Pakosta previously told the BBC she had met then-UK Justice Secretary Shabana Mahmood in Lithuania.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government is planning to release thousands of prisoners early this October, as it scrambles to free up space in jails almost at 100% capacity.
On Monday, Downing Street did not rule out renting space in foreign prisons, when asked by reporters if the government was considering doing so.
A No 10 spokesperson said the government was focused on "creating that extra capacity within the system domestically".
"In terms of renting prison places abroad, it's just not a quick fix," the spokesperson added.
"It will require primary legislation underpinned by a complex international agreement which would take several years to agree."
A government source told the BBC that renting foreign prison space would not help with the short-term crisis in jails.
Burnham has ordered the justice secretary to come up with a plan to create more space in jails by September.
He said the plan would be based on removing more foreign national offenders from prisons, releasing some offenders on indefinite sentences, and using space in women's jails for male inmates.
Options explored
Other parties have come up with their own ideas for dealing with overcrowding in prisons.
At a news conference on Monday, Reform UK suggested 10,000 prison spaces could be freed up if all foreign criminals were sent abroad to serve their sentences.
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said his party was exploring options to transfer foreign criminals in the UK to prisons in other countries, including El Salvador and Kosovo.
When asked if he had other countries in mind, Farage said: "Yes there are Baltic state options as well.
"I mean, conversations could certainly be had with Lithuania, for example, or perhaps Estonia as well."
A Reform UK spokesman said its policy was focused on El Salvador, Kosovo and "possibly others if they are open to the idea".
In recent days, the Conservatives have also urged Burnham to revive their plan to rent prison cells overseas, a policy they introduced when the party was in government in 2023.
The proposal aimed to mirror models used by Norway and Belgium in the Netherlands, where both countries rented cells to deal with overcrowding in their prisons.
Conservative shadow home secretary Chris Philp said this was "an idea that we legislated for in government but Labour subsequently did not pursue that".
"That was a catastrophic mistake by the Labour government that should be urgently reversed."
The Conservatives did not respond to requests to comment on Estonia's rejection of a prison rental deal with the UK.
In a statement, Lithuania's Ministry of Justice said: "There have been no discussions or consultations regarding the possibility of accepting the transfer of all Lithuanian citizens imprisoned in the United Kingdom".
A spokesperson said the Lithuanian government did not "see any scope for entering into practical arrangements of this kind".
The Kosovo government, which has agreed to lease 300 of its jail cells to Denmark as part of a deal worth £170m (€200m), appeared more open to working with other countries on prisoner transfers.
A Kosovo government spokesperson said: "We value the willingness of partner countries to initiate and advance new co-operation initiatives that serve common interests, mutual priorities, and the strengthening of international justice mechanisms".
But the spokesperson stressed Kosovo would focus on enacting its deal with Denmark "before entering into any new agreement of a similar nature".
The BBC has previously been told both former Conservative and Labour ministers independently came to the view that renting prison space abroad would be expensive.
Sweden has agreed to pay up to £52m (€61m) a year to Estonia if the Baltic nation does house 600 of its offenders at the Tartu prison.
Estonia said from the 301st inmate onwards, Sweden would pay an additional £7,254 (€8,500) per prisoner, per month.
The average annual cost per prisoner in a public-sector prison in England and Wales was £60,018 in 2024/25, according to Ministry of Justice data.

title: Lebanon passes long-sought amnesty law, a day after death penalty repeal
summary: The legislation will 'exceptionally' reduce certain prison terms, says Lebanon's parliament speaker.
full_text:
Lebanon passes long-sought amnesty law, a day after death penalty repeal
The legislation will ‘exceptionally’ reduce certain prison terms, says Lebanon’s parliament speaker.
Lebanon’s parliament has approved a general amnesty law that is expected to benefit thousands of convicted prisoners, detainees and wanted people.
The legislation passed Wednesday in a “show-of-hands vote”, reported Lebanon’s official National News Agency. It is the first law of its kind since 1991.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3Lebanon ‘files new lawsuit against’ ex-central bank chief Riad Salameh
- list 2 of 3Bashar al-Assad, Atef Najib sentenced to death in landmark Syria trial
- list 3 of 3Lebanese soldiers injured while Israeli troops intrude on southern town
The office of the country’s parliament speaker said the law would “exceptionally” reduce certain prison terms.
Long demanded by numerous Lebanese political factions, the amnesty law aims to reduce overcrowding in prisons, where many inmates await trial for years.
However, it has faced backlash from some family members of Lebanese soldiers and servicemen killed in attacks, who fear the perpetrators could receive undue leniency.
Lebanese authorities did not immediately announce the number of people who would be freed or receive reduced sentences under the law, which comes a day after Lebanon’s parliament also formally abolished the death penalty.
According to Imad al-Hout, one of the lawmakers in favour of the bill, the law reduced the sentences of those facing death and life imprisonment to 17 “prison years”.
That is equivalent to 12 years and nine months of actual imprisonment in Lebanon, where a prison year is calculated as nine months.
The law also calls for the release of inmates in ongoing trials who have been detained for more than 12 prison years without charges.
In its 2025 report, the country’s National Human Rights Commission said that prisons had an overcrowding rate of 300 percent, with prison authorities reporting at least 6,268 inmates by the end of March.
‘Long-awaited’
A push for general amnesty grew after the 2024 fall of longtime Syrian president Bashar al-Assad, as Lebanon jailed many prisoners over events linked to the Syrian civil war.
Most of those prisoners hail from northern Lebanon’s Sunni-majority city Tripoli and are accused of crimes that include attacking the Lebanese army, participating in clashes and planning bombings.
Other political forces, including the Iran-backed Shia movement Hezbollah, have been demanding amnesty for their communities.
Thousands of families from the eastern Baalbek and Hermel regions, bastions of Hezbollah and its ally Amal, where illicit cannabis cultivation is widespread, have been demanding amnesty for drug-related offences and car theft for years.
Christian parties, meanwhile, pushed for an amnesty law to include the families of those who joined an Israeli-backed group and fled to Israel after its withdrawal from southern Lebanon in 2000, fearing reprisals, particularly from Hezbollah and its supporters.
Deputy Walid Baarini praised the “long-awaited passage” of the amnesty law and expressed hope it would mark “a new chapter” that brings justice “to those who deserve it”.
“Amnesty is not forgetting a right, but rather prioritising mercy and wisdom when they align with the requirements of justice and the national interest,” he wrote in a post on X.
Lebanon previously passed a general amnesty law in the wake of its 1975-90 civil war.

title: Why the UK faces a prisons crisis amid row over release of cop killers
summary: The killers of PC Andrew Harper had been set to partake in early release scheme as prison system on verge of collapse.
full_text:
Why the UK faces a prisons crisis amid row over release of cop killers
The killers of Police Constable Andrew Harper had been set to partake in early release scheme as prison system stands on the verge of collapse.
The UK’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham has become embroiled in a row about an early prison release scheme to alleviate overcrowding in England and Wales, which ignited furious public outcry when it emerged that two of the killers of Police Constable (PC) Andrew Harper could benefit from the plan.
Under the Sentencing Act 2026, which was passed under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer, prisoners in England and Wales who are serving fixed, determinate sentences will be released as early as one-third of the way through their jail time in order to free up space. The scheme is set to begin in October this year.

list of 3 items
